messages.content: Please write a thank-you note, about 50 words, to my friend Ritu. She lent me her camera for my school project and it helped me a lot. I'm Anil.

Dear Ritu,
Thank you so much for lending me your camera for my school project. It helped me a lot, and I could not have managed so well without it. I took good care of it. You are a true friend, and I am very grateful for your kindness and trust.
Love,
Anil
I broke my brother's toy car by mistake. Write a short sorry note I can leave on his bed, about 45 words. His name is Rohan and I'm Kabir.

Dear Rohan,
I am really sorry that I broke your toy car. It was a mistake, and I did not mean to hurt it. I know how much you like it. Please forgive me and let me make it up to you.
Your brother,
Kabir
Write a congratulations message, around 40 words, for my neighbour Mrs. Gomes, whose son Joel won a gold medal in swimming. I'm Rahul Menon.

Dear Mrs. Gomes,
Warm congratulations to you and your family! I heard that Joel won the gold medal in swimming. He must have worked very hard for it. You must be very proud. Please give him my best wishes.
Regards,
Rahul Menon
A classmate of mine, Tanvi, is at home with a bad cold. Write a get-well note from the whole class, about 50 words. We are Class 7B.

Dear Tanvi,
We miss you in class! The room is quieter without you. Please rest well and do not worry about the lessons, because we will share our notes with you. Get well soon and come back with a big smile.
From all your friends in Class 7B
Write a short reminder message for my team about submitting the monthly report by Thursday evening. Around 40 words. I'm Divya.

Hello team,
This is a friendly reminder to send in your monthly reports by Thursday evening. Please check your numbers once before you submit. If you need any help, message me so I can help.
Thanks,
Divya
Write an invitation, about 60 words, for my daughter Ishita's 7th birthday party. It is on Sunday at 4 pm at Green Park Club, and the theme is jungle animals. It is from Sunita and Prakash.

You are invited!
Ishita is turning seven, and we are having a jungle animals party. Come dressed as your favourite animal and join us for a fun afternoon.
Date: Sunday
Time: 4 pm
Place: Green Park Club
Please let us know if you can join us. We can't wait to see you!
Warm regards,
Sunita and Prakash

Write an invitation for parents to our school's science fair, about 55 words. It is on Friday, 10 am, in the main hall. Students from Classes 5 to 8 will show their work, and it is signed by Mrs. D'Souza, Science Coordinator.

Dear Parents,
Our students request the pleasure of your company at the Science Fair. Children from Classes 5 to 8 will show their working models and experiments. Your visit will encourage them greatly.
Date: Friday
Time: 10 am
Venue: Main Hall
We look forward to seeing you there.
Yours sincerely,
Mrs. D'Souza, Science Coordinator
Write a casual invite, asking friends to come over for a board game night at my place on Saturday evening. About 50 words. I'm Neha.

Hey everyone,
It's board game night at my place this Saturday evening. Come over for a fun night of games, laughs and good company. Bring your favourite game if you have one. Please let me know if you can make it. It will be so much fun!
See you soon,
Neha
Our family is hosting a small Navratri garba evening this Saturday at 7 pm in our building courtyard. Write an invitation to the neighbours, about 50 words. We are the Patel family.

Dear Neighbours,
We are hosting a small garba evening for Navratri this Saturday at 7 pm in our building courtyard. Please come with your family and join us in the dance. It will be a lovely evening of music and festive cheer. We would love to celebrate with you.
Warm wishes,
The Patel family
I'm Vikram, captain of our colony cricket team. Write a message inviting new players to trial matches this Sunday at 7 am on the ground behind the temple, around 50 words.

Hello cricket lovers!
Our colony team is looking for new players. Trial matches will be held this Sunday at 7 am on the ground behind the temple. Boys and girls of all ages are welcome, whether you bat, bowl or just love the game. Come and be part of the team.
Captain Vikram
Please write a polite request to my school principal asking for permission to use the library after school hours to prepare for exams. Around 60 words. I'm Meena of Class 10.

Respected Principal,
I am Meena of Class 10. Our board exams are close, and I would like to prepare well for them. I request you to kindly allow me and my classmates to use the school library after school hours for our studies. Thank you for considering my request.
Thank you,
Meena, Class 10
Write a polite complaint to our building's watchman about people parking in front of my gate. Around 55 words, no anger. I'm Mr. Kulkarni of Flat 12, and the cars block my scooter.

Dear Watchman,
I hope you are well. Some cars have been parked in front of my gate, and I cannot take my scooter out. Could you please ask visitors to use the parking area instead? I would be grateful for your help. Thank you for looking after our building.
Regards,
Mr. Kulkarni, Flat 12

A tailor stitched my daughter's school uniform too short and has not fixed it. Write a firm but polite complaint message, about 65 words. I collected it last Monday, he promised to alter it within two days, and I need it by Saturday because school reopens on Monday. I'm Mrs. Fernandes.

Dear Tailor,
I collected my daughter's school uniform from your shop last Monday, and it is much shorter than the size I gave. You promised to alter it within two days, but it is still not done. Please fix it by Saturday, as school reopens on Monday. I would be grateful for your help. Thank you.
Mrs. Fernandes
Draft a mail to my teacher, Mr. Iyer, saying I could not submit my history project on time because I was unwell, and asking for two more days. Around 75 words. I'm Zoya from Class 9.

Subject: Request for extension on history project

Dear Mr. Iyer,
I am Zoya from Class 9. I could not submit my history project on time because I was unwell. I have been working on it carefully, and I want to hand in my best work. May I please have two more days to submit it? I am sorry for the trouble.
Thank you for understanding.
Yours sincerely,
Zoya
I need to ask my manager, Ms. Rao, for a day off next Friday for my cousin's wedding. Write the email, about 85 words. I'm Imran, and my current work will be finished by Thursday.

Subject: Leave request for Friday

Dear Ms. Rao,
I hope you are doing well. I would like to request a day of leave next Friday, as I must attend my cousin's wedding. I will complete my current tasks by Thursday and send you the final files before I leave. Please let me know if there is anything else you need from me before then. Kindly confirm if this works for you.
Thank you,
Imran
Please email my neighbour Mr. Desai about the noise from his terrace parties late at night. Polite, about 65 words. I'm Kavya from the flat below.

Subject: A small request about late-night noise

Dear Mr. Desai,
I am Kavya from the flat below yours. I enjoy hearing the cheer on your terrace, but the music has continued late at night, and I cannot sleep well. Could you please lower the volume at night? I would be very grateful. Thank you for being such a kind neighbour.
Best wishes,
Kavya

Draft a notice for the school notice board about a change in the bus timing next week. Buses leave 30 minutes earlier on Monday and Tuesday, and normal timings resume on Wednesday. About 55 words. Sign it Transport Office.

NOTICE
Change in Bus Timing

All students who use the school bus are informed that the buses will leave thirty minutes earlier than usual on Monday and Tuesday next week. Please reach your bus stop on time. Parents, please note this. Normal timings will resume from Wednesday.

By order,
Transport Office
Write a notice for our apartment lift, around 65 words, saying that it will be under repair on Wednesday from 10 am to 1 pm. Sign it Secretary, Sunrise Apartments.

NOTICE TO ALL RESIDENTS

The lift will be closed for repair on Wednesday from 10 am to 1 pm. During this time, please use the stairs and take care while climbing. Kindly plan your trips in advance so that you are not caught unprepared. We are sorry for the inconvenience and thank you for your patience.

Secretary, Sunrise Apartments
Write a notice inviting local residents to a tree-planting morning in Rose Garden Park on Sunday, 7 am. About 70 words. Sign it Garden Welfare Group.

TREE-PLANTING MORNING

Join us this Sunday at 7 am in Rose Garden Park for a morning of planting trees together. Come with your family, friends and neighbours, and help us make our neighbourhood greener. Everyone is welcome, and every pair of hands will make a difference. Let us make our neighbourhood greener, one tree at a time.

Garden Welfare Group
Describe a tea stall by the roadside on a rainy evening in about 80 words.

The tea stall sits under a faded blue tarpaulin by the road. Rain drums on the sheet as customers crowd close, holding their bags over their heads. The owner pours milky tea from a dented kettle into small glasses. Steam rises and smells of ginger and cardamom. A stove glows orange, and plates of hot pakoras are passed around. Nobody is in a hurry now. Outside, the street shines wet and grey, but here, it is warm.
Describe the sound of a thunderstorm arriving over a village, around 70 words.

First, the wind rises and shakes the leaves. Dogs bark, and mothers call the children inside. Then a low rumble rolls across the fields, like a giant moving furniture in the sky. The thunder grows louder until the windows rattle. A flash of light lights up the lane, and big drops begin to fall on the tin roofs. Soon the whole village is filled with the loud, happy sound of rain.
Describe a Christmas midnight mass in a small church in Goa. About 90 words, please.

The little church stands white and shining under the stars. Inside, hundreds of candles glow, and the air smells of wax and fresh flowers. Families sit close together in their best clothes, the children yawning but excited. The choir begins to sing, and the old carols fill the hall softly. A small crib stands near the altar with a tiny baby in the straw. When the bells ring at midnight, everyone smiles and hugs. Outside, the village lights twinkle, and the night feels peaceful.
Write about 80 words describing a vegetable market early in the morning.

Before sunrise, the vegetable market is already awake. Carts roll in loaded with fresh spinach, bright tomatoes and long green beans. Sellers arrange their heaps carefully and sprinkle water to keep everything fresh. Voices call out prices, and scales clink. Buyers walk slowly, pinching tomatoes and smelling coriander. A porter hurries by with a basket on his head. The ground is wet and muddy, and the whole place smells of earth and green leaves.
Write a description of a very hot afternoon in a small town in exactly five sentences.

The sun hangs high and bright over the small town, and the tar on the road shines like a black mirror. Shops pull down their shutters, and even the stray dogs lie still in the shade. A lonely ice-cream cart rings its bell and is soon surrounded by sweating schoolchildren. Ceiling fans turn slowly in the houses, giving little relief. By evening, a gentle breeze comes, and the whole town sighs in thanks.
Diary entry wanted: about 75 words, from a boy who got selected for the school football team today.

Dear Diary,
I can hardly write because my hands are still shaking! The coach read out the team list after practice, and my name was there. I am in the school football team! I ran all the way home and told my family, who hugged me and cheered. Everyone said they will come to my first match. I must practise my passing every day now. Tonight, I will sleep with my football next to my bed.
A girl lost her pet rabbit, Snowy, today, and her Mummy comforted her. Write her diary entry, about 80 words.

Dear Diary,
Today was a sad day. When I woke up, Snowy did not come running to the door of his cage. Mummy sat with me and said he had grown old and had gone to sleep forever. I cried for a long time. Then we buried him in the garden, and I put a small flower on top. I will always remember how he nibbled my fingers. Goodnight, Snowy.
Can you write about 90 words in diary form for someone on the first night of a long train journey across India.

Dear Diary,
I am writing this on the upper berth, with the train rocking me gently. Outside, small stations flash by with yellow lights and sleepy tea-sellers. An aunty below me shared her thepla, and we talked for an hour. The little boy opposite taught me a card game. I never thought a train could feel so friendly. The wheels make a steady song, and my eyes are getting heavy. Tomorrow, we will wake up in a new state.
I'd like a diary entry, about 100 words, by a young woman after her first day as a teacher in a village school.

Dear Diary,
Today I stood in front of my first class. Thirty small faces looked at me, and my heart was beating so loudly. I forgot half of what I had planned, so I simply asked each child her name and her favourite food. We laughed a lot. A girl named Basanti gave me a wildflower and said, "Teacher, you smell like the market." I did not know whether to laugh or cry. I am tired, but I feel happy. I think I will love this place.
Write a tiny story for children, about 100 words, about a little cloud who is afraid to rain.

Once there was a little cloud called Pippa who was afraid to rain. "If I rain, I will disappear," she said. The other clouds floated away, and Pippa stayed alone above a dry brown field. Below, a farmer looked up and sighed, and the flowers hung their heads. Pippa felt sorry for them. She took a deep breath and let one small drop fall. Then another. Soon the field was green and the flowers danced. Pippa was still there, and she was fluffier and happier than ever.
Tell me a short story for young kids, about 100 words, about a squirrel who forgets where he hid his nuts.

Sonu the squirrel hid his nuts all over the park before winter. But when the cold days came, he could not remember where he had put them. He looked under the bench and behind the swing, and found nothing. His tummy rumbled. Then his friend Mina the sparrow said, "Look at the big banyan tree." Sonu dug at its roots and found a pile of nuts! There, a new little tree was also growing from one he had forgotten. Sonu smiled. "I planted a tree by mistake," he said happily.
I need a story for my class's reading hour, about 100 words, about a girl who is scared of speaking on stage but finally does it.

Anaya loved reading poems aloud at home, but on stage her voice always disappeared. When her teacher chose her for the annual day speech, her hands turned cold. At night she practised in front of her teddy bear. On the big day, she looked at the crowd and her mind went blank. Then she saw her little brother in the front row, waving at her. She smiled and began. Her voice shook at first, then grew strong. When she finished, everyone clapped loudly. Anaya had done it.
Write a short paragraph of about 80 words on why drinking water from a clean bottle is better than buying many plastic ones.

A reusable bottle is a small choice that makes a big difference. Plastic bottles are used once and then thrown away, and they often end up in drains and rivers. A steel or glass bottle can be filled again and again for years. It saves money, too, because you do not have to keep buying water. Just wash it every day and carry it with you. It is an easy way to keep our streets and our planet cleaner.
Write a paragraph for my class essay on 'Why Grandparents Are Special', about 80 words.

Grandparents are special because they have time for us. They tell stories of old days, teach us songs, and share recipes that have been in the family for years. When we are scolded, they quietly take our side. They remind us where we come from and how to be kind. A hug from a grandparent feels warm and safe. I am lucky to have mine, and I try to visit them as often as I can.
Write a short paragraph, around 70 words, on why playing outdoors is good for children.

Playing outdoors is good for children in many ways. They run, jump and climb, and that makes their bodies strong. They learn to share and to take turns when they play team games. Fresh air and sunshine make them feel cheerful. They also meet friends and discover how fun life is without a screen. After a long afternoon outside, children are tired, hungry and happy, and they sleep well at night.
Write a short rhyme for kids, four lines, about a rainy day.

Pitter-patter, drip and drop,
Rain is falling, will not stop.
Splash, splash, in my boots I go,
Puddles jumping, to and fro!
Write a simple poem, 4 lines, about a sleepy cat in the sun.

The cat lies down in a golden beam,
And blinks her eyes as if in a dream.
She stretches long and gives a yawn,
Then purrs herself to sleep till dawn.
Could you write a short poem for my mother for her birthday? Simple words, about 50 words.

Dear Mother, you wake before the sun,
You smile until the day is done.
You cook with love, you hold my hand,
You always seem to understand.
Today is yours, so rest and cheer,
You are the best, my mother dear.
Happy birthday! May every year
Bring joy and laughter, always near.
Make a funny rhyme for children, six lines, about a boy who loves mangoes.

Manu loved mangoes, big and sweet,
He ate them standing on his feet.
He ate them morning, noon and night,
His face was yellow, what a sight!
His mother laughed, "Dear Manu, stop!"
Then he ate one more and went plop!
Write a short note of encouragement, about 50 words, for my friend Pooja who failed her driving test the first time. I'm Leela.

Dear Pooja,
Please do not feel bad about the test. Many people need a second try, and each try teaches us something. You are a careful driver, and I am sure you will pass next time. Let's celebrate when you do!
Your friend,
Leela
Say thank you to my manager, Mr. Khan, for supporting me during a hard month. About 50 words. I'm Sheetal.

Dear Mr. Khan,
I want to thank you for your support this month. When things were hard, your help and encouragement made a big difference to me. I truly appreciate your patience and kindness. It made a hard month much easier, and I learnt a great deal from you.
With gratitude,
Sheetal
Write a thank-you note, about 45 words, to Mrs. Bhatt, a neighbour who brought us soup when my mother was unwell. Don't mention any medical details. I'm Sameer, writing for my family.

Dear Mrs. Bhatt,
Thank you so much for the soup you brought us. It was warm and tasty, and we all enjoyed it. Your kindness meant a lot to us. We are lucky to have such a caring neighbour.
Warm regards,
Sameer and family
Write a postcard message from Darjeeling to my grandmother, whom I call Ajji, about 55 words. I'm Pranav.

Dear Ajji,
Greetings from Darjeeling! The hills are green and misty, and the tea gardens look like soft carpets. The air is cool and fresh, and I wish you were here to see it. I am having a lovely time and I miss you. I will tell you everything when I come home.
Love,
Pranav
Write a polite message to my friend Arjun asking him to return the cricket bat I lent him last month. Our school match is on Saturday. About 50 words. I'm Ravi.

Hi Arjun,
I hope you are well. I wanted to ask about my cricket bat, which I lent you last month. Our school match is on Saturday, and I would like to practise with it before that. Could you please bring it to school soon? Thanks a lot!
Ravi
Email my class teacher, Mrs. Thomas, and ask her which chapters will be in the maths test on Monday. I'm Aarav from Class 6. About 60 words.

Subject: Question about Monday's maths test

Dear Mrs. Thomas,
I am Aarav from Class 6. I could not note down the chapters for Monday's maths test because I was late leaving class. Could you please tell me which chapters will be included? I want to prepare well. Thank you for your time.
Yours sincerely,
Aarav
Write a 60-word paragraph on why it is nice to help in the kitchen on a Sunday.

Helping in the kitchen on a Sunday is a joy. Sundays are slow, so the whole family has time to cook together. You can wash the vegetables, stir the dal, or roll out the dough. You learn useful skills and get to taste everything first. Best of all, you spend time with your family, and the food somehow tastes better when you have made it yourself.
Describe fireworks on Diwali night in about 70 words, for little children.

When it gets dark on Diwali, the sky becomes a big painting. Whoosh! A rocket goes up and bursts into red stars. Boom! Then come green and golden flowers that fall slowly. The little sparklers fizz in our hands and make tiny circles of light. Every house has rows of tiny lamps. Everyone shouts, "Wow!" We clap our hands and hold our ears. Diwali is a night of light and joy.
Write a message to my roommates reminding them that the gas cylinder needs to be booked this weekend. About 50 words. I'm Shruti.

Hi all,
A quick reminder that our gas cylinder needs to be booked this weekend. Could one of us please book a new one? It would be great if we could decide who will do it today. Please reply here once it is done. Thanks, everyone!
Shruti
We ordered a family dinner from a local restaurant and the rice was cold and one dish was missing. Write a polite complaint, about 60 words, to the manager. I'm Mohan Reddy.

Dear Manager,
We ordered a family dinner from your restaurant. When it arrived, the rice was cold, and one of the dishes we asked for was missing. We were disappointed by this. Could you please look into it and let us know how it can be put right? Thank you for your time.
Sincerely,
Mohan Reddy
Please write a story for young children, about 100 words, about a firefly who is afraid of the dark.

Chintu the firefly lived in a big mango tree. All his friends glowed bright at night, but Chintu was afraid of the dark and hid in a leaf. "I can't go out," he said. One night, a baby bird fell from its nest and cried in the black garden. Nobody could see it. Chintu shook with fear, but he flew down and began to glow. His little light showed the way to the nest. The mother bird hugged him. From then on, Chintu was never afraid of the dark again.
Write a short notice, about 40 words, saying the school library will be closed on the day of the Holi holiday and will reopen the next day. Sign it Librarian.

NOTICE

The school library will remain closed on the day of the Holi holiday. It will reopen the next day. Students are advised to plan their reading and book returns around the holiday. Happy Holi to all!

Librarian
Thank my friend Maya's parents, whom I call Uncle and Aunty, for having me stay over at their house during the holidays. Around 50 words, from me, Tara.

Dear Uncle and Aunty,
Thank you so much for letting me stay at your home during the holidays. You made me feel like part of the family, and I enjoyed every day of my stay. Please tell Maya I will miss her. I hope I can return your kindness soon.
With love,
Tara
I spilled juice on my friend Harsh's library book. Help me write a short apology message, around 45 words. I'm Dev.

Hi Harsh,
I am really sorry about your library book. I spilled juice on it, and I feel terrible about it. It was an accident, and I did not mean to spoil it. Please tell me how I can make it up to you. Please forgive me.
Yours,
Dev
My cousin Neelam just had a baby girl. Please write a joyful message of congratulations, about 50 words. It is from her aunt and uncle, Rekha and Sanjay.

Dear Neelam,
Congratulations on your beautiful baby girl! We are so happy for you and your family. May she bring you lots of laughter and sweet, sleepy cuddles. We cannot wait to meet her and hold her tiny hands. Sending you our blessings.
All our love,
Aunt Rekha and Uncle Sanjay

Write a get-well message, around 45 words, for my grandfather, whom we call Dada, who is resting at home after a knee operation. Keep it cheerful and don't give any medical advice. It is from his grandchildren.

Dear Dada,
We are thinking of you every day and sending you lots of love. The house feels quiet without you. Rest well and take all the time you need. We cannot wait to see you up and about again. Come back to your old self soon!
Your grandchildren
Write a reminder note for my son Aman to carry his umbrella and lunch box to school tomorrow. Short, about 35 words, and friendly. Sign it Mummy.

Good morning, Aman!
Please remember to carry your umbrella and your lunch box to school tomorrow. Do not forget them at home! Have a lovely day at school!
Love,
Mummy
Write a congratulation message, about 50 words, to my colleague Farah on getting her first job promotion. I'm Gaurav.

Dear Farah,
Congratulations on your promotion! You have earned it with your hard work. I am very happy for you, and I am sure you will do wonderfully in your new role. This is only the beginning, and I wish you every success ahead.
Warm wishes,
Gaurav
Write a thank-you note from the whole class (Class 6C) to our teacher Mr. Das after a wonderful school trip to the museum. About 45 words.

Dear Mr. Das,
Thank you for taking us to the museum. We had a wonderful trip and learnt so much. You answered our questions patiently and made the visit great fun. We will remember it for a long time. Please take us again soon!
Your students,
Class 6C
My cricket ball broke my neighbour Mr. Pillai's flower pot. Write a sorry note, about 45 words, that I can leave at his door. I'm Karthik of Flat 4.

Dear Mr. Pillai,
I am very sorry that my cricket ball broke your flower pot. I should not have played so near your house. I will be more careful from now on. Please let me replace the pot. Please forgive me.
Sincerely,
Karthik, Flat 4
Write a note to remind my sister, whom I call Sis, to return the library books on Friday. About 50 words, and make it a bit funny. I'm her brother.

Dear Sis,
Alert! Alert! Your library books are begging to go home on Friday. They are tired of waiting for their return trip. Please save them, and save me from having to remind you again. I will never let you forget it.
Your loving brother
Please write a note, about 45 words, thanking my aunt, whom I call Masi, for the lovely sweater she knitted for me. I'm Pia.

Dear Masi,
Thank you for the beautiful sweater you knitted for me. It fits perfectly, and it is so soft and warm. I know you put a lot of love into it. I will treasure it always, and I will think of you whenever I wear it.
Love,
Pia
Write an invitation to our housewarming puja, about 65 words. We are the Joshi family, moving into a new flat (Flat 305, Lotus Heights) on Saturday at 10 am.

Dear Friends and Family,
We have moved into our new home, and we would be delighted to have you share this joy. We are holding a small housewarming puja on Saturday at 10 am. We would love to have you with us. Your blessings and presence will make the day special. Please come and bring your smiles.
With warm regards,
The Joshi family, Flat 305, Lotus Heights
Invite everyone to a farewell lunch, about 65 words, for our colleague Mr. Nair, who retires on Friday. Lunch is in the office canteen at 1 pm.

Dear Colleagues,
Mr. Nair retires this Friday after many years with us. Please join us in the office canteen at 1 pm for a farewell lunch in his honour. Come and share your favourite memories of him, and help us give him a warm send-off. We hope to see you all there.
Warm regards,
Your colleagues
Draft an invitation, about 60 words, to an old-students reunion at our school next month. Date: second Saturday. Time: 4 pm. Tea and snacks. Sign it Alumni Committee.

Dear Friends,
Remember the classrooms, the school bell and the friends you made? We are bringing everyone back together for an Old Students' Reunion on the second Saturday of next month at 4 pm. Come and meet your classmates and teachers, and relive the best days of your life. Tea and snacks will be served.
See you there!
Alumni Committee
Write a short message inviting my friends to fly kites with me on the terrace on Makar Sankranti morning. About 50 words. I'm Anita.

Hello friends,
Come and fly kites with me on my terrace this Makar Sankranti morning! Bring your kites and strong thread, and let us race them across the sky. It will be a fun day full of sunshine and cheering. Please come early and bring a big smile!
Anita
Help me invite our neighbours to a Lohri bonfire in the society garden on Thursday at 7 pm. Around 55 words, with a warm tone. Sign it The Garden Committee.

Dear Neighbours,
Join us for a Lohri bonfire in the society garden this Thursday at 7 pm. Let us gather around the warm fire and celebrate the festival together. Please come dressed warmly. We hope the warmth of the fire and of friendship will brighten the cold evening. Everyone is welcome!
The Garden Committee
Write a polite complaint to a bus company because my long-distance night bus to Jaipur last Friday came three hours late and no one told us anything. Around 60 words. I'm Naveen Gupta.

Dear Sir or Madam,
I travelled on your night bus to Jaipur last Friday. It arrived three hours late, and we received no information at the stop. Many passengers were left waiting without any news. I request you to look into the reasons and to inform passengers in future. Thank you for your attention.
Yours faithfully,
Naveen Gupta
Write a letter to my landlord asking him to repair the leaking tap in our kitchen. Polite, about 55 words. I'm Rohini, tenant of Flat 2B.

Dear Landlord,
I hope you are well. The kitchen tap in Flat 2B is leaking, and water is wasted all day. Could you please send a plumber at your earliest convenience? Please let me know when the person can come. Thank you very much for your help.
Regards,
Rohini
I ordered a glass vase and it came broken in the parcel. Write a polite complaint to the courier company, about 60 words, asking for a solution. I'm Lalitha Rao.

Dear Customer Care,
I received a parcel from your company, and the glass vase inside was broken. I was very disappointed, as I had been looking forward to using it. I request you to investigate the matter and tell me how I can get a replacement or a refund. I would be grateful for a quick reply.
Sincerely,
Lalitha Rao
Write a request to my class teacher asking if I can change my seat because I cannot see the board well from the back. Around 50 words. I'm Yash of Class 8.

Dear Teacher,
I am Yash of Class 8. I am sitting in the last row, and I cannot see the board clearly. Could you please let me move to a seat nearer the front? I think it will help me follow the lessons better. Thank you very much for your kindness.
Yours sincerely,
Yash
Compose an email for my son Arjun's teacher, Ms. Alvarez, asking for a meeting about his reading. Say that I am free after 5 pm on weekdays. About 70 words. My name is Peter Dsouza.

Subject: Request for a short meeting

Dear Ms. Alvarez,
I am Peter Dsouza, Arjun's father. I would like to talk to you about his reading and how I can support him at home. Could we meet for a few minutes soon? I am free after 5 pm on any weekday. Please suggest a time that suits you. Thank you for all your help.
Kind regards,
Peter Dsouza
Write an email to my manager asking permission to join an online communication-skills course on Saturdays. About 70 words. I'm Hari.

Subject: Request to join a communication-skills course

Dear Manager,
I would like to join an online communication-skills course that is held on Saturdays. I believe it will help me write better reports and speak with confidence in meetings. Thank you for your consideration.
Regards,
Hari
Write a polite email to the neighbour who shares our water tank, asking if we can take turns cleaning it every month. About 65 words. I'm Sudha, from the ground floor.

Dear Neighbour,
I hope you and your family are well. Since we share the water tank, I wondered if we could take turns to clean it every month. We could decide together who does it first. It would keep the water fresh for all of us. Please tell me what you think.
Warm regards,
Sudha

Dear Dr. Banerjee,
I hope this message finds you well. I am Anisha, who took your course on modern history last year. I am applying for a master's programme, and I would be honoured if you could write a recommendation letter for me. The last date is next month, and I am happy to send you any details you may need. I am very grateful for your guidance and time.
Sincerely,
Anisha Sen
Write an email, about 70 words, to our society secretary asking the society to set up a water bowl corner for birds in summer. I'm Mr. Shetty.

Thank you,
Mr. Shetty

Residents' Welfare Association

Management Committee

Students of Classes 9 and 10 who are taking part in the Annual Day programme must attend the rehearsal in the auditorium on Thursday after school. Please be on time and come ready to practise. Your presence is needed so that the programme goes well on the day.

Cultural Secretary
Describe a small railway station at dawn in about 80 words.

The railway station wakes up before the sun. A tea-seller lights his stove, and the first steam rises into the cold air. Pigeons shuffle on the tracks, and a porter yawns beside his trolley. The loudspeaker crackles with a sleepy voice announcing the first train. Passengers huddle in shawls and carry old bags tied with rope. The sky turns pink behind the water tank. When the whistle blows, the whole platform comes alive at once.
Describe a village fair on a winter evening, about 90 words.

The village fair glitters under strings of yellow bulbs. A giant wheel turns slowly, and the children scream with joy as it rises. Women bargain for bangles at small stalls, and the air smells of hot jalebis and roasted corn. A drummer plays near the temple while a magician draws a crowd. Boys throw rings at prizes they will never win, and laugh anyway. Everyone wears woollen caps and warm smiles. When the night grows late, the lights go on shining, and nobody wants to leave.
Describe a neighbourhood bakery in the morning, in about 80 words.

The bakery on our lane opens at six, and the smell of fresh bread reaches the end of the street. Inside, trays of golden buns and soft pav are lined up on the counter. The baker's hands are covered in flour, and he hums as he works. Children press their noses against the glass case and point at the cream rolls. A bell rings with every customer. Soon the shelves are half empty, but the warm smell stays all day.
In around 75 words, describe a mountain lake covered in morning fog.

The lake lies silent under a thick white blanket of fog. You cannot see the other shore, only the dark outlines of pine trees that seem to float in the air. The water is still, like glass. A single duck glides through the mist and leaves a thin ripple behind. Cold air touches your cheeks, and everything sounds soft and far away. Slowly, the sun rises, and the fog lifts like a curtain.
A girl's diary entry about a school picnic to a river, about 80 words, please.

Dear Diary,
Today was the best day ever! Our whole class went on a picnic to the river. We played antakshari on the bus, and Mr. Verma sang louder than all of us. We paddled in the water, and Ria slipped and fell, but she laughed it off. We shared lunch under a big banyan tree, and I ate three of Kavya's puris. I am so sleepy now, but I do not want this day to end.
Diary page, about 90 words, for a boy who has just moved into a hostel away from home.

Dear Diary,
Today I was left at the hostel. I waved bravely until the car disappeared, and then I felt a lump in my throat. The room is small, and my roommate Faizan seems friendly. He shared his biscuits with me. The dinner bell rang at eight, and the food was plain but warm. I miss home food and the noise at home. I will try to be strong. Tomorrow, I will find the way to my classroom without getting lost.
Give me a diary entry, about 70 words, from a girl whose team lost the school badminton final today.

Dear Diary,
We lost the final today. I felt so angry on the court that I threw my racket. Later, I felt ashamed. Our coach said that we played with heart, and that this is just one match. My partner cried, and I hugged her. I think we will practise even harder now. I will not give up. Next year, the cup will be ours.
I need a diary entry, about 80 words, of a child at home alone on a rainy Sunday who finds a way to have fun.

Sunday

Dear Diary,
It rained all day, and I was bored. Everyone at home was out, so I had the house to myself. First, I watched the rain, and then I made a fort from cushions and bedsheets. I read my comics in the fort with a torch. After that, I drew a picture of the rain. It turned out to be a very good Sunday after all. When my family came home, they loved my fort.
I want a diary entry of about 90 words by a teenager who spent the day helping her grandmother harvest vegetables at the farm.

Dear Diary,
Today I woke up early and went to the farm with my grandmother. The air smelled of wet soil. We picked tomatoes, brinjals and spring onions, and my hands got dirty. Grandma works faster than I do! She told me stories of her childhood while we filled the baskets. I got a blister on my thumb, but I did not mind. At lunchtime, we ate roti and chutney under a tree. It was the best lunch I have had.
Write a tiny story for children, about 100 words, about a lost baby elephant who finds his way home by following a song.

Bholu, a baby elephant, wandered away from his herd while chasing a butterfly. Soon he was lost deep in the forest, and the trees all looked the same. He felt scared and began to cry. Then he heard a soft song, far away. It was his mother, humming the tune she sang each night. Bholu followed the sound through the bushes and across the stream. At last he saw the herd and ran into his mother's trunk. "Never wander off again," she said, smiling. Bholu promised, and fell asleep to the song.
Write a short story for kids, about 85 words, about a girl who bakes a cake for her mother's birthday but it sinks in the middle.

Kavya wanted to surprise her mother with a cake. She mixed the flour, sugar and eggs carefully and put the cake in the oven. But when she took it out, the middle had sunk into a deep hole. Kavya's eyes filled with tears. Then she had an idea. She filled the hole with whipped cream and strawberries. When her mother came home, she gasped. "What a special cake!" she said, and hugged her. Kavya learnt that mistakes can sometimes make things even sweeter.
Write a story, around 85 words, for primary school children about two friends who quarrel over a toy and then solve the problem.

Sameer and Raju both loved the red toy truck. One day, they pulled it so hard that a wheel came off. "You broke it!" cried Sameer. "No, you did!" said Raju. They sat far apart and did not talk. Soon, they felt sad and lonely. Then Raju picked up the wheel and said, "Shall we fix it together?" They found some glue and worked side by side. The truck rolled again, and both boys smiled. After that, they took turns playing with it.
Tell me a short story for children, about 85 words, about a boy who finds a wallet in the school corridor and returns it.

Dev saw a brown wallet lying in the school corridor. He opened it and found some money and a photo of a girl. He thought about keeping it, but then he imagined the owner crying. He took it to his teacher, Mrs. Rao, who announced it in the assembly. A tall boy from Class 9 ran up, looking very relieved. "Thank you!" he said. "It had my sister's photo." Dev felt warm inside, and from that day, everyone in school knew him as honest Dev.
Write a story for children, about 85 words, about a little seed that is tired of waiting underground.

Deep in the soil, a small seed called Sundar waited and waited. "Nothing ever happens down here," he complained to a worm. "Be patient," said the worm. But Sundar was so bored. Then one day, rain came and soaked the earth. Sundar felt something tickling inside him. A tiny green shoot pushed upward, and it broke through the soil. Above, there was sunshine and a blue sky! Sundar stretched and grew into a strong sapling. "So that is what waiting was for," he said happily.
Why should we be kind to stray animals? Give me a paragraph of about 80 words on it.

Stray animals have no homes, and they often go hungry on hot or rainy days. A little kindness can make a big difference to them. We can put out a bowl of fresh water, share a few scraps of food, or simply speak gently. We should never throw stones or tease them. Animals feel hurt and fear just like us. When we treat them with care, we show that we are kind people, too.
Explain in a paragraph, about 80 words, the benefits of learning a musical instrument for young people.

Learning a musical instrument teaches young people many good things. First, it builds patience, because no one plays well on the first day. It also trains the ears and the hands to work together. Playing in a group teaches teamwork and listening. When you finally play a song for your family, the pride you feel is wonderful. Music can also be a quiet friend on a hard day. Whether it is a flute, a guitar or a harmonium, it is worth the practice.
My teacher asked for a paragraph on 'What Makes a Good Neighbour'. Write about 80 words for a 13-year-old.

A good neighbour is someone who is kind and helpful. She says hello with a smile and does not make loud noises late at night. When there is a problem, a good neighbour is the first to help, whether it is a lost cat or a power cut. She shares sweets at festivals and respects other people's privacy. We may not choose our neighbours, but we can choose to be good ones, and that makes the whole street happier.
Please give me a paragraph of around 80 words about why the monsoon is my favourite season.

The monsoon is my favourite season because it changes everything. After the heat of summer, the first rain makes the whole world smell fresh. The trees turn deep green, and the dusty roads shine. I love to sit by the window with a cup of hot tea and watch the water run down the glass. Sometimes I dance in the rain with my friends, and we do not care if we are wet. For me, rain means happiness.
Write a four-line poem about the moon looking over a sleeping town.

The moon looks down on the sleeping town,
She smiles at the roofs as the stars come down.
She guards each window, each lane, each tree,
And whispers, "Goodnight," to you and me.
Write a short rhyme, 4 lines, for children about a heavy school bag.

My school bag is heavy, it has so much to hold,
Two books, a tiffin, and a bottle that's cold.
My shoulders say, "Oh!" and my back says, "Stop!"
I walk like a turtle with a house on top.
Write a simple 4-line poem about autumn leaves falling.

The leaves come down in red and gold,
They dance and twirl, so brave and bold.
They cover the lane with a rustling sound,
A colourful carpet on the ground.
Write a fun six-line poem about a cup of chai on a cold morning.

The kettle sings, the steam comes up,
I hold my warm and happy cup.
Ginger, cardamom, a pinch of cheer,
The cold goes away when chai is near.
One sip, and I smile, so bright,
Chai makes the morning feel just right.
Write a short poem for my best friend about how we always make each other laugh. Around 65 words, rhyming.

We laugh at jokes that no one gets,
We share our snacks and make our bets.
When days are grey, you make them bright,
You help me feel that things are right.
Through all the years and all the fun,
You're the best friend under the sun.
So here's to us, and here's to more,
To all the laughs we have in store!
Can you write a short thank-you note, about 50 words, to our school watchman Ramu Kaka who always greets us with a smile? We are Class 5.

Dear Ramu Kaka,
Thank you for greeting every one of us with a smile. You always have a kind word and a wave for us. You keep our school safe, and you make us feel welcome. We are lucky to have you.
With respect,
The students of Class 5
I was late for a team meeting because of a traffic jam. I need a short apology message to my team, around 45 words. I'm Chetan.

Hello everyone,
I am sorry for joining the meeting late. A heavy traffic jam delayed me on the way, and I should have allowed more time. Thank you all for your patience, and for carrying on without me. I will catch up on anything I missed.
Regards,
Chetan
Help me write a brief apology to my teacher for talking in class today. About 40 words, in my own voice. I'm Mehul, Class 7.

Dear Teacher,
I am sorry for talking during your lesson today. I know it disturbed my classmates and you. It was not respectful, and I will not do it again. I will listen carefully from now on.
Yours sincerely,
Mehul, Class 7
My sister Anjali got excellent results in her Class 12 exams. Write a happy congratulation message, about 40 words. I'm her brother Nikhil.

Dear Anjali,
Congratulations on your wonderful results! Your hard work has paid off, and I am so proud of you. Let's celebrate together soon. The sky is the limit for you.
Love,
Your brother Nikhil
Our friends Mohit and Sarita have just bought their first home. Could you write a congratulation message for them, around 45 words? It is from Ana and Leo.

Congratulations on your first home! We are so happy for you both. May it be filled with laughter, good food and many happy memories. Wishing you a lifetime of joy under its roof.
Warm wishes,
Ana and Leo

We hope you are feeling better soon. We miss you very much in class. Please rest well, and do not worry about us. We will work hard while you are away. Take care and come back soon!
Your students, Class 4A

I heard about your arm, and I am so sorry! I hope you are not too bored at home. Rest well, and remember that I am only a message away if you want some company. Come back soon, because the team needs you!
Your friend,
Rahul

Aditi

Your daughter,
Sia

Eid Mubarak in advance! We would be very happy if you could come and share our Eid lunch at our home. The meal begins at 1 pm, and we will share a lovely meal together. Your company makes the festival more joyful. Please bring your family, and let us celebrate together.

We want to surprise our class teacher at a farewell. Write a little invitation to Class 8, around 60 words, for a secret party on Friday at lunch break. Sign it Class Representatives.

Our dear class teacher is leaving, and we are planning a surprise farewell party on Friday during the lunch break in our classroom. Please come and join the celebration, and do not tell anyone, especially our teacher. Let us make this a farewell she will never forget.
Class Representatives
Invite my friends to a lakeside picnic next Sunday morning, around 55 words. We will meet at my house at 8 and cycle there together. I'm Imran.

Hey friends,
Let's go on a picnic by the lake next Sunday morning! We will meet at my house at 8 and cycle there together. Bring something yummy to share, and your best smile. Tell me if you can join, and we will plan the rest. It will be a day to remember!
See you,
Imran
Could you write a polite letter from me to our club secretary asking for guitar classes for beginners? About 60 words. My name is Nishant, and I am a member of the Youth Club.

Dear Secretary,
I am Nishant, a member of the Youth Club. I would like to learn the guitar, and I think other members would enjoy it too. I request you to kindly consider arranging classes for beginners. It would be a wonderful chance for all of us to learn something new. Thank you for considering this.
Yours faithfully,
Nishant
The swing in our colony playground is broken and dangerous. Write a polite complaint to the municipal office, about 55 words. I'm Rukmini Nair of Maple Colony.

To the Municipal Officer,
The swings in the children's playground at Maple Colony are broken and dangerous. Children play there, and there is a risk of falling. I request you to repair or replace the swings as soon as possible. Thank you for your help.
Yours sincerely,
Rukmini Nair
My internet has been down for three days. Draft a courteous complaint to the service provider, about 60 words, asking for a quick fix. I'm Ashok Menon.

Dear Support Team,
My internet connection at home has not worked for the last three days, and the delay is causing me great difficulty. Please send a technician as soon as possible and tell me when I can expect the problem to be fixed. I would be grateful for a quick reply. Thank you.
Regards,
Ashok Menon
Please help me write a note to the school librarian asking to keep a book for one more week, since I couldn't finish it. About 50 words. I'm Diya of Class 7.

Dear Librarian,
I am Diya of Class 7. I have borrowed a book from the library, but I could not finish reading it. May I please keep it for one more week? I will return it on the new date and take good care of it. Thank you.
Diya

Write a message to my hostel warden asking for permission to go home for the weekend for my sister's engagement this Sunday. I would leave on Friday evening and return on Sunday night. About 60 words. I'm Ashna in Room 12.

Dear Warden,
I am Ashna from Room 12. My sister's engagement ceremony will be held this Sunday, and I would very much like to attend. I request your permission to leave the hostel on Friday evening and return on Sunday night. I would be very grateful if you could allow this. Thank you for your kind consideration.
Yours sincerely,
Ashna
I'm 15 and want to join the district swimming coaching camp. Write an email to the coach asking about trial dates, in about 65 words. Name: Arush Malhotra.

Subject: Query about trial dates

Dear Coach,
I am Arush Malhotra, fifteen years old, and I would like to join your district swimming coaching camp. I enjoy swimming very much and want to improve my skills. Could you please tell me when the trials will be held? I will be very grateful for any information. Thank you for your time.
Sincerely,
Arush Malhotra
Need an email to our HR team asking for an experience certificate, since I'm leaving at the end of the month. About 60 words. I'm Sanya Kapoor.

Subject: Request for experience certificate

Dear HR Team,
I will be leaving the company at the end of this month. I would be grateful if you could prepare my experience certificate before my last working day. Please tell me if you need any documents from my side. Thank you for your support during my time here.
Best regards,
Sanya Kapoor
Please draft a short email to a bookshop asking when the novel I ordered ten days ago will arrive. About 70 words. Order name: Rekha Thomas.

Subject: Status of my book order

Dear Sir or Madam,
I placed an order for a novel at your shop ten days ago under the name Rekha Thomas, and I have not received it yet. Could you please tell me when I can expect delivery? If the book is out of stock, kindly let me know. Thank you for your help.
Yours sincerely,
Rekha Thomas

As a parent, I'd like to ask the school principal if the school bus can stop near our new apartments, Green Valley Apartments. Compose a respectful email, about 70 words. I'm Mr. Thakur, father of a Class 4 student.

Subject: Request for a bus stop near Green Valley Apartments

Dear Principal,
I am Mr. Thakur, father of a Class 4 student. We live in Green Valley Apartments, and I would like to ask whether the school bus could add a stop near our apartments. It would be a great convenience for the families here. I would be happy to share any details you may need. I would be thankful if you could consider this request.
Respectfully,
Mr. Thakur
Make a notice for the school's Science Club meeting this Thursday at 3 pm in Lab 2. All students from Class 8 up are welcome. Around 55 words. Sign it Mr. Rao, Club Advisor.

SCIENCE CLUB MEETING

The Science Club will meet this Thursday at 3 pm in Lab 2. All students from Class 8 and above are welcome. Come with your questions, ideas and curiosity, and be part of the fun. We look forward to seeing you there!

Mr. Rao, Club Advisor
I need a notice for a rangoli competition at our society for Diwali, around 60 words. It will be Saturday at 5 pm in the courtyard, with prizes for children and adults. Sign it Cultural Committee.

RANGOLI COMPETITION

Our society invites all residents to a Diwali rangoli competition on Saturday at 5 pm in the courtyard. There will be prizes for both children and adults. Everyone is welcome to take part. Come and make our building bright and beautiful for the festival, and share the joy with your neighbours!

Cultural Committee
Prepare a notice for the neighbourhood that there will be a book fair in the community hall from Friday to Sunday, 10 am to 6 pm. About 55 words. Sign it Library Friends Group.

BOOK FAIR

A book fair will be held in the community hall from Friday to Sunday, between 10 am and 6 pm. Come and browse the books, and find something new to read. Everyone in the neighbourhood is welcome, so bring your family and friends. Happy reading!

Library Friends Group
Describe a sunrise at the beach in about 80 words.

The sky turns pale grey, then soft pink. A thin line of orange appears at the edge of the sea, and slowly the sun rises like a big gold coin. The waves catch the colour and glow. A few fishermen push their boats into the water, while crows and gulls cry overhead. The sand is cool and damp under bare feet. A small crab runs sideways and disappears into a hole. It is a quiet and perfect start to the day.
Describe a school canteen during the lunch break, about 90 words.

At the lunch bell, the canteen explodes with noise. Children rush in and form a long queue at the counter. Plates clatter, and the cook shouts, "Next!" The air smells of hot samosas and sweet tea. At one table, a group of boys argue about last night's match. At another, two girls share a packet of chips and giggle. A teacher walks past, smiling and shaking her head. Within twenty minutes, the tables are empty again, and the cleaners come in to sweep up the crumbs.
Write about 70 words on how a garden looks on the first day of spring.

On the first day of spring, the garden seems to wake up. Tiny buds open on the rose bushes, and new green leaves peek out from the old branches. Bees buzz from flower to flower, and butterflies flutter about. The grass is soft and wet with dew. A robin sings from the fence. The air is fresh and sweet. After the long, cold winter, everything is alive again, and so are we.
Describe a small town library in the afternoon, about 80 words.

In the afternoon, the town library is quiet and cool. Sunlight falls through the tall windows onto long wooden tables. An old man reads the newspaper, and a girl with plaits sits cross-legged on the floor, lost in a picture book. The librarian stamps cards with a soft thump. The ceiling fan creaks as it turns. There is a smell of old paper and polish. Nobody speaks above a whisper, yet the whole room feels full of stories.
Diary time: a student on the last day of school before the summer holidays, in about 75 words.

Dear Diary,
It is finally the last day of school! We cleaned our desks, returned our library books, and said goodbye to our teachers. My best friend and I promised to meet at the park during the holidays. I walked home slowly, because I did not want to leave the school gate. But I am also excited for ice cream, mangoes and long mornings. Summer, here I come!
Write a diary entry, about 75 words, of a girl who made a new friend at the park today after feeling shy.

Dear Diary,
I felt very shy at the park today. All the children were playing, and I stood alone near the slide. Then a girl with a red ribbon came and asked, "Do you want to play with me?" Her name is Sunaina. We played catch, and we climbed the small hill together. She laughs just like a bell! We decided to meet again tomorrow. I am so glad I said yes.
Diary entry, about 90 words, for a boy who got a very low mark on a test and is nervous about telling his parents.

Dear Diary,
I got a very low mark in maths today. My stomach felt heavy all the way home. I have been rehearsing what to say to my parents. I know I did not study enough, and I feel ashamed. But I think it is better to tell them the truth than to hide the paper. Tonight, I will show it to them and ask for help. I hope they will understand. I must try harder next time.
Write about 90 words in diary form for a traveller on a houseboat in Kerala.

Dear Diary,
We are floating slowly on a houseboat in the Kerala backwaters. The water is calm, and green palm trees line the banks. The cook has made fish curry and red rice, and I ate more than I should. A kingfisher dived near our boat this afternoon. In the evening, we saw village women washing clothes at the edge, and children waved at us. I have never felt so peaceful. I wish this trip would last a month.
Please write a diary entry of about 75 words for a girl who had a fun sleepover with her friends.

Dear Diary,
Last night, three of my friends slept over at my house. We made popcorn and watched a funny film. Then we told ghost stories in the dark under blankets, and Ritu screamed so loudly that everyone came running! We giggled until midnight. This morning, we made pancakes, and Aisha burnt hers. Now the house is quiet again, and I miss them already. I hope we can do it again very soon.
Tell a children's story, about 100 words, about a crow who learns to share a piece of bread with a hungry dog.

Kallu the crow found a big piece of bread and flew to a high branch. Below, a thin brown dog was looking up at him, sniffing. "Please, can I have a little?" the dog asked. "No!" said Kallu. "It is mine." He began to eat, but a crumb fell, and then the whole piece slipped down. Kallu was sad and hungry. Then the dog picked it up, broke it in two, and offered Kallu half. Kallu was ashamed. "Thank you," he whispered. From then on, they shared everything they found.
Write a tiny story, about 80 words, for children about a boy who forgets his homework and tells the truth.

Rahul forgot his homework notebook at home. In the morning, his friend Jay whispered, "Say your dog ate it!" Rahul thought about it, but his tummy felt funny. When the teacher asked, he stood up and said, "Ma'am, I forgot my notebook. I am sorry." The class waited. Ma'am smiled. "Thank you for being honest, Rahul. Bring it tomorrow." Rahul felt light as a feather. At home, he finished his work, packed it first in his bag, and went to bed happy.
Write a gentle story for small children, about 85 words, about a girl who is scared of thunder, and her grandmother helps her.

Mira hated thunder. Whenever the sky growled, she hid under her blanket. One stormy night, the thunder was very loud, and she ran to her grandmother's room. "Grandma, I am scared," she whispered. Grandma hugged her and said, "Let's count the seconds after each flash. Thunder is just the sky clapping." They counted together, and each clap felt smaller. Soon, Mira was giggling. "The sky is clapping for the rain!" she said. That night, she slept peacefully, and she was never afraid of thunder again.
Write a short story, around 100 words, for kids about a boy who lights a diya for the first time and learns to be careful.

Arnav was seven, and he wanted to light a diya on Diwali night. "Let me do it, Papa!" he begged. Papa gave him a long matchstick and showed him how to hold it away from his clothes. Arnav's hands shook, but he lit the wick. The little flame danced. "Wow!" he said. Then a breeze came, and his sleeve almost touched it. Papa gently moved him back. "Fire is beautiful, but we must be careful," he said. Arnav nodded. He placed the diya at the door and smiled.
Make up a story for children, about 100 words, about a turtle who wins a race by never giving up.

Tara the turtle wanted to join the forest race, and the animals laughed. "You are too slow," they said. But Tara signed up anyway. At the start, the rabbit and the deer dashed away. Tara walked one step at a time, never stopping. By noon, the rabbit was napping, and the deer was drinking water. Tara kept going, past the hill and the stream. In the evening, she crossed the finish line first, tired and smiling. The animals gasped and then clapped. "You won," said the owl, "because you never gave up."
Can you give me a short paragraph, about 80 words, on why we should say 'thank you' more often?

Saying "thank you" costs nothing, but it means so much. When we thank a person, we show that we notice what she or he did for us. It makes the other person feel respected and happy. A simple thank you to the bus driver, the shopkeeper or the cleaner can brighten their whole day. It also teaches us to be grateful for small things. If we say it every day, kindness will spread, and the world will feel a little warmer.
A paragraph for a nature club newsletter, about 70 words, on why we should save water at home.

Water is precious, and we must use it wisely. A running tap while we brush our teeth wastes many litres. We can close it between uses and fix every leaking pipe. We can collect used water to wash the floor or to water plants. Small habits at home may seem tiny, but together they save a lot. If we save water today, our children will have enough to drink tomorrow.
Write 80 words on how a family dinner without phones feels, for a school essay about family time.

A family dinner without phones feels warm and close. We look at each other's faces instead of our screens. Everyone tells funny stories from their day, and we laugh while we pass the dal and rice. We really listen to one another. Nobody is in a hurry. When dinner ends, we feel full, not only in the stomach but also in the heart. It is the best part of my day.
Write a four-line poem for children about a little frog who jumps in puddles.

A little green frog went hop, hop, hop,
He jumped in puddles, he would not stop.
Splash! went the water, up to his chin,
And all of his friends said, "Come on in!"
Please write a rhyme of 6 lines for a toddler about brushing teeth before bed.

Brush, brush, brush your teeth,
Up on top and underneath.
Little circles, round and round,
Make a clean and happy sound.
Rinse and spit, and say goodnight,
Sparkly smile, shiny bright!
Could you compose a short poem, 4 to 6 lines, about being homesick when you move to a new city?

The streets are strange, the faces new,
I miss the home I always knew.
The evening lights are bright and loud,
But I feel small inside the crowd.
Still, hope will rise like morning's glow,
And friendly faces I will know.
Write a rhyming poem of four lines about a rainbow after the rain.

The rain has gone, the sky is bright,
A rainbow shines with coloured light.
Red and yellow, green and blue,
A painted bridge in every hue.
I'd like a short poem, about 55 words, thanking teachers, to recite on Teachers' Day.

You teach us letters, you teach us sums,
You wipe our tears when sadness comes.
You show us how to be good and kind,
You plant great dreams within our mind.
Thank you for your patient care,
For all the lessons that you share.
We will remember you each day,
Dear teachers, in every way.
Say thank you to my colleague Prakash for covering my shift when my father was visiting from abroad. About 50 words, please. I'm Alok.

Dear Prakash,
Thank you for covering my shift while my father was visiting from abroad. Because of you, I could spend precious time with him. I will happily return the favour whenever you need it. You are a wonderful colleague, and I am very grateful.
Warm regards,
Alok
I need to politely remind my flatmate Brinda that she owes me her share of the broadband bill. Around 45 words, no pressure. I'm Sneha.

Hi Brinda,
Hope your day is going well. This is just a small reminder about your share of the broadband bill. Could you send it to me when you get a chance? Thanks a lot, and there is no hurry at all.
Sneha
I promised my friend Zubin I'd help him move and then cancelled. Write a short, honest sorry message, about 55 words. I'm Faisal.

Hi Zubin,
I am really sorry that I cancelled on helping you move. I know you counted on me, and I let you down. I should have told you earlier. Please let me make it up to you. Is there anything I can still do to help? I feel bad about it.
Faisal
Our neighbours' daughter Ananya got into medical college. Write them a message of congratulations, about 55 words. They are Mr. and Mrs. Iyer, and it is from the Sinha family.

Dear Mr. and Mrs. Iyer,
Heartiest congratulations on Ananya's admission to medical college! She truly deserves this, and you must be so proud. Please give her our blessings and best wishes. We are sure she will go far, and we are delighted for your whole family.
Warm regards,
The Sinha family
My friend Meghna has just returned home from the hospital after a long stay. Write a warm welcome-back message, about 55 words, with no medical advice. It is from her friends.

Dear Meghna,
Welcome home! The house must feel so good after all that time away. We missed you so much, and we are very happy to know you are back home. Please take all the time you need. We are always here whenever you want a chat or a cup of tea.
Your friends
Congratulate my brother Chirag, who just ran his first ten-kilometre race and finished. Around 50 words, with a bit of humour. I'm his sister Vani.

Dear Chirag,
You did it! You actually ran ten kilometres, and you finished! I am so proud of you. Your legs may complain for a while, but you have earned a very big plate of food. Let's celebrate soon, and I will happily listen to every detail of the race.
Your sister, Vani
Write a short message for my father, whom I call Papa, who is travelling tonight, wishing him a safe journey. Around 40 words. I'm Tina.

Dear Papa,
Wishing you a safe and comfortable journey tonight. Please call us when you reach, and take care on the way. We will miss you at home and look forward to seeing you back soon.
Love,
Tina
Remind my parents, whom I call Mummy and Papa, to switch off the geyser and gas before they leave for the wedding tomorrow. About 40 words, friendly tone. I'm Kunal.

Dear Mummy and Papa,
Just a little reminder before you leave for the wedding tomorrow. Please switch off the geyser and the gas,. Have a lovely time, and eat a lot of sweets for me!
Love,
Kunal
I'd like to thank the volunteers who cleaned our beach on Sunday. Write a short post, around 45 words, for our community group. Sign it Beach Care Team.

Dear Volunteers,
A big thank you to everyone who came to clean our beach on Sunday. Together, you made the sand look beautiful again. Your hard work shows how much one small group can do. We are proud to be part of it.
Beach Care Team
My friend Shalini is turning thirty. Write a funny but warm birthday message, about 45 words. I'm Meera.

Dear Shalini,
Happy thirtieth birthday! You are officially old enough to give advice and young enough to ignore it. You have always made life brighter with your laughter. May this year be full of cake, adventure and very few boring days. Love you lots!
Meera
Invite our relatives to a small thread ceremony for my son Aryan, about 55 words. It is next Saturday at 9 am at our house, followed by lunch. It is from Hema and Girish.

Dear Relatives,
We are happy to invite you to the thread ceremony of our son Aryan. It will take place next Saturday at 9 am at our house, and lunch will follow. We would be deeply grateful for your blessings and your presence. Please bring the whole family and share this special day with us.
Yours lovingly,
Hema and Girish
Plan a short invitation, about 50 words, for my team to a Friday evening tea and snacks at 5 pm in the office pantry to welcome a new teammate, Zainab. I'm Jyoti.

Dear Team,
Please join us this Friday at 5 pm in the office pantry for tea and snacks. Let us welcome our new teammate, Zainab. Come and say hello, share a laugh, and help her feel at home. It will be a lovely evening!
Warm regards,
Jyoti
I'm starting a small book club for friends. Write an invitation about 55 words for the first meeting at my house on Sunday at 4 pm. We will discuss one short story. I'm Ananya.

Hello book lovers,
I am starting a small book club, and I would love to have you join. Our first meeting is at my house on Sunday at 4 pm. We will talk about one short story, which I will share with you before then. There will be good company and lively conversation. Come as you are, and bring a friend.
Ananya
Invite my neighbours' kids to a free cycling day I am hosting on Saturday morning at 8 in the lane behind the park, around 50 words. Sign it Uncle Rajan.

Dear children,
Come and join my Cycling Day this Saturday at 8 in the morning in the lane behind the park. Come with your bicycle and get ready to ride and have fun. It is free for everyone. Your parents are welcome to come and cheer. See you there!
Uncle Rajan
Our colony is holding a Christmas carol evening. Could you draft the invitation, about 55 words? Friday, 7 pm, near the clock tower. Sign it The Colony Choir.

Dear Neighbours,
Come and sing with us at our Christmas Carol Evening this Friday at 7 pm near the clock tower. Bring your voices and your family, and join us for plenty of joyful music. Everyone is welcome, whether you can sing well or not. Let us fill the lane with cheer!
The Colony Choir
A mobile shop sold me a charger that does not work. Write a polite complaint to the shopkeeper, around 60 words, asking for a replacement. I bought it on Monday. I'm Lakshman.

Dear Shopkeeper,
I bought a phone charger from your shop on Monday, and it does not work. I would like to bring this to your attention and request a replacement. Could you please replace it at your earliest convenience? I am sure we can resolve this easily. I would be grateful for your help.
Yours sincerely,
Lakshman
I stayed at a hotel where the room was not cleaned and the bathroom was dirty. Write a polite but clear complaint to the hotel manager, about 70 words. Name: Mr. Anand Verma, Room 214.

Dear Manager,
I am staying in Room 214, and I would like to bring some problems to your attention. The room has not been cleaned, and the bathroom is dirty. This has made my stay uncomfortable. Please send housekeeping as soon as possible, and I would appreciate it if the room could be cleaned thoroughly. I am sure you will take this seriously. Thank you.
Regards,
Anand Verma
Help me ask my upstairs neighbour, kindly, to stop hanging wet clothes that drip onto my balcony. About 55 words. I'm Madhavi, Flat 3.

Dear Neighbour,
I hope you are well. I wanted to mention something small. The wet clothes on your balcony sometimes drip onto my balcony. Could you please wring them out a little more before hanging them? I would really appreciate it. Thank you for understanding, and have a lovely day.
Warm regards,
Madhavi, Flat 3
Our local market's pavement has a big pothole where an old lady nearly fell. Write a polite message, around 60 words, to the ward office to ask for repair.

Dear Sir or Madam,
There is a large pothole on the pavement at our local market. An elderly lady almost fell in it, and it could cause a serious accident. I request you to have it repaired as soon as possible. I hope the matter can be given priority. Thank you for your attention.
Yours sincerely,
A concerned resident
Draft an email to a client, Mr. Ghosh, politely saying that the project will be delayed by three days because of a data issue, and apologising. About 65 words. I'm Pallavi.

Subject: Update on project delivery

Dear Mr. Ghosh,
I wanted to inform you that the project will be delivered three days later than planned. An issue was found in the data, and I want to fix it properly before sending anything to you. I sincerely apologise for the delay, and I understand that it may cause inconvenience. Thank you for your patience and understanding.
Sincerely,
Pallavi
I have to ask my manager to review a presentation before Wednesday. Compose a short email, about 55 words. Manager's name is Mr. Pinto; I'm Divya.

Subject: Request to review presentation

Dear Mr. Pinto,
I have prepared my presentation. Could you please review it before Wednesday and tell me what to improve? I would be grateful for any suggestions you have. I will make the changes as soon as I get your comments. Thank you very much for your time and guidance.
Best regards,
Divya
Please email my landlady, Mrs. Fernandes, to say that I will be moving out at the end of next month and ask about the process. About 70 words. I'm Aman.

Subject: Notice of moving out

Dear Mrs. Fernandes,
I am writing to inform you that I will be moving out of the flat at the end of next month. Could you please let me know the process I should follow, and any steps I need to complete before I leave? Please tell me if you need anything else from my side. Thank you for your time.
Sincerely,
Aman
Email my cousin Reena in Bengaluru, asking whether I can stay with her for two nights next month during my job interview. Friendly tone, about 70 words. I'm Gita.

Subject: Can I crash at your place?

Hi Reena,
I hope you are doing well! I have an interview in Bengaluru next month, and I was wondering if I could stay with you for two nights. I promise to be a quiet guest and not to trouble you. Please tell me if it is convenient. I would love to catch up, too.
Lots of love,
Gita
Make a notice announcing that the community hall will be used for a free stitching class for women on Tuesdays and Thursdays at 11 am. About 55 words. Sign it Women's Welfare Group.

FREE STITCHING CLASS

A free stitching class for women will be held in the community hall every Tuesday and Thursday at 11 am. Come and learn a useful skill in a friendly group. All women are welcome, so bring a friend along. We look forward to seeing you there, and we hope you will enjoy every class.

Women's Welfare Group
Prepare a notice for our neighbourhood about a free Sunday movie for children in the community hall, at 4 pm. About 60 words, cheerful tone. Sign it Cultural Group.

FREE MOVIE FOR KIDS!

Come and watch a fun children's film this Sunday at 4 pm in the community hall. It is free for all children, so bring your friends and your biggest smile. Parents are welcome to come along and enjoy it too. Let us enjoy a cheerful afternoon together!

Cultural Group
Write a notice about a clothes donation drive next Saturday at the community centre from 9 to 1. About 55 words. Sign it Seva Group.

CLOTHES DONATION DRIVE

Our community centre will collect clean, usable clothes next Saturday between 9 am and 1 pm. Please bring any clothes that you no longer need. They will be given to families who need them. Every piece will make someone's life a little easier. Thank you for your kindness.

Seva Group
Write a notice for the bus stand's board saying that the 7 am bus to Mysuru will leave from platform 3 for the next week only. About 65 words. Sign it Station Manager.

NOTICE TO PASSENGERS

For the next week only, the 7 am bus to Mysuru will leave from Platform 3. Please check the board before boarding so that you do not miss your bus. Passengers are advised to reach the platform a little early and plan their journey accordingly. We regret the change and thank you for your patience.

Station Manager
Describe a busy bus stop in the evening in about 85 words.

At six in the evening, the bus stop is packed. Office workers stand with tired faces and heavy bags, checking their watches. A flower-seller offers jasmine strings, and a boy sells peanuts in paper cones. When a bus arrives, everyone pushes forward at once, and the conductor shouts the stops. A small girl waits holding a grown-up's hand tightly. Horns blare and dust rises. Finally, the bus moves away, and a quiet minute follows before the next crowd arrives.
Describe how a street looks on a winter morning with fog, about 80 words.

The street is wrapped in a soft grey fog. Cars crawl with their lights on, and the streetlamps look like pale moons. People walk with shawls tied over their heads and breath that rises like smoke. A man at the corner warms his hands at a small fire. The milkman's bicycle bell rings somewhere in the mist, but you cannot see him. Everything is slow and muffled, as if the world has been wrapped in cotton.
Describe a flower market just before a festival, in about 90 words.

The flower market is a flood of colour. Heaps of orange marigolds, white jasmine and red roses lie in baskets on the ground. Women thread garlands quickly, their fingers busy and quick. The scent is so strong that it makes you dizzy. Buyers bargain loudly, and sellers shout the price of a metre of flowers. A boy carries a huge sack of petals on his head. Bees buzz around in the morning light. Every stall seems to say that the festival will be beautiful.
Describe my grandfather's armchair and the corner of the house where he sits, in about 70 words. He reads the newspaper there every morning.

In the corner of the house stands my grandfather's armchair, where he sits and reads the newspaper every morning. The seat has taken the shape of him after so many mornings, and the arms are worn smooth. The corner is quiet, and the rustle of newspaper pages is the only sound. Nobody else sits in the chair. It feels like a quiet throne in the middle of our busy home.
I'd like a diary entry, about 75 words, for a shopkeeper at the end of a very slow day with almost no customers.

Dear Diary,
It was a very slow day. Only a few customers came, and some of them just asked for directions. I sat behind the counter and arranged the shelves three times. Still, an old customer came in for her bread and chatted with me for half an hour. That was nice. Tomorrow is a new day, and hopefully it will bring people back to the shop.
Write the diary entry of an old woman who is happy because her grandchildren visited her for the whole day. About 75 words.

Dear Diary,
Today my house was full of noise again, and I loved every minute of it. My grandchildren came in the morning with a bag of mangoes and big hugs. We played carrom, and little Sia beat me twice. I cooked puris and aloo curry, and they finished it all. When they left in the evening, the house became quiet. But my heart is full, and I will sleep with a smile tonight.
A diary entry of about 80 words, please, for a young man who has just finished painting his first big canvas.

Dear Diary,
Tonight I put the last stroke on my first big painting. It took me six weeks. It shows our old banyan tree at sunset. I stepped back, and for the first time I felt proud of my work. Of course, the leaves are a bit crooked, and the sky is too orange. But it is mine. I will hang it in my room and show it to my friends tomorrow. I want to paint more.
Diary entry, about 95 words, by a person who feels nervous before the first day of a new job tomorrow.

Dear Diary,
Tomorrow I start my new job, and I cannot sleep. I have ironed my shirt twice and packed my bag three times. What if I forget someone's name? What if I make a mistake in the first hour? Then I tell myself that everyone feels nervous on the first day. I will smile, listen well, and ask questions. I will reach early and take a deep breath at the door. Whatever happens, I will learn something new. Goodnight, diary.
Could you write a diary entry, about 85 words, for a girl on her first aeroplane ride.

Dear Diary,
Today I flew in an aeroplane for the first time! At the airport, I stared at the big planes outside the glass. When ours began to run, my heart thumped. Then, suddenly, we were in the air, and the houses below looked like tiny toys. I saw the clouds from above, white and fluffy like mountains of cotton. The juice and snacks were also good. I did not want to land. I will fly again someday.
