Write a short story for children, about 80 words, about a fisherman who finds a tiny fish in his net and decides to let it go.

Old Raghu cast his net into the sea every morning. One day, among the big fish, he found a tiny silver one. "You are too small to sell," he said. The little fish trembled. Raghu looked at it for a while, then gently lowered it back into the water. "Go and grow," he said. Years later, when his nets stayed empty during a storm, a huge shoal of silver fish swam in. Raghu smiled. He knew the sea remembered kindness.
Please write a funny story, about 100 words, for children about a monkey who steals a hat and gets into trouble.

Bantu the monkey saw a red hat on a cart and grabbed it. He put it on his head and danced happily on a roof. But the hat was too big, and it fell over his eyes. He could not see! He walked straight off the roof and landed in a pile of hay. The hat's owner, a hat seller, laughed. "You look like a little king," he said. Bantu felt silly. He gave the hat back, and the seller gave him a banana in return. Bantu went home happy.
Story for young readers, please, about 100 words, in which two friends get lost in a market and find each other by singing a song.

Asha and Noor were shopping with their grandmother when a crowd pushed them apart. Both girls were lost in the busy market. Asha felt scared, and she tried to call, but her voice was lost in the noise. Then she remembered their favourite song and started to sing it. At the other end of the market, Noor heard the tune and sang back. They followed each other's voices until they met near the sweet shop. They hugged tightly. "Next time, we hold hands," they said, and held them all the way home.
Write a bedtime story, around 100 words, about a little girl who cannot sleep until her father shows her how to count the stars.

Little Riya could not sleep. She tossed and turned, and her pillow felt too warm. Her father came in and said, "Let's go to the window." They looked at the dark sky full of stars. "Let's count them, softly," he said. They began, one, two, three, and soon lost count. Riya laughed quietly. "There are too many!" Her father tucked her in. "Then count them in your dreams," he whispered. Riya closed her eyes and began to count again. Before she reached ten, she was fast asleep.
Give me a story for children, around 85 words, about a baby bird who is afraid to fly from the nest and finds the courage.

Pinky, a baby sparrow, sat at the edge of her nest and looked down. The ground was very far away. "I'll fall," she whispered. Her mother flew nearby and called, "Just spread your wings, dear." Pinky shut her eyes and jumped. For a moment, she dropped, and her tummy tickled. Then the wind caught her tiny wings, and she was flying! She saw the treetops and the sunlit river. "I am flying!" she chirped. Her mother smiled. From that day, Pinky flew every morning without fear.
Write a paragraph, about 80 words, on how video calls help families who live far apart.

Video calls bring families closer when they live far apart. A grandmother in a village can see her grandson's first steps in another city. Parents can watch their children blow out birthday candles on a screen. Festivals no longer feel lonely, because everyone can share the sweets and songs together. Of course, a call is never the same as a hug, but it makes the distance feel smaller. A smiling face on a screen can brighten even a hard day.
I need a paragraph of about 80 words on why home-cooked food tastes special.

Home-cooked food tastes special because it is made with care. The person who cooks knows who likes less salt and who wants an extra chilli. The smell of tadka drifting from the kitchen tells us that someone is thinking of us. We eat together and talk about our day. Even a simple meal of dal and rice feels like a feast when it is made at home. It feeds not only our hunger, but also our hearts.
Put into a paragraph, about 70 words, the pleasure of an evening walk after a busy day.

An evening walk is a gentle reward after a busy day. The sun is soft, and the air feels cooler. You see neighbours chatting, children playing, and birds returning to their trees. Your mind slows down and your worries seem smaller. You can walk alone and think, or with a friend and talk. When you return home, you feel calm and ready for a simple dinner and a good night's sleep.
Write a paragraph of about 70 words about what I like about gardening. I grow tomatoes and roses on my balcony.

I love gardening because it teaches me patience. On my balcony, I grow tomatoes and roses in old tins and pots. Every morning, I water them and look for new buds. When a red tomato finally ripens, I feel so proud. Sometimes the roses bring a butterfly or a bee. Gardening is slow, quiet work, but it makes my days cheerful. A small green corner can bring a big joy.
Write a short poem, six lines, about a river that flows from the mountains to the sea.

From a mountain's snowy crown I start,
I tumble down with a joyful heart.
Through valleys, fields and towns I flow,
Where children splash and grasses grow.
At last I meet the sea so wide,
And rest in her arms at the end of my ride.
Write a four-line lullaby for a baby.

Sleep, my little one, sleep tight,
The moon is up, the stars are bright.
Close your eyes, the day is done,
Dream of sunshine and of fun.
Write a funny four-line poem about a hungry elephant who ate all the bananas.

A hungry elephant, big and grey,
Ate all the bananas in one day.
His tummy rumbled, "Oh, what a shame!
Now there are none, and I'm to blame!"
Write a short rhyme with 4 lines about two friends who play together every evening.

We meet at five, you and me,
We play beneath the mango tree.
We run and jump, we laugh and shout,
Until the stars come peeking out.
Write a simple poem of 4 to 6 lines about feeling proud after finishing something difficult.

I climbed the hill, the path was steep,
My legs were tired, my breath was deep.
But when I stood upon the top,
I smiled so wide I could not stop.
The world looked small, the sky looked free,
And I felt proud of what I could be.
My cousin Meera made me a handmade bookmark with dried flowers for my birthday. Write a thank-you note to her, about 45 words.

Dear Meera,
Thank you for the lovely bookmark. I love how you pressed the flowers so carefully, and I will use it often. It was so thoughtful of you to make something yourself. I will keep it safe for years.
With love,
Your cousin
I forgot to feed my sister Pooja's fish while she was away for the weekend. Write a short sorry note to her, about 50 words.

Dear Pooja,
I am very sorry that I forgot to feed your fish while you were away. I should have set a reminder. I know how much they mean to you. Please forgive me, and let me make it up to you.
With love
Write a congratulations message, about 40 words, for my colleague Arjun, who has just been promoted to senior engineer.

Dear Arjun,
Congratulations on your promotion to senior engineer! You have earned it through your hard work, and I am very happy for you. I am glad to work with you. Well done, and best wishes for your new role.
Best regards
Mr. Kulkarni next door sprained his ankle and cannot go out. Write a short get-well note, about 40 words, that I can slip under his door.

Dear Mr. Kulkarni,
I was sorry to hear about your ankle. I hope it mends quickly and that you are out and about again soon. If you need any help, please just knock on my door. Get well soon!
Warm wishes
Write a reminder note, about 35 words, for my brother to charge his laptop tonight and pack the charger for his college presentation tomorrow.

Hey,
Quick reminder: please charge your laptop tonight and put the charger in your bag. You do not want a flat battery during your presentation tomorrow. Pack it before you sleep. You will do really well!
With love
I missed a week of class and my friend Leela shared all her notes with me. Write a thank-you message to her, about 45 words.

Dear Leela,
Thank you so much for sharing your notes from the week I missed. Your notes made it much easier to catch up, and I could follow every topic. I really appreciate your help. Whenever you miss a class, my notes are yours.
Your friend
My group's science project was delayed because I forgot to bring my part to school. Write a sorry message to my group mates, about 50 words.

Hi everyone,
I am really sorry that I forgot to bring my part of the project. It slowed all of us down, and that was my mistake. I will bring it as soon as I can, and I will help finish the rest. Thank you for being patient.
Your group mate
My friend Kavya's first poem has been published in a magazine. Write her a congratulations message, about 45 words.

Dear Kavya,
Congratulations on seeing your first poem in print! I always knew your words deserved readers, and now many people will enjoy them. I am so proud of you. Please read it aloud to me when we meet. This is only the beginning!
Your friend
I am the class teacher. Write a reminder to parents, about 40 words, that the signed picnic permission slip must reach school by Monday.

Dear Parents,
This is a reminder that the signed permission slip for the class picnic must reach school by Monday. Please do not forget to send it with your child. Thank you for your help.
Class Teacher
My friend Rohan's family is moving to another city next week. Write him a warm goodbye message, about 40 words, saying I will miss him and we should stay in touch.

Dear Rohan,
I will miss you so much. Our time together made every day better. I hope you find good friends in your new city, but please do not forget us. Let us call often and meet during the holidays.
Your friend
Help me invite my relatives to a surprise dinner for my parents' 30th wedding anniversary. It is at our house on Saturday at 7 pm. Keep it to about 40 words, and ask guests to keep the secret.

Dear all,
You are warmly invited to a surprise dinner for my parents' 30th wedding anniversary. It will be at our house this Saturday at 7 pm. Most importantly, please keep it a secret! We hope to see you there.
Invite people to a poetry reading evening at our neighbourhood library on Friday at 6 pm. About 50 words, and anyone can read their own poem.

Come and share a poem! Our neighbourhood library invites you to a poetry reading evening this Friday at 6 pm. Everyone is welcome, and anyone may read a poem of their own. You can also just sit back and listen. Please join us for an evening of words.
It's my 10th birthday soon, and I want to invite my classmates to a pool party on Sunday at 4 pm at the community pool. Write the invitation in about 45 words.

Hello, friends!
I am turning 10 and I am having a pool party. Please come to the community pool this Sunday at 4 pm. Come ready to swim and have fun, and bring your biggest smile. I cannot wait to splash around with you all!
Write a short message, about 50 words, inviting my classmates to study for the science exam at my house on Thursday at 6 pm.

Hi everyone,
Let us study for the science exam together! Please come to my house on Thursday at 6 pm. Bring your notebooks and any questions you want to ask. We can test each other and share our best tips. Hope you can join!
We want to invite our cousins to a Raksha Bandhan lunch at our house. Write a warm invitation in about 55 words. Mention that all the sisters will tie rakhis before lunch.

Dear cousins,
Raksha Bandhan is almost here, and we would love to celebrate with you. Please join us for lunch at our house. All the sisters will tie rakhis before we eat, so come a little early. We will have plenty of food and plenty of laughter. It would not feel complete without you!
With love
An online shop sent me school shoes in the wrong size. Write a polite email to the shop, about 70 words, asking to exchange them for the correct size.

Subject: Request to exchange shoes

Dear Sir or Madam,
I ordered a pair of school shoes from your online shop, but the pair that reached me is the wrong size. Could you please tell me how I can exchange them for the correct size? I would be grateful for a reply soon. Please let me know if you need the order details. Thank you for your help.
Yours faithfully
Write a polite request, about 50 words, to our sports teacher to let me borrow the school football for the weekend, because my cousins and I want to practise. I promise to return it on Monday.

Dear Sports Teacher,
May I please borrow a school football for this weekend? My cousins and I would like to practise together. I promise to look after it carefully and return it to you on Monday. I would be very grateful for your permission. Thank you for your time.
Yours respectfully
The air conditioning was not working during the film we saw at a cinema hall, and the seats were sticky. Write a polite complaint to the manager, about 60 words.

Dear Manager,
We watched a film at your cinema hall recently, and I must share two problems. The air conditioning was not working, so the hall became very hot. The seats were also sticky and uncomfortable. These things spoiled our visit. I hope you will look into them soon, so that other visitors can feel comfortable.
Yours sincerely
The streetlight in our lane has not worked for two weeks, and it is dark at night. Write a letter, about 65 words, to the municipal office asking them to repair it.

Dear Sir or Madam,
I am writing to report that the streetlight in our lane has not worked for two weeks. The lane is very dark at night, and it is hard to walk there safely. I request you to send someone to repair the light as soon as possible. Thank you for your attention.
Yours faithfully
A laundry shrank my sweater and offered no apology. Write a polite complaint, about 50 words, to the shop owner.

Dear Sir or Madam,
I gave my sweater to your laundry. When I collected it, it had shrunk and no longer fits me. Nobody apologised for the damage. I would like to talk about this problem calmly. Please contact me so that we can find a fair solution.
Yours sincerely
Write an email, about 50 words, to my course coordinator asking when the certificates for last week's workshop will be sent.

Subject: Workshop certificates

Dear Coordinator,
I attended last week's workshop and enjoyed it very much. I wanted to ask when the certificates will be sent to the participants. Could you please let me know the expected date? Thank you for your help.
Kind regards
Write a short email, about 55 words, to my colleague sharing today's meeting notes and asking her to review them by Thursday.

Subject: Meeting notes for review

Hi,
Please find today's meeting notes attached. Could you read through them and tell me if I have missed anything or written anything wrongly? It would be great if you could review them by Thursday, so that I can send the final version to everyone. Thank you for your help.
Best regards
I need a quotation for 40 chairs for our school function. Write an email, about 60 words, to a furniture vendor asking for the price and delivery time.

Subject: Request for a quotation

Dear Sir or Madam,
We are organising a school function and need 40 chairs. Could you please send me a quotation with the price per chair and the total cost? Please also tell me how soon you can deliver them. Thank you very much.
Yours faithfully
I got into the college I wanted. Write an email, about 80 words, to my old school teacher who always encouraged me, telling her the news and thanking her.

Subject: Good news and thank you

Dear Teacher,
I hope you are well. I am writing to share some happy news: I have got a place in the college I wanted. I still remember how you encouraged me in class and how you always believed in me. Your belief in me made a real difference, and I am truly grateful. I hope to meet you in person soon.
With respect and thanks
Email HR, in about 60 words, to ask whether my training session can be moved to the following week, because I will be travelling for a family function.

Subject: Request to change my training date

Dear HR team,
I am scheduled to attend the training session, but I will be travelling for a family function. Would it be possible to move my session to the following week? I am happy to join any batch that suits you. Please let me know. Thank you for your understanding.
Regards
Notice wanted, about 50 words: the school lost-property box will be emptied on the last Friday of the month, so students should collect their things before then. Sign it School Office.

NOTICE
The lost-property box will be emptied on the last Friday of this month. Students who have lost any item should check the box before that day. Please do not wait until the last day. Anything left in the box after that day will be cleared away.
School Office
Write a notice, about 45 words, for our housing society's annual general meeting on Sunday at 11 am in the clubhouse. All residents should attend. Sign it Secretary, Housing Society.

NOTICE
The annual general meeting of our housing society will be held this Sunday at 11 am in the clubhouse. All residents should attend, so please mark the date. Please be on time. Your presence matters.
Secretary
Housing Society
Make a notice, about 45 words, saying the art room will be closed all week while it is being repainted. Classes will use the library instead. Sign it Art Department.

NOTICE
The art room will remain closed all this week while it is being repainted. Art classes will be held in the library instead. Please do not enter the art room until the painting is finished. Thank you for your understanding.
Art Department
Our grocery co-op needs a notice, about 40 words, reminding members to bring their own cloth bags, because plastic bags will no longer be given. Sign it Management.

NOTICE
From now on, our co-op will no longer give out plastic bags. Members, please bring your own cloth bags whenever you come to shop. Please remember to carry them before you leave home. Thank you for helping us make this change.
Management
Describe an auto rickshaw ride through narrow lanes in a busy old city, about 65 words.

The auto rickshaw rattles into the narrow lane, and the driver honks twice at a boy on a bicycle. Shop signs brush past my shoulder, and the smell of frying samosas drifts in. We slow down for a cow resting in the middle of the road, then squeeze past a vegetable cart. Every turn feels like a small adventure. I hold the bar tightly and smile.
Describe a bowl of hot rasam on a rainy day in about 60 words.

Outside, the rain drums on the roof. Inside, a steel bowl of hot rasam sits in front of me. The red-gold soup is thin and fragrant, with curry leaves floating on top. The first sip is sour, spicy and warm all at once. It clears my nose and warms my fingers. I close my eyes, and for a moment the whole grey day feels cosy.
Describe a school playground right after the last bell rings, about 70 words.

The last bell rings, and the doors burst open. Children pour into the playground like water from a tap. Bags are thrown on the grass, and a ball is already flying. Two girls race to the swing, laughing. A teacher calls out a gentle warning to slow down, but nobody listens. The quiet building behind them seems to sigh with relief. The playground is full of noise again.
Describe a lighthouse at dusk, about 70 words.

At dusk the lighthouse stands tall on the rocks, white against a darkening sky. Waves crash at its feet and the wind smells of salt. Slowly, the great lamp at the top begins to turn, sending a long beam across the water. A small fishing boat glides home along that bright path. The lighthouse does not move. It simply watches and guides, night after night.
Describe the view of green fields from a hot-air balloon in about 75 words.

The balloon rises so gently that I hardly feel it leave the ground. Below me, the fields spread out like a patchwork quilt in every shade of green. A thin river curls through them, shining in the morning sun. Tiny houses sit among the trees, and a farmer looks up and waves. It is very quiet up here, except for the occasional roar of the burner. I feel light and free.
A diary entry, about 65 words, for a girl on the day she learned to whistle after weeks of trying.

Dear Diary,
Today I finally learned to whistle! I have been trying for weeks, and my lips only made a puff of air. This afternoon I stood by the window, rounded my lips gently and blew softly. A clear little note came out! I ran to show my family, and they clapped. I felt so proud. Now I want to learn a whole song. Goodnight!
Please write about 70 words in diary form for a boy who lost his first tooth today and feels both excited and a little scared.

Dear Diary,
My first tooth came out today! It was wobbly for days, and while I was eating an apple, it just fell into my hand. I was a little scared when I saw the gap, but also very excited. Everyone at home said the tooth fairy might visit. I put the tooth under my pillow before bed. I keep poking the gap with my tongue. It feels so funny!
Diary time: about 70 words for a girl who finished reading her first big novel and feels sad that it has ended.

Dear Diary,
I finished my first big novel tonight. It had so many pages that I thought I would never reach the end, but I did. Now I feel strangely sad. I spent so many evenings with the characters, and they felt like friends. I closed the book and held it for a minute. I will start another soon, but this one will always be special. Goodnight, Diary.
I need a diary page, about 70 words, for a young woman the night before her sister's wedding, feeling happy and a little emotional.

Dear Diary,
Tomorrow my sister gets married. The house is full of flowers and relatives, and the smell of sweets is everywhere. Tonight we sat on the terrace and talked, just the two of us, like when we were little. I felt happy for her, but I also felt a small ache, because things will change. She squeezed my hand and said nothing. I will remember this night always.
Write a diary entry, about 65 words, from a boy who tried cooking an omelette for the first time and burnt the first one.

Dear Diary,
Today I made an omelette by myself for the first time. The first one burnt black on the bottom, and the whole kitchen smelled of smoke. I was ready to quit, but then I remembered that everyone burns the first one. I lowered the flame and tried again. The second omelette was golden and soft. I ate it proudly. Next time, I will not forget the salt!
Write a story of about 100 words about a girl, her mango tree and a squirrel who keeps taking the fruit. The ending must be that she learns to share.

Nisha watched her mango tree all summer. When the first fruit turned yellow, a squirrel snatched it and ran. The next day, it took another. Nisha was cross and made a scarecrow, but the squirrel simply sat on its hat. One evening she found the squirrel sitting on a branch, nibbling happily, with its tiny face covered in juice. Nisha laughed. The tree had plenty of fruit. From then on, she picked what she needed and left a few on the lowest branch for her small friend.
Write a story, about 90 words, about a boy whose kite string snaps, and a stranger helps him get the kite back. End with the boy thanking him.

Imran's kite soared high above the rooftops until the string snapped. The kite floated away and caught on a tall tree near the market. Imran stood below, sad and helpless. A stranger carrying a bag of vegetables stopped and looked up. He put down his bag, found a long bamboo pole from a nearby shop and gently lifted the kite from the branches. Imran took it with both hands. "Thank you so much!" he said, grinning. The stranger smiled and went on his way.
Write a gentle story, about 100 words, about a shopkeeper who finds a customer's forgotten umbrella and walks through the rain to return it. End happily.

It rained hard one afternoon, and a woman left her umbrella behind at Mr. Rao's small stationery shop. He noticed it only after she had gone. Mr. Rao looked at the rain, then picked up the umbrella and locked the door. He did not know where she lived, but he remembered she had mentioned the blue house near the temple. He walked there and knocked. The woman opened the door, surprised, and then smiled widely. "You walked all this way for me?" she said. They both laughed and shared tea.
Tell a fable, about 85 words, about a fox who tries to steal a drum, but is surprised by the sound. The fox must learn a lesson at the end.

A hungry fox found a big drum under a tree while the villagers slept. "I will carry it away," he thought, and he tiptoed closer. But his paw hit the drum, and it went BOOM! The fox jumped in fright. Lamps lit up, and the villagers ran out shouting. He dropped the drum and fled into the forest. Panting, he learned that stealing never stays quiet, and that it is better to ask than to take.
Write a short story, about 100 words, about a girl with a magic pencil who draws a bridge so that a line of ants can cross a puddle. Keep it sweet.

Mina found a pencil that glowed softly when she held it. She drew a smiley sun, and warmth filled the room. Then she noticed a line of ants stopped at a big puddle in the yard. They could not cross. Mina knelt down and drew a small bridge from one side to the other. The lines shimmered and became real wood. One by one, the ants marched across, as if saying thank you. Mina smiled and put the pencil away, happy to have helped in such a tiny way.
Write a paragraph of about 70 words on why a regular morning routine helps students start the day well, for a school magazine.

A regular morning routine helps students begin the day calmly. When you wake up, wash and eat at the same time each day, you stop rushing and forgetting things. You have time to pack your bag and enjoy your breakfast. A calm start makes it easier to listen in class and to feel confident. Small habits like these cost nothing, yet they make the whole day easier. Try it for a week and see.
For a school debate, write about 80 words on why walking to school is better than going by car.

Walking to school has many advantages. First, it is good exercise, and it wakes up the body before class. Second, it gives us time to chat with friends or simply enjoy the fresh air. Third, fewer cars mean less smoke and noise near the school gate. Finally, children who walk learn to notice their neighbourhood and its people. A walk of even a few minutes can make the school day start with a smile. That is why walking is the better choice.
Write a paragraph, about 75 words, on why volunteers are important to a community. Make it suitable for a notice board.

Volunteers are the quiet helpers of every community. They clean streets, teach children, help older people and organise events, without asking for payment. When people give a little of their time, big things become possible. Volunteering also brings neighbours together and builds friendships. If you have a free hour, please think about joining us. Every pair of hands matters, and every small effort makes our neighbourhood a kinder, better place for everyone.
Write a four-line rhyme for children about a school bell that rings too early on a sleepy morning.

The school bell rang, ding-dong, so loud,
It woke me from my cosy cloud.
I yawned and stretched, and rubbed my eyes,
Then rushed to class in sleepy surprise.
Write a short poem, four lines, about a train that runs through the night.

The train goes rolling through the night,
Its windows glow with golden light.
The wheels go clickety-clack, clickety-clack,
And rock me softly down the track.
Write a six-line rhyme for kids about an umbrella that wants to go out in the sunshine.

My umbrella sat beside the door
And sighed, "I'm tired of the pour.
Each time I'm used, the sky is grey;
I'd love a bright and sunny day."
So out we went in morning light,
And it twirled happily, shining bright.
My uncle drove us to the airport at 4 in the morning. Could you write a thank-you note to him, about 50 words?

Dear Uncle,
Thank you for driving us to the airport so early this morning. It was still dark, and I know you gave up your sleep for us. It meant so much to us. I am truly grateful for your help and your kindness.
With love
I accidentally broke Grandma's steel tumbler while washing up. Please write a short sorry note, about 50 words, that I can leave on the kitchen table.

Dear Grandma,
I am very sorry that I broke your steel tumbler while washing up. I know it mattered to you. It slipped from my wet hands. Please do not be upset with me. I will wash up more carefully from now on.
Your grandchild
Sana just won our school spelling bee. Write a congratulations message for her, about 45 words.

Dear Sana,
Congratulations on winning the school spelling bee! It is a wonderful achievement, and I am so happy for you. You have worked hard and you deserve this win. I am so proud to call you my classmate. Well done!
Your classmate
Our local tailor altered my sister's wedding blouse overnight when it did not fit. Write a thank-you note to him, about 45 words.

Dear Tailor,
Thank you for altering my sister's wedding blouse overnight. It fits perfectly now, and she is very happy. We will never forget your kindness. The whole family is grateful for your skill and your kindness.
With thanks
Remind my flatmate that the wifi bill has to be paid by the 5th. Keep it friendly and short, about 35 words.

Hi,
Just a friendly reminder that the wifi bill has to be paid by the 5th. Could you please send your share before then? Thanks a lot! Let me know if you need anything from me.
Cheers
The night security guard waited at the gate with an umbrella for me when I came home late in the rain. Help me write a thank-you note to him, about 50 words.

Dear Guard,
Thank you for waiting at the gate with an umbrella when I came home late in the rain. It was a small act, but it made me feel cared for. I am grateful for the way you look after our building every night. Please take care of yourself too.
Regards
I laughed at my friend Sunita's new haircut and she looked hurt. Write a sincere apology message, about 50 words.

Dear Sunita,
I am sorry for laughing at your new haircut. It was rude, and I saw that it hurt you. I did not mean to hurt you, but I should have thought before I spoke. I value our friendship. Please forgive me, and let me make it up to you.
Your friend
My mother has just finished her college degree through evening classes after many years. Write a proud congratulations message for her, about 55 words.

Dear Mother,
Congratulations on finishing your degree! You studied in the evenings after so many years, and you never gave up. You have shown me that it is never too late to learn. I am so proud of you. Let us celebrate together soon. I love you very much.
With love
Our school library wants a short reminder for students, about 40 words, that all borrowed books must be returned before the exams begin.

Dear students,
This is a reminder that all books borrowed from the library must be returned before the exams begin. Please check your bags and shelves at home. Returning books on time helps other students who need them. Thank you for your help.
Librarian
A colleague gave me a small potted plant for my new desk. Write a thank-you message, about 40 words.

Dear colleague,
Thank you for the lovely plant. It brightens up my new desk and makes the space feel like my own. It was a very kind gesture. I promise to water it regularly and keep it healthy!
Best wishes
Please help me invite my family to my graduation ceremony on Saturday at 10 am in the college auditorium. About 45 words.

Dear family,
I am happy to tell you that I will graduate this Saturday at 10 am in the college auditorium. It would mean the world to me if you could all come and share this special day. I look forward to seeing you there.
With love
Invite my colleagues to a Sunday morning trek, starting at 6 am from the office car park. Mention that they should wear sturdy shoes. About 50 words.

Hello team,
Let us start our Sunday with a trek! We will leave from the office car park at 6 am sharp. Please wear sturdy shoes. It will be a fun way to spend time together outside work. Do join us if you can.
Regards
We are hosting an open-mic evening for students in the school hall next Friday at 5 pm. Draft an invitation, about 55 words, for students of all classes.

Open-mic evening for all students!
Do you love to perform? Come and take the stage in the school hall next Friday at 5 pm. Students of all classes are welcome to take part or simply cheer from the audience. It will be a fun and friendly evening, so bring your friends and your best talents. Come and enjoy a happy evening.
A potter in our neighbourhood is holding a clay workshop for children on Sunday at 3 pm. Write an invitation for parents, about 45 words.

Dear Parents,
Your child is invited to a clay workshop this Sunday at 3 pm. A potter from our neighbourhood will help the children enjoy working with clay. It will be a messy and happy afternoon. Please send your child ready to have fun.
Grandparents' Day is on Friday at our school. Write an invitation to our grandparents, about 50 words, inviting them for a morning of songs and tea.

Dear Grandparents,
We warmly invite you to Grandparents' Day at our school on Friday. We will sing songs and serve you tea. It is our chance to say thank you for all your love and care. Please come and spend the morning with us. We cannot wait to see you!
Your grandchildren
I sprained my wrist and cannot play in PT class this week. Write a polite request, about 50 words, to my class teacher asking if I can sit out.

Dear Teacher,
I sprained my wrist and cannot take part in PT class this week. May I please sit out during the period and watch instead? I will join the activities again when my wrist feels better. Thank you for understanding.
Yours sincerely
My suitcase arrived two days after my flight landed. Write a polite complaint to the airline, about 70 words, asking them to explain and to make sure it does not happen again.

Dear Sir or Madam,
My suitcase arrived two days after my flight landed. It caused me a great deal of inconvenience. I would like to understand why this delay happened. Please look into the matter and reply to me with an explanation. I also request you to take steps so that such delays do not happen to other passengers.
Yours faithfully
The shower at our gym has had no hot water for a week. Write a polite complaint, about 55 words, to the gym manager.

Dear Manager,
I am writing about the shower at our gym, which has had no hot water for a week now. This makes it uncomfortable to use. I would be grateful if you could look into this and repair it soon. Thank you for your time.
Yours sincerely
Our library has very few novels for teenagers. Write a polite request to the head librarian, about 50 words, asking if more could be bought.

Dear Librarian,
I enjoy borrowing books from our library, but I have noticed that there are very few novels for teenagers. May I respectfully request you to consider buying some more? It would give us more to choose from. Thank you for considering this.
Yours sincerely
I bought a storybook from a bookshop and it has six pages missing. Please write a polite complaint, about 60 words, asking for a replacement.

Dear Sir or Madam,
I bought a storybook from your shop recently, and when I started reading it, I found that six pages were missing. I was disappointed. Could you please replace the book with a complete copy? I am happy to return the faulty one. Thank you for your help.
Yours faithfully
Write an email to a pen-friend abroad describing my school day, in about 70 words. I start at 8 am, love lunch break and my favourite subject is geography.

Subject: My school day

Dear friend,
I hope you are doing well. I wanted to tell you about my school day. It starts at 8 am. The morning classes go quickly, and I really look forward to lunch break, which I love. My favourite subject is geography. I would love to hear about your school day too, so we can compare. Please write back soon!
Best wishes
I finished the quarterly report a day early. Write a short email to my manager letting her know, in about 50 words, and offering to help with anything else.

Subject: Report completed

Dear Manager,
I am pleased to let you know that the quarterly report is ready and I finished it a day early. I have attached it for your review. If there is anything else you would like me to help with, please tell me.
Regards
I'm a parent, and I'd like an email to a cricket coach asking for the dates of the next trial for under-14 players, in about 55 words. It is for my son.

Subject: Under-14 trial dates

Dear Coach,
I am writing as the parent of a boy who is keen to try out for your under-14 team. Could you please tell me the dates and the time of the next trial? Please also let me know what he should bring. Thank you for your time and guidance.
Yours sincerely
Compose an email to the school office asking for a bonafide certificate, in about 60 words. I am a Class 11 student and need it for a scholarship form.

Subject: Request for a bonafide certificate

Dear Sir or Madam,
I am a student of Class 11 and I need a bonafide certificate to complete a scholarship form. Could you please tell me how I can apply for it and how long it will take? Thank you for your help.
Yours faithfully
We have a leaking pipe in the kitchen. Draft an email to a plumber, around 45 words, asking if he can visit on Saturday morning.

Subject: Request for a visit

Dear Sir,
There is a leaking pipe in our kitchen, and we would like it repaired. Could you please visit on Saturday morning? Kindly let me know if that time suits you and what it will cost. Thank you.
Regards
Announce a parent-teacher meeting on Saturday from 10 am to 1 pm. In a notice of about 45 words, ask parents to meet class teachers in their own classrooms. Sign it Principal.

NOTICE
A parent-teacher meeting will be held this Saturday from 10 am to 1 pm. Parents, please meet the class teachers in their own classrooms. We look forward to a useful discussion about every child's progress. Your presence will make it a success.
Principal
Write a notice, around 40 words, that the bicycle parking area behind our apartment block has moved next to the main gate. Sign it Society Office.

NOTICE
The bicycle parking area behind our apartment block has been moved next to the main gate. Residents, please park your cycles in the new place from now on. Thank you for your understanding.
Society Office
We need a notice for Annual Day rehearsals: every day this week after school in the hall, for all students in the dance group. About 40 words, please. Sign it Cultural Committee.

NOTICE
Rehearsals for Annual Day will be held every day this week after school in the hall. All students in the dance group must attend. Please be punctual and give your best effort.
Cultural Committee
Put a short notice on the school gate saying a set of house keys was found near it and can be claimed at the office. About 35 words. Sign it School Office.

NOTICE
A set of house keys was found near the school gate. If they are yours, please come to the school office to claim them. Please collect them at your earliest convenience.
School Office
Describe my grandmother's old sewing machine as it hums in a corner of the room, about 70 words.

In the corner of the room sits my grandmother's old sewing machine. Its black body is worn smooth from years of use, and its golden letters have faded. When she presses the pedal, it hums and clatters, and the needle dances up and down. Bits of colourful cloth pile up beside it. She has stitched many clothes on this machine, and each one carries a little of her patience.
Describe the school bus at 7 in the morning, in about 60 words.

The yellow school bus rolls up at 7 in the morning, and the doors fold open with a squeak. Sleepy children climb in with heavy bags. Someone is eating a roll, and two friends are whispering a secret. The driver greets everyone with a smile. The seats fill up, the engine hums, and the bus moves on, full of yawns and early chatter.
Write about 55 words describing a sugarcane juice stall on a hot afternoon.

At the corner, a man feeds long sticks of sugarcane into a clanking machine. Golden juice flows into a tall glass, with ice and a squeeze of lime. The queue of thirsty people grows longer under the hot sun. I take a glass and drink it in one go. It is sweet and cool, and the heat melts away.
Describe the view from the top of a mountain after a hard climb, in about 70 words.

My legs ache and my breath is short, but I have finally reached the top. The whole world lies below me, with tiny villages, silver rivers and rows of misty hills. The wind is cold and fresh, and the sky seems very close. I sit on a rock and drink some water. All the tiredness is gone, replaced by a wide, happy feeling that I cannot put into words.
Describe a fruit seller's cart at midday in the market, about 60 words.

The fruit seller's cart is a rainbow on wheels. Red apples are stacked in neat pyramids, and bananas hang like yellow bunting. Oranges, guavas and grapes crowd together, and the smell of ripe mangoes drifts across the lane. The seller calls out his prices in a singsong voice. A woman presses a papaya gently, smiles and says she will take two.
I'd like about 70 words of diary writing from a girl after her school's Annual Day dance, when she forgot a step but kept going.

Dear Diary,
Tonight was our Annual Day dance. My heart was thumping as the curtain rose. In the middle, I forgot a step and my mind went blank. But I kept smiling and followed the girl next to me. Nobody noticed, and the audience clapped loudly at the end. Everyone said I was brave. I felt so relieved and proud!
Diary entry for a boy on the day his family brought home a puppy, about 70 words.

Dear Diary,
We brought a puppy home today! He is small and brown, with big floppy ears. At first he hid under the sofa, but soon he came out to sniff my shoes. He chewed my slipper and then fell asleep in my lap. I felt so happy that my chest almost hurt. I think we will be best friends. I must think of a good name for him.
Give me a diary page of about 70 words about a day in my grandparents' village, where I ate fresh guavas and chased chickens.

Dear Diary,
Today I spent the whole day in my grandparents' village. I climbed the guava tree and ate the fresh fruit, with its sweet pink insides. Then I chased the chickens around the yard until they scattered, squawking. My grandmother laughed and told me to stop. In the evening, we sat outside and watched the stars. The city seems so far away. I wish I could stay longer.
Pretend you're a ten-year-old who fell off a bicycle today. Write the diary entry, about 65 words, showing that the child was brave and tried again.

Dear Diary,
Today I fell off my bicycle and scraped my knee. It stung, and I almost cried. For a moment I wanted to put the bicycle away and never ride it again. But I told myself I could try again, and I did. I wobbled, but this time I stayed on. My knee still hurts, but I feel brave. Tomorrow I will ride farther.
A girl helped a lost child find his parents at a village fair. Write her diary entry for that evening, about 70 words.

Dear Diary,
Today at the village fair, I saw a little boy standing alone and crying. I asked him his name and held his hand. We walked around the fair and I asked people if they knew his parents. After a while, a worried woman ran towards us and hugged him tightly. She thanked me again and again. I felt happy that I had helped. I hope he is safe tonight.
Tell a story of about 90 words about a girl who loses a glove in the snow. It must end with a hedgehog using it as a bed.

Asha ran across the snowy field, laughing, until she noticed that one of her red gloves was gone. She looked behind every tree and under every bush, but found nothing. Sadly, she went home with one cold hand. Weeks later, when the snow melted, she walked the same path and saw something red under a hedge. The glove was lying there, and inside it a small hedgehog was curled up, fast asleep. Asha smiled and left it as a bed.
Write a story of about 85 words about a boy who builds a robot from junk. At the end, the robot must help him water the garden.

Tarun collected old tins, wires and bottle caps from the junk shop. For weeks he worked in the garage, twisting wires and fixing bolts. Finally, a small robot stood on its square legs. It had two bottle-cap eyes and a funnel for a mouth. Tarun pressed a button, and the robot let out a whirr. It rolled forward on its wheels. The next morning, Tarun handed it a small watering can. The robot gently watered each plant in the garden, row by row, while he watched proudly.
I'd like a story, about 90 words, about a baker who notices a hungry cat outside his shop every night. End with them becoming friends.

Every night, when the baker locked up his shop, he saw a thin cat watching from the corner. At first he chased it away. But one cold evening the cat looked so hungry that the baker felt ashamed. He took a small piece of leftover bread and a saucer of milk and put them by the door. The cat ate slowly and looked up at him. The next evening, it was waiting. Soon it was sleeping beside the warm oven each night, purring contentedly.
Please write a story, about 100 words, about two neighbours who built a wall between their houses and then made a little door in it.

Two neighbours quarrelled over a mango tree, and one of them built a high wall between their houses. For months they did not speak. One day a ball from one garden flew over the wall and landed in the other. The boy next door knocked on the wall, calling for his ball. Nobody answered. His father felt sorry and took a small hammer. By evening there was a little wooden door in the wall. The other neighbour came through it with the ball and a mango. They both laughed, and shared the fruit.
Make up a story, about 80 words, about a smooth grey stone in a stream that dreams of seeing the sea, and a river that finally carries it there.

A smooth grey stone lay in a stream and listened to the water. "Where do you go?" it asked. "To the sea," said the water. The stone sighed. "I wish I could see it." Each day the stream flowed, and each day the stone slipped a little farther. After many seasons, a big monsoon flood lifted the stone and carried it all the way down the river. At last it rolled onto soft sand and heard the great waves. "It is wonderful!" it said.
Write a paragraph for a school newsletter about 70 words long on why we should save water every day, with easy tips like closing the tap while brushing.

Water is precious, and saving it begins with small daily habits. Close the tap while you brush your teeth. Take shorter showers, and use a bucket for washing the bicycle. Fix any dripping tap at home as soon as you can. If we all do these little things, we save thousands of litres in a year. Tomorrow's children will thank us for taking care of water today.
Why does teamwork matter in sport? Write a paragraph for my school magazine, about 75 words.

Teamwork matters in sport because no player can win alone. In a team, each person has a job, and the game goes well only when everyone does it. Players learn to trust one another, pass the ball and support a friend who has made a mistake. A team that works together can beat a team of stars. Teamwork also teaches us to share joy in winning and lessons in losing.
Write 65 words in a paragraph about why neat handwriting still matters, for a class essay.

Neat handwriting still matters, even in a time of keyboards. When writing is clear, others can read it easily, and mistakes are fewer. Taking time to form each letter well also helps us slow down and think. Teachers can mark neat work faster, and notes are easier to revise later. Good handwriting is a small gift to your future self. A little practice each day can improve it.
Write a four-line rhyme for children about a bus that is always late.

The bus is late, the bus is late,
We stand and wait beside the gate.
It finally comes, with a honk and a sigh,
And off we go, as the clouds float by.
Four lines of poetry, please, about the stars coming out one by one at night.

The sun slips down behind the hill,
The world grows quiet, calm and still.
One tiny star, then two, then three,
Are shining bright for you and me.
Write a six-line poem for kids about a pair of red rain boots that love puddles.

My little boots are bright and red,
They splash through puddles, so I said,
"Let's jump in every pool we see,
As deep and wide as it can be!"
My boots cheer loudly, splish and splash,
And off we go in a happy dash.
My grandmother stitched the broken strap of my school bag by hand. Please help me write a thank-you note to her, about 50 words.

Dear Grandmother,
Thank you for stitching the broken strap of my school bag by hand. It looks strong again, and it means so much to me that you did it yourself. You saved me from needing a new bag, and I will carry it with pride. I love you very much.
Your grandchild
I used my roommate's phone charger without asking and left it at college. Write a short, sincere sorry message to her, about 50 words.

Hi,
I am sorry that I took your phone charger without asking, and I am even sorrier that I left it at college. I should have asked first. I will bring it back as soon as I can. Please tell me if there is anything else I can do to make up for it.
Your roommate
My friend Dev just got his first job. Write him a happy congratulations message, about 45 words.

Dear Dev,
Congratulations on your first job! You deserve this, and I am delighted for you. I am sure you will do very well. Let us celebrate soon, and the first round is on you! Well done, my friend.
Cheers
Our teammate twisted his knee during practice. Write a get-well message from the team, about 45 words, without any advice about treatment.

Hi teammate,
We were sorry to see you hurt at practice, and we miss you on the field already. Take all the time you need to rest. We are thinking of you and looking forward to seeing you back. Get well soon!
The team
Write a reminder note, about 40 words, for my father, whom I call Papa, to take his spectacles and train ticket when he leaves for the railway station tomorrow.

Dear Papa,
A small reminder for tomorrow: please take your spectacles and your train ticket before you leave for the railway station. Have a safe and pleasant journey, and call us when you reach.
With love
An electrician came to fix our wiring on a public holiday. Write a thank-you note to him, about 45 words.

Dear Sir,
Thank you for coming to fix our wiring on a public holiday. You gave up your day off, and we are very grateful. Our wiring is working properly again, and we feel safe. Your quick, careful work made a big difference to us.
Regards
We played loud music at my party last night and probably kept the neighbours awake. Write a sorry note to them, about 55 words.

Dear Neighbours,
We are sorry for the loud music at our party last night. We realise it must have kept you awake, and we should have kept the volume lower. Thank you for being patient with us. We will be more careful next time. Please let us know if anything like this bothers you again.
Warm regards
Our school choir won the inter-school competition. Write a congratulations message from the principal to the choir, about 40 words.

Dear choir members,
Congratulations on winning the inter-school competition! You have made the whole school proud. Your hard work and your beautiful singing have brought us this great victory. Enjoy this win, and keep singing.
Principal
Remind all parents in my class that the winter uniform starts from Monday. Keep it polite and about 35 words.

Dear Parents,
This is a gentle reminder that the winter uniform will be worn from Monday. Kindly make sure your child comes to school in the full winter uniform. Thank you for your help.
Class Teacher
I stayed with a host family for a week during a student exchange. Write them a thank-you note, about 60 words.

Dear host family,
Thank you for welcoming me into your home for a whole week. I felt like one of the family from the very first day. I will always remember your kindness and how well you looked after me. I hope you can visit me one day, and I can host you. Thank you again for everything.
Gratefully
My mother is retiring after many years of teaching. Write an invitation to a small tea party at our home in her honour, on Sunday at 4 pm. About 50 words.

Dear friends,
After many years of teaching, my mother is retiring, and we would like to honour her with a small tea party at our home. Please join us this Sunday at 4 pm. Your presence will make her feel very special. Come and share your memories and a cup of tea with her.
Warm regards
I help at the neighbourhood library. Write an invitation, about 40 words, for a children's storytelling hour on Saturday at 11 am.

Calling all young readers!
Our neighbourhood library invites you to a children's storytelling hour this Saturday at 11 am. Come and listen to wonderful stories, and bring a friend along. It will be a happy morning for everyone.
Invite my friends to a stargazing night on our rooftop this Friday after dinner. About 45 words, and tell them to bring a blanket.

Hello friends,
Come and watch the stars with me on our rooftop this Friday after dinner! Please bring a blanket to sit on. It will be a magical night of stargazing, so come with your sense of wonder. See you there!
Our class is holding a bake sale at school next Wednesday to raise money for the library. Write an invitation, about 50 words, to the whole school.

Come to our bake sale!
Our class invites everyone to a bake sale at school next Wednesday. We have plenty of tasty homemade treats. All the money we raise will go to the library. Please come with your friends and a good appetite. Every bite helps a reader!
My desk chair at the office is broken and hurts my back. Write a polite request to the office administrator, about 55 words, asking for a replacement.

Dear Sir or Madam,
The chair at my desk is broken and hurts my back. I request you to kindly arrange a replacement chair for me. I would be very grateful for your help. Please let me know if you need to see the chair. Thank you for your time.
Regards
A tuition centre changed my son's class timing without telling us, and he missed the lesson. Write a polite complaint to the centre, about 50 words.

Dear Sir or Madam,
The timing of my son's class was changed, but nobody informed us, so he missed the lesson. This is upsetting. I understand that schedules can change, but I request you to send a message to parents when it does. Thank you for your understanding.
Yours sincerely
Garbage keeps getting left on the stairs of our apartment block. Write a polite complaint to the apartment manager, about 55 words, asking him to take action.

Dear Manager,
I am writing to bring a problem to your notice. Garbage bags are often left on the stairs of our building. Could you please remind residents to use the bins and take action so that the stairs stay clean? It makes the building unpleasant for everyone. Thank you for your attention.
Yours sincerely
My maths teacher added my marks wrongly on the answer sheet. Write a polite request, about 50 words, asking him to check the total.

Dear Sir,
I have looked carefully at my maths answer sheet, and I think the marks may have been added wrongly. May I request you to please check the total again? I am sorry to trouble you. Thank you very much for your time and help.
Yours sincerely
Our travel agent promised a room with a sea view, but we got a room facing a car park. Write a polite complaint, about 55 words, asking for a refund of the difference.

Dear Sir or Madam,
You promised us a room with a sea view for our holiday, but the room we were given faced the car park. We were disappointed. I request you to look into the matter and refund the difference in the price. I look forward to your reply.
Yours sincerely
I'm a teacher. Compose an email to a museum asking about visiting hours and group rates for a school group, in about 60 words.

Subject: Visit by a school group

Dear Sir or Madam,
I am a teacher and would like to bring a group of students to your museum. Could you please tell me your visiting hours and whether there are special rates for school groups? We would also appreciate it if you could say how to book a guided tour. Thank you.
Yours faithfully
Please draft an email asking a colleague to cover a meeting for me on Tuesday afternoon because I have to visit a bank, in about 55 words.

Subject: Can you cover Tuesday's meeting?

Hi,
I have to visit the bank on Tuesday afternoon and cannot attend the meeting. Would you be able to cover it for me? I can send you the agenda and my notes beforehand. I would be happy to return the favour. Thank you so much.
Best regards
I have to quit the school hockey team until my exams are over. Write an email to the coach, about 70 words, that is respectful and says I hope to rejoin.

Subject: Leaving the team for now

Dear Coach,
I am writing to say that I must take a break from the hockey team until my exams are over. I have enjoyed every practice, and I am sorry to leave. I need to give my studies full attention at this time. I hope I can rejoin the team afterwards. Thank you for all your guidance.
Yours sincerely
We want our school sports day to have a chief guest. Write an invitation email, about 70 words, from the principal to a retired athlete who is not named.

Subject: Invitation to our sports day

Dear Sir or Madam,
On behalf of our school, I would like to invite you to be the chief guest at our annual sports day. Your achievements in sport inspire our students greatly. We would be honoured if you could join us as our chief guest and share a few words with the students. Your presence would mean a lot. Please let me know if you can accept.
Yours sincerely
Principal
The community swimming pool will be shut next Monday for cleaning. Make a notice of about 40 words for the notice board. Sign it Pool Management.

NOTICE
The community swimming pool will remain closed next Monday for cleaning. It will reopen once the cleaning is done. Please plan your swimming accordingly. We regret any inconvenience this may cause, and thank you for your understanding.
Pool Management
Please create a notice, about 50 words, saying that second-hand school uniforms will be sold at low prices in the school hall on Friday after class. Sign it School Office.

NOTICE
Second-hand school uniforms will be sold at low prices in the school hall on Friday after class. Parents who wish to buy a uniform for their child are welcome to visit. Please come and take a look, and spread the word to other families. Thank you.
School Office
Draft a notice, around 45 words, saying that the water tank on our building's roof will be cleaned on Sunday and the water may be muddy that evening. Sign it Society Management.

NOTICE
The water tank on the roof of our building will be cleaned this Sunday. The water may look muddy that evening, so please use it with care. We apologise for the inconvenience and thank you for your patience.
Society Management
Write a notice, about 35 words, reminding residents that the terrace is closed after 9 pm for the sake of those who are sleeping. Sign it Society Office.

NOTICE
Residents are reminded that the terrace is closed after 9 pm, so that those who are sleeping are not disturbed. Please keep to this rule. Thank you for being considerate.
Society Office
Describe a tailor's shop in a busy market in about 80 words.

The tailor's shop is small and crowded. Rolls of colourful cloth lean against the walls, and a tape measure hangs around the tailor's neck. His sewing machine whirs steadily as he guides a bright green fabric through it. Customers wait on a wooden bench, flipping through old fashion pictures. Threads and buttons lie scattered on the floor, and the air smells of fresh cotton. Every few minutes the tailor looks up, smiles and says, "Almost ready."
Describe a school corridor during exams, in about 60 words.

The corridor is quiet during the exams. The usual shouting and running have stopped. Behind each classroom door, pens scratch on paper. A teacher walks slowly with soft footsteps, and a fan creaks overhead. Outside, a nervous student waits for a late friend, whispering the last answers to himself. The silence feels heavy and full of thinking, until the bell finally rings.
Describe a courtyard in an old house with a tulsi plant in the middle, about 60 words.

In the middle of the courtyard stands a tulsi plant on a small stone platform. Its leaves are green and sweet-smelling, and a little lamp sits at its base. Morning light slants through the open sky above. Pigeons walk along the edge of the roof, and the floor is cool under bare feet. The whole house feels peaceful here.
Describe the sunrise over paddy fields in the countryside, in about 60 words.

The sky turns pink and gold over the paddy fields. Mist rests on the green rows, and drops of dew shine on every blade. A farmer walks along the narrow mud path with a tool over his shoulder, and a white egret lifts off from the water. The air is cool and smells of wet earth. The day begins slowly and gently.
Describe sitting around a campfire at night with friends, about 75 words.

The campfire crackles and sparks fly up into the dark. We sit in a circle with our faces glowing orange, and our shadows dance on the grass. Someone roasts corn on a stick, and the smell makes everyone hungry. Another friend tells a ghost story in a low voice. We laugh and shiver together. Above us, the sky is full of stars, and the night feels warm.
A diary page of about 60 words by a student who has just got her exam results and is relieved and happy.

Dear Diary,
Today the results came out. My hands were shaking as I opened the paper, and then I saw my marks. I had passed well! I felt so relieved that I almost cried. I could not wait to tell everyone. I was so afraid for nothing. Tonight I will sleep peacefully, without a single worry.
About 65 words in diary form, please, from a teenage girl who babysat her baby cousin for the first time and found it harder than she expected.

Dear Diary,
Today I looked after my baby cousin for the first time. I thought it would be easy, but it was not! He cried when he was left with me, and I did not know what to do. I sang songs, made faces and walked around the room with him. Finally, he fell asleep on my shoulder. I was so tired, but happy. Babysitting is real work!
My grandfather taught me chess today. Write a diary entry in my voice, about 70 words, that shows I lost but enjoyed it.

Dear Diary,
Today my grandfather taught me chess. He placed the board between us and explained how each piece moves. We played a game, and I lost very quickly. He did not mind, and he smiled kindly when I made a silly move. Even though I lost, I enjoyed it very much. I asked him for another game tomorrow, and he said yes. I think I will love this game.
A boy joined the school choir today and felt shy at first. Write his diary entry, about 80 words.

Dear Diary,
Today I joined the school choir. At first I felt shy and stood at the back, hoping nobody would notice me. When the teacher played the first note, everyone began to sing, and I quietly joined in. Slowly I forgot to be nervous. By the end, I was standing with the others and singing loudly. It felt good to be part of a group. I will go again next week.
Write about 70 words in diary style for a child who saw the sea for the very first time on a family trip.

Dear Diary,
Today I saw the sea for the first time! It was much bigger than I had imagined. The waves rolled in and out, and the water was so blue. I took off my shoes and let the foam tickle my toes. A family member held my hand when a big wave came. I picked up shells and put them in my pocket. I never want to leave.
Here's an idea: a story of about 100 words about a scarecrow who is lonely in a field until a little girl begins to talk to him each day. It must end with her bringing him a new hat.

A scarecrow stood alone in a wheat field. Birds sat on his arms and laughed at him. He felt very lonely. One morning a little girl walked by and said, "Good morning!" She came every day after that, telling him about her school and her friends. The scarecrow could not answer, but he listened happily. When winter came, his old hat was torn and the wind blew it away. The next day the girl came running with a bright new hat. "This is for you," she said, and smiled.
I'd like a story of about 90 words about a boy who is always losing his pencil. One day he finds a tiny door in the desk. End with him finding his lost pencils inside.

Ravi lost a pencil every single day. His teacher sighed, and his pencil box was always empty. One morning, Ravi noticed a tiny door in the corner of his desk. He knocked softly, and it creaked open. Inside was a small room, and in it were all his missing pencils, stacked like firewood. A tiny voice said, "Please be more careful!" Ravi laughed and took them back. After that, he kept his pencil in his bag, and he never lost another one.
Tell a story, about 85 words, about a bus driver who waits for an old lady running towards the bus stop, even though he is late. End with her giving him a sweet.

The bus driver glanced at his watch. He was already late, and the passengers were restless. Then he saw an old lady hurrying towards the bus stop, holding her bag and a stick. She waved, out of breath. The driver sighed, then smiled and stopped the bus. She climbed in slowly, and the passengers made room for her. "Thank you, son," she said, and fished a sweet out of her bag. The driver took it with a grin. The day seemed a little brighter after that.
Give me a short story, about 90 words, that begins with a clock running backwards. Give it a gentle twist ending: it turns out he was looking at its reflection in a mirror.

One morning, Kavi noticed the big clock in the hall was running backwards. The hands turned slowly the wrong way. "Is time going back?" he wondered. He ran to tell his family, who laughed and said, "Look again." Kavi stared at the clock, then turned his head. He had been looking at a mirror. The clock in it was only a reflection. The real clock, on the wall behind him, was ticking normally. Kavi felt a little silly, and then laughed with his family.
Write a story, about 100 words, about a village lantern festival where a small boy's lantern keeps going out, but a girl helps him. It should end with both lanterns floating up together.

At the village lantern festival, everyone carried a glowing lantern to the river. Little Ashok held his own, but a breeze blew it out again and again. He felt sad as the other lanterns floated away. A girl standing nearby saw him and came over. "Let me help," she said. She cupped her hands around his lantern and lit it again with her own. Together they walked to the water and set both lanterns on the river. They floated up in the warm night, side by side, and Ashok smiled.
For a school newsletter, about 70 words on why reading the newspaper is good for older students.

Reading a newspaper helps older students understand the world around them. It tells us what is happening in our city, our country and far-off places. It also builds our vocabulary and helps us form our own opinions. Even ten minutes a day makes a difference. You might discover a sport, a hobby or a problem you want to help solve. Start with one page that interests you, and then read more.
Why do cities need trees? Write a paragraph of about 80 words for a class essay.

Cities need trees because they make life better for everyone. Trees give shade, and they keep the streets cooler on hot days. They give homes to birds and small animals. Their leaves clean the air a little and make the streets look beautiful. A walk under trees is calmer than a walk on a bare road. When cities plan new roads and buildings, they should save the trees and plant many more.
Why does saying sorry take courage? Write about 70 words for teenagers.

Saying sorry is harder than it sounds. It means admitting that you made a mistake, and that can feel uncomfortable. You may worry that the other person will be angry or that you will look weak. But an honest apology shows strength. It tells people that you care about them more than your pride. It can mend a friendship and make you feel lighter. Be brave and say it.
Give me four lines of verse about waves on the shore.

The waves roll in, then roll away,
They write on sand and wash the day.
The shells are left in a silver line,
And the sea sings softly, calm and fine.
Write a six-line rhyme for children about a tiffin box that holds a surprise.

My tiffin box is shiny and round,
It rattles with a lovely sound.
At lunch I lift the lid up high,
And see a treat that makes me sigh.
A yummy paratha, warm and neat,
A packed surprise that tastes so sweet.
Write a gentle four-line lullaby for a sleepy puppy.

Close your eyes, my little pup,
The day is done, the moon is up.
Dream of bones and meadows wide,
Safe and warm right by my side.
My cousin has her classical dance exam tomorrow. Write a good-luck message for her, about 45 words.

Dear cousin,
Good luck for your dance exam tomorrow! You have practised hard, and I am sure it will show. Just breathe, smile and enjoy it. I am cheering for you, and I know you will shine on that stage.
With love
Our food took more than an hour to arrive at a restaurant, and nobody explained why. Write a polite complaint to the manager, about 55 words.

Dear Manager,
We visited your restaurant, and our food took more than an hour to arrive. Nobody explained the reason or offered an apology. A wait this long was very frustrating for us. I hope you will look into it and improve your service. Thank you for your attention.
Yours sincerely
Our coach gave us extra practice sessions on weekends for the whole month. Write a thank-you note from me to him, about 45 words.

Dear Coach,
Thank you for the extra practice sessions on weekends this month. You gave up your free time for me, and I have learnt a great deal from you. Your patience and encouragement mean a lot to me. I am very grateful.
Your player
I submitted my homework two days late because of a family function. Write a polite sorry note to my teacher, about 45 words.

Dear Teacher,
I am sorry that I submitted my homework two days late. I had a family function, and I could not find the time. I should have told you earlier. It will not happen again. Thank you for your understanding.
Yours sincerely
My sister-in-law Pallavi has just opened a small bakery. Write her a warm congratulations message, about 40 words.

Dear Pallavi,
Congratulations on opening your bakery! What a wonderful new adventure this is, and I am so proud of you. I wish you great success and many happy customers. Best of luck for everything ahead.
With love
My friend Joel has a fever and cannot join our school trip. Write a cheerful get-well message, about 45 words.

Dear Joel,
I am sorry you cannot come on the trip. It will not be the same without you! Please rest and get well soon. I will tell you every funny thing that happens when I get back. See you soon!
Your friend
Write a reminder to my team that our Wednesday potluck lunch is on, and everyone should bring one dish. About 40 words, in a cheerful tone.

Hi team,
A cheerful reminder that our potluck lunch is on Wednesday! Please bring one dish to share. It can be anything you like, sweet or savoury. Let us enjoy good food together and a little break from work. See you there!
Cheers
Please write a short thank-you note, about 50 words, to the cleaning staff at our school for keeping the classrooms spotless all year.

Dear cleaning staff,
Thank you for keeping our classrooms so clean all year. Your hard work often goes unnoticed, but it makes our school a pleasant place to learn. We appreciate everything you do. We promise to keep our desks and floors tidy too.
From the students
I promised to take my little sister to the park on Sunday but did not, because I was busy with homework. Write a sorry note to her, about 45 words. I'm her brother.

Dear sister,
I am sorry that I did not take you to the park on Sunday. I know you were waiting, and I broke my promise. I had homework, but I should have told you earlier. Let us go to the park together very soon.
Your brother
Class 5 performed a play at the school assembly today. Write a congratulations message from their teacher, about 55 words.

Dear Class 5,
Congratulations on your wonderful play at the assembly today! You performed so well, and I am sure everyone enjoyed it. Your hard work and teamwork showed. I am very proud of each one of you. Well done, and thank you for your effort.
Your teacher
Remind my roommate to lock the door when she leaves for work and take the spare key. Short and polite, about 35 words.

Hi,
A quick reminder: please remember to lock the door when you leave for work, and take the spare key with you. It would be a great help to me. Thank you so much!
Your roommate
My friend's father drove me home late at night when the buses had stopped. Write a thank-you message to him, about 45 words.

Dear Sir,
Thank you for driving me home late at night when the buses had stopped. It was late, and I was worried about how I would get home. I am thankful for your kindness and for making sure I reached safely. Please accept my sincere thanks.
Regards
Help me write a farewell party invitation, about 50 words, for my classmate who is moving abroad. The party will be on Friday at lunch break, in the school garden.

Dear friends,
Our classmate is moving abroad, and we want to give them a farewell they will never forget! Please join us on Friday at the lunch break in the school garden. Come and say goodbye with smiles, and wish them the very best for their new life.
From your classmates
A new colleague joined our team this week. Write an invitation, about 45 words, to a welcome tea in the pantry on Thursday at 4 pm.

Dear team,
Please join us for a welcome tea this Thursday at 4 pm in the pantry. Our new colleague has just joined us, and we would like to say hello over tea. Come along and make our newest team member feel at home.
Our school is holding a drawing competition for Children's Day. Write a notice-style invitation, about 50 words, for students of Classes 3 to 5. Sign it Art Department.

Drawing Competition for Children's Day!
Students of Classes 3 to 5 are invited to take part in a drawing competition to celebrate Children's Day. Come and show us your imagination, and let your colours do the talking. Every child is welcome to join the fun. We look forward to your wonderful drawings.
Art Department
I'd love to invite my friends to a cycling ride on Sunday morning that starts at the park gate at 6 am and ends with breakfast. Write it in about 55 words.

Hi friends,
Let us go for a cycling ride this Sunday morning! We will meet at the park gate at 6 am and ride together. When we are done, we will stop for a hearty breakfast. Please bring your cycle. It will be great fun. Hope you can come!
My cousin is getting married and the mehndi evening is on Thursday at 6 pm at our house. Write an invitation to the girls in the family, about 50 words.

Dear girls,
Our cousin's wedding is near, and we are holding a mehndi evening at our house this Thursday at 6 pm. Come and join us for an evening of mehndi and fun. It would not be a celebration without all of you! We cannot wait to see you there.
With love
We ordered a birthday cake for my daughter and it arrived stale. Write a polite complaint to the bakery, about 45 words, and ask for a replacement or refund.

Dear Sir or Madam,
We ordered a cake from your bakery for my daughter's birthday. It arrived stale, and we were very disappointed. I request you to either replace the cake or give us a refund. Thank you for your attention.
Yours faithfully
The branches of my neighbour's tree are blocking the light into my window. Write a friendly request, about 55 words, asking him to trim them.

Dear Neighbour,
I hope you are well. I wanted to mention that the branches of your tree have grown across my window and are blocking much of the light. Would you be willing to trim them when you have a moment? I would be very grateful. Please let me know if I can help in any way.
Warm regards
I'm a student who wants to use the school computer lab for an hour after class on weekdays. Write a polite request to the principal, about 60 words.

Dear Principal,
I am a student of this school, and I would like to request permission to use the computer lab for an hour after class on weekdays. I believe this time would help me learn and practise. May I kindly request your permission? I would be very grateful for your help. Thank you for your consideration.
Yours sincerely
A taxi driver took a very long route and charged me far more than I expected. Write a polite complaint, about 60 words, to the taxi company.

Dear Sir or Madam,
I took a taxi from your company, and the driver took a very long route to my destination. As a result, the fare was far more than I had expected. I would like to request you to look into this and explain how the fare was calculated. I look forward to your response.
Yours faithfully
A mechanic repaired my bicycle but the brakes still do not work well. Write a polite complaint, about 50 words, asking him to fix it properly.

Dear Sir,
I gave my bicycle to your shop for repair, but the brakes still do not work well. This makes it unsafe to ride. I request you to please check them again and fix them properly. I am happy to bring the bicycle back whenever it suits you. Thank you.
Yours sincerely
Draft an email to my professor asking for a short appointment next week to discuss my project topic, in about 55 words.

Subject: Request for an appointment

Dear Professor,
I would like to discuss my project topic with you and would be grateful for a short appointment next week. Please tell me which day and time suit you best, and I will arrange my schedule accordingly. Thank you for your time and guidance.
Yours sincerely
Tell everyone in the office, by email, that from Monday, lunch will start at 1 pm instead of 12.30 pm. Keep it to about 40 words.

Subject: New lunch timing

Dear all,
Please note that from Monday, lunch will start at 1 pm instead of 12.30 pm. Kindly plan your day accordingly. If this causes any problem, please let me know. Thank you for your understanding.
Regards
There is a broken footpath near our market where people keep tripping. Write a letter to the editor of a local newspaper, about 55 words, asking the authorities to repair it.

To the Editor,
I am writing about the broken footpath near our local market, where people keep tripping. It is dangerous for everyone who walks there. I request the authorities to repair the footpath soon, before somebody gets hurt. I hope that, with your help, this issue will get the attention it needs.
Yours faithfully
Write a friendly email to my class group asking everyone to send me their photos from last week's trip, about 50 words, by Sunday evening.

Subject: Photos from the trip

Hi everyone,
I hope you all enjoyed last week's trip as much as I did! Could you please send me the photos you took? I would love to collect them all in one place. Please send them by Sunday evening. Thank you!
Cheers

A blood donation camp will be held in the clubhouse this Sunday from 9 am to 1 pm. Healthy adult residents are warmly invited to take part. Your donation can help a person in need. Thank you for your generosity.
Society Committee
