NOTICE
Registrations for the inter-house quiz are open until Friday. Students who wish to take part should give their names to their house captain. Please do not wait until the last day. Prepare well and enjoy the quiz.
Quiz Committee
The school canteen is adding a new snack menu from Monday. Write a short notice, about 35 words, for the board. Sign it Canteen Management.

NOTICE
From Monday, the school canteen will offer a new snack menu. Students are welcome to try the new items during the break. We hope you enjoy them, so do give them a try!
Canteen Management
School library notice, please: it will be closed on Thursday for stocktaking and will reopen on Friday. About 35 words. Sign it Librarian.

NOTICE
The school library will be closed on Thursday for stocktaking. It will reopen on Friday. Please plan your visits accordingly. We apologise for the inconvenience. Thank you for your understanding.
Librarian
Describe a tea garden on a misty hillside in about 70 words.

The tea garden rolls down the hillside in neat green rows. Mist drifts between the bushes, and the air is cool and damp. Women in bright clothes move along the rows, picking the top leaves with quick fingers and dropping them into baskets on their backs. A thin path winds between the bushes. Everything smells of fresh leaves, and the whole hill seems to be breathing softly.
Describe a pond full of lotus flowers early in the morning, in about 60 words.

Pink lotus flowers rest on a still green pond. Large round leaves float like plates, and drops of water roll across them like silver beads. A dragonfly lands on a bud and takes off again. A faint ripple spreads across the water where a fish has risen. The early light is soft, and the pond looks like a quiet, secret garden.
Write a description of an ancient banyan tree in a village square in about 80 words.

The old banyan tree stands in the middle of the village square. Its thick branches spread wide, and long roots hang down like ropes. Beneath it is a stone platform where elders sit and talk, and children play hide and seek around the trunk. Birds nest in its leaves, and a cool shade covers everyone below. It has seen many generations come and go, and it still stands quietly, as if listening to every story.
How would you describe a school assembly on a cold morning? Give me about 70 words.

On a cold winter morning, the children gather in neat rows on the ground. Their breath makes small clouds in the air, and many have woollen caps pulled down over their ears. The teacher at the microphone leads the prayer, and the children's voices rise together. A few shiver and stamp their feet. When the national anthem finishes, they rush to class, glad to be warm again.
Describe the sound of rain on a tin roof in about 55 words.

The first raindrops land on the tin roof with soft taps. Soon the taps become a rapid drumbeat, and the whole roof seems to sing. Inside, the sound fills the room and makes every other noise disappear. It is a loud, steady, friendly music that makes me feel snug and sleepy. I pull my blanket up and listen.
My sister and I adopted two kittens today. Write my diary entry, about 65 words, with some of our funny first moments.

Dear Diary,
Today we brought home two kittens! One is grey and the other is ginger. At first they hid under the bed, and we had to coax them out with a saucer of milk. Then the ginger one chased my shoelace around the room, and the grey one climbed onto my sister's head. We laughed so much. I think this house will never be quiet again!
Summer holidays begin today. Write a diary entry, about 70 words, from a child on this first day, who is unsure how to fill the days.

Dear Diary,
Today was the first day of the summer holidays. I woke up late and ate a long breakfast, and then I did not know what to do. No school bag, no bell, no homework. It felt strange and wonderful. I made a list of things to try, like painting, reading and flying a kite. Let us see how many I can do!
Today I did a magic trick for my family and it worked. Give me about 60 words of diary writing about it, in the voice of a ten-year-old.

Dear Diary,
Today I performed my first magic trick in front of my whole family! I made a coin disappear and then found it behind someone's ear. Everyone gasped, and someone asked me to do it again. I was so nervous that my hands shook, but the trick worked. I felt like a real magician. I will practise some more.
Here is a diary entry I need, about 65 words, from a girl who cleaned out her cupboard and found her favourite old toy.

Dear Diary,
Today I cleaned my cupboard, and I found my old stuffed rabbit at the very back. His ear was a bit torn, but he looked just the same. I remember carrying him everywhere when I was little. I sat on the floor and hugged him for a long time. I will not give him away. I put him on my bed.
A boy won second prize in a drawing competition at school today. Write his diary entry, about 60 words, showing he is proud but wishes he had won first.

Dear Diary,
Today I won second prize in the school drawing competition! My teacher shook my hand, and my friends clapped. I felt proud, but a tiny part of me wished it was first prize. When I saw the winning drawing, I understood why it won. It was really lovely. Next year I will work even harder and try again.
Tell a story of about 80 words about a rooster who forgets how to crow, and a little girl who helps him remember. End with the sun rising on cue.

Every morning, the rooster crowed to wake up the village. But one day he opened his beak, and nothing came out. He felt so ashamed that he hid in the barn. A little girl found him there. "Don't worry," she said gently. "Try again." She stood beside him and crowed softly herself. The rooster stretched his neck, took a deep breath and let out a loud, proud cock-a-doodle-doo! At that very moment, the sun rose over the hills.
Write a gentle story, about 85 words, about a boy who buries a coin in the garden, hoping a money tree will grow. Instead, it should end with him learning to enjoy a different surprise: a sunflower.

Mohan was told that anything planted in the soil will grow. So he buried a shiny coin in the garden, hoping for a tree full of money. Every day he watered the spot and waited. Weeks passed, and nothing sprouted. He felt foolish. One morning, he noticed a green shoot a short distance away. It grew taller and taller, until a bright yellow sunflower opened. Mohan smiled. It was not the tree he wanted, but it was a better surprise, and it made him very happy.
I'd like a story of about 90 words about the moon visiting a small girl who cannot sleep. It should end with the girl falling asleep.

Mira lay awake, staring at the ceiling. Suddenly, a silver beam slipped through her window. It was the moon, who had come down to see why she was not asleep. "I am scared of the dark," whispered Mira. "But I am here," said the moon softly. "I light the night for everyone." She smiled and felt less afraid. The moon sat quietly beside her window, glowing. Mira closed her eyes and listened to the quiet, and soon, she was fast asleep.
Tell a story, about 100 words, about a rickshaw puller who finds a bag left behind by a passenger and returns it. End with the passenger thanking him warmly.

Raju pulled his rickshaw through the busy streets all day. One evening he noticed a bag on the back seat, left behind by his last passenger. He looked inside and saw only clothes and papers. He did not know the passenger's name, so he went back to the stand where he had picked him up and waited. An hour later, the worried passenger came running. Raju held up the bag. The man smiled with relief and thanked him again and again. "You are an honest man," he said.
Two ants meet on a leaf floating down a stream. Write a children's story, about 85 words, about how they work together to reach the bank.

Two ants were riding on a leaf down a stream, when the leaf started to spin. One ant said, "We must reach the bank!" The other said, "But the water is deep." They looked around and saw a twig hanging low near the shore. The first ant held the leaf steady, and the second ant stretched out and caught the twig. Then they pulled the leaf closer, together. At last, they stepped onto dry land, happy and tired.
Write 70 words on why curiosity helps us learn, for a class assembly.

Curiosity is the wish to know more. When we ask questions and wonder why things happen, we learn much faster than when we simply memorise. Curious children read more, try new things and are not afraid of mistakes. Great discoveries began with someone asking, "What if?" So never be shy to ask a question in class. Your curiosity can take you far.
For a youth magazine, about 70 words on why listening is as important as speaking in a friendship.

Listening is as important as speaking in a friendship. When you listen, you show your friend that you care about what they feel. People open up when they know someone is paying attention. Without listening, we only hear our own voice, and misunderstandings grow. Good friends take turns speaking and listening. Next time a friend talks, put down your phone and really hear them.
Write a short paragraph, about 65 words, about why a sense of humour helps in hard times, for a school magazine.

A sense of humour helps us in difficult times. When we laugh at a small mistake or a silly situation, our worries feel lighter. Laughter also brings people closer, because we share a happy moment. It does not mean we ignore problems. It means we face them with a smile and keep going. Even on a bad day, one good laugh can change the mood.
A four-line poem for my mother, please, about her lap being the safest place in the world.

Your lap is where I always rest,
It is the place I love the best.
When I am sad or tired or small,
Your arms will catch me if I fall.
Write a short rhyme, six lines, for children about a clock that is always in a hurry.

Tick-tock, tick-tock, the clock is fast,
It wants the hours to rush on past.
It hurries round the numbered face,
In a very, very, very big race.
The clock is quick, it cannot wait,
So hurry up, or you'll be late!
Make up a funny four-line poem about a monkey who steals a hat.

A cheeky monkey stole my hat,
And wore it proudly, just like that.
He tipped it, bowed and climbed a tree,
And now it fits him better than me.
Our Class 4 will present an assembly on Friday at 9 am about saving electricity. Please write a short invitation to parents, about 45 words. Sign it Class 4 Teacher.

Dear Parents,
Class 4 will present the school assembly this Friday at 9 am, and the topic is saving electricity. The children have worked hard to prepare it. Please come and see what they have learnt. Your presence will encourage them. We look forward to seeing you.
Class 4 Teacher
Write a note for my housemate Ritu asking her to water the balcony plants twice while I am away this weekend. About 40 words. I'm Sana.

Hi Ritu,
I'll be away this whole weekend. Could you please water the balcony plants twice while I'm gone? I really appreciate your help, and I will happily return the favour. Thank you so much. I owe you one!
Sana
Class 3 has made hand puppets and will put on a show on Saturday at 11 am in the school courtyard. Write an invitation to parents, about 50 words. I'm their teacher, Mrs. Fernandes.

Dear Parents,
The children of Class 3 have made their own hand puppets and are ready to perform a puppet show. Please join us on Saturday at 11 am in the school courtyard. Your smiles and applause will make the children very happy. We hope to see you there.
Mrs. Fernandes
Class 3 Teacher

I am Meera Joshi of Class 8. I would like to request your permission to start a reading club for students of Classes 6 to 8. The club would meet once a week in the library to read and talk about books together. I believe it would help many of us enjoy reading more. I hope you will kindly consider my request.
Yours sincerely,
Meera Joshi
Class 8

Please write a job application email, about 90 words, for the post of junior librarian at a public library. My name is Divya Nair and I have a library science diploma and two years of experience at a school library.

Dear Sir or Madam,
I am writing to apply for the post of junior librarian at your library. I hold a diploma in library science and have two years of experience working in a school library. I enjoy helping readers find the books they need and keeping the shelves in good order. I would be glad to attend an interview at your convenience. Thank you for your time and consideration.
Yours sincerely,
Divya Nair
Write a notice: the computer lab will be closed from Monday to Friday during term exams and reopen the next Monday. About 45 words. It is from the IT Department.

NOTICE
Computer Lab Closed During Exams
All students are informed that the computer lab will remain closed from Monday to Friday during the term exams. It will reopen the following Monday. Please plan your work accordingly. Thank you for your understanding.
IT Department
Describe a tea stall on a cold morning in about 60 words.

The tea stall glows in the grey morning. Steam rises from a big kettle, and the smell of ginger and cardamom drifts down the lane. Men in woollen caps stand close to the stove, rubbing their hands. The owner pours tea into small glasses with a quick flick of his wrist. Everyone sips slowly, wrapped in warmth, and for a moment the cold seems far away.
Write a diary entry, about 70 words, for a boy on his first day at a new school. He felt nervous in the morning but made one friend by lunch.

Dear Diary,
Today was my first day at the new school, and my stomach hurt all morning. I walked into class and could not find a single face I knew. Then, at lunch, a boy offered to share his seat and asked about my old school. We laughed over silly jokes and talked until the bell rang. Now I feel much better. I think tomorrow will be easier.
Write a story, about 90 words, about a girl who finds a wallet on the road and returns it to the owner. End with the owner smiling.

Anjali was walking home from school when she saw a brown wallet lying on the road. She picked it up and looked inside. There was an identity card with an address. Anjali knew the street, so she decided to take the wallet there at once. An elderly man opened the door, looking worried. When she held out the wallet, his eyes widened. "I was just about to go and look for it," he said. Then the owner smiled warmly and thanked her.
Write a paragraph of about 70 words on why we should keep our streets clean, for our class notice board.

A clean street makes everyone happier. When we throw litter on the road, it blocks drains, spoils the view and attracts flies. We can easily avoid this by putting waste in dustbins and carrying a small bag when no bin is nearby. Clean streets are also safer for children and animals. If each of us does a little, our whole neighbourhood will look bright and welcoming.
Write a four-line rhyme about a snail, for a six-year-old. About 30 words.

A little snail went out to play,
He took his house along all day.
He moved so slow, he moved so small,
But he got there in the end, that's all!
Our cricket practice is moved to 6 am on Saturday because of the heat. Write a short message for the team group, about 35 words. I'm the captain, Zubin.

Hi team,
Saturday's practice has been moved to 6 am because of the heat. It will be cooler then, so we can train properly. Please be there on time. See you all at the ground!
Zubin (Captain)
Invite my classmates to a board-game evening at my house on Friday at 7 pm. Keep it casual, about 45 words. I'm Arjun.

Hey everyone,
I'm hosting a board-game evening at my house this Friday at 7 pm. Come along, bring your favourite game if you have one, and get ready for some friendly competition. Do let me know if you can make it.
Arjun
I waited a long time for my food at a restaurant and the dal arrived cold. Write a polite complaint to the manager, about 60 words. I'm Farah Khan.

Dear Manager,
I visited your restaurant and was disappointed. I had to wait a long time for my food, and when the dal finally arrived, it was cold. I understand that restaurants get busy, but I hope you can look into this and improve the service. Thank you for your attention.
Sincerely,
Farah Khan

I hope you are well. I am Rahul Menon, and I had the pleasure of studying economics under you in my final year. Thank you for your time and support.
Yours sincerely,
Rahul Menon

Sports Day on Friday
All students are informed that our school Sports Day will be held this Friday. Every student must come in their house colour. Please arrive on time and cheer for your house with spirit. Let us make the day joyful and memorable for everyone.
Sports Department
Describe a temple courtyard at dawn in around 70 words.

The temple courtyard is still and cool at dawn. The stone floor is damp from a morning wash, and a soft light spreads across the pillars. A bell rings once, its sound floating up through the quiet air. An old woman lights a lamp and folds her hands in prayer. Pigeons murmur on the roof. The scent of flowers and incense drifts around, and the day begins peacefully.
Please write a diary entry, about 65 words, for a girl who won her school's spelling bee today. Show that she was happy but also thought of her friend who came second.

Dear Diary,
I won the spelling bee today! When the teacher said the winning word, I spelled it right, and everyone clapped. I felt like I was floating. But then I saw my friend, who came second, trying to smile. I hugged her and told her she was amazing. I hope she knows that I really meant it. What a day!
Write a note to my mother, whom I call Mummy, about 35 words, saying I reached the hostel safely and will call after dinner. I'm Pooja.

Dear Mummy,
I reached the hostel safely. Please don't worry about me. I will call you after dinner and tell you everything. Please take care of yourself too. I miss you already. Love you lots.
Pooja
My dance class is holding its annual show on the second Sunday of March at 5 pm in the town hall. Write an invitation to our families, about 55 words, from Madhuri Dance Class.

Dear Families,
Madhuri Dance Class invites you to our annual show on the second Sunday of March at 5 pm in the town hall. Our students are excited to perform for you. Please join us, clap loudly and enjoy the evening. We would be delighted to see you there.
Madhuri Dance Class
Construction next door goes on after 9 pm and we cannot sleep. Write a polite complaint to our society secretary, about 70 words. I'm Suresh Pillai, Flat 304.

Dear Secretary,
I live in Flat 304. For some time now, the construction work next door has continued after 9 pm, and the noise makes it hard for us to sleep. I request you to please speak to those in charge and ask them to stop work at a reasonable hour. Your help in this matter will be greatly appreciated.
Thank you,
Suresh Pillai
Write an email, around 90 words, introducing myself to a new pen friend in Japan. I'm Sneha, 13, from Chennai, and I like painting and cricket.

Subject: Hello from Chennai

Dear Friend,
My name is Sneha, and I am 13 years old. I live in Chennai, a big city in southern India. In my free time, I like painting and playing cricket. I would love to know about your life in Japan and what you enjoy doing. Please write back and tell me about your school, your family and your favourite things. I am looking forward to hearing from you.
Your new friend,
Sneha
Write a notice for our building: the water supply will be off on Tuesday from 10 am to 2 pm. About 45 words. It is from the Building Committee.

NOTICE
Water Supply Off on Tuesday
Residents are informed that the water supply to our building will be off this Tuesday from 10 am to 2 pm. Please plan your day accordingly. We regret the inconvenience and thank you for your understanding.
Building Committee
Write a 60-word description of a mango tree in the summer.

The old mango tree stands at the corner of the yard, wide and green. In summer, its branches bend under the weight of golden fruit. The air smells sweet and warm. Birds hop between the leaves, pecking at ripe mangoes, and squirrels race along the trunk. Children wait below with open hands. Its cool shade is the best place on a hot afternoon.
Please write a diary entry, about 55 words, for a boy who planted a tulsi plant on the balcony with his grandmother today.

Dear Diary,
Today my grandmother and I planted a tulsi plant on our balcony. She showed me how to press the soil gently around the roots. My hands got very dirty, and we both laughed. She says I must water it every morning. I promise to look after it well, because it is now our plant.
Please write a story, about 80 words, about a boy who is afraid of the dark. End with him switching off the light by himself.

Kabir always slept with the light on because he was afraid of the dark. One night, the bulb was bright, but he noticed his toys sitting quietly on the shelf. Nothing in the room had changed. The bear was still the bear, and the chair was still a chair. Kabir took a deep breath and listened to the soft night sounds. Then he climbed out of bed, reached up, and switched off the light himself.
Please write a paragraph of about 80 words on why teamwork matters, for a school essay.

Teamwork matters because no one can do everything alone. When people work together, each person brings a different skill, and the work becomes easier and better. In a football match, a goal is scored by the whole team, not by one player. At school, group projects teach us to listen, share ideas and help one another. Teamwork also builds trust, because we learn that others will support us. A good team also celebrates success together, which makes every victory sweeter.
Write a six-line rhyme about rain for a first-grade class. About 30 words.

Pitter-patter, drip and drop,
Rain is falling, will not stop.
Puddles here and puddles there,
Splashing boots are everywhere.
When the rain has gone away,
Rainbows come out to play.
Write a message, about 40 words, wishing my friend Tanvi good luck for her dance audition tomorrow. I'm Isha.

Hi Tanvi,
Best of luck for your dance audition tomorrow! You have worked so hard, and I know you will shine on that stage. Just enjoy every step. I'll be thinking of you. Call me when it's over!
Isha
Write a polite and kind request to my neighbour to keep her dog quiet at night, about 60 words. I'm Gita from Flat 2B. Her name is Mrs. D'Souza.

Dear Mrs. D'Souza,
I hope you are well. This is Gita from Flat 2B. I wanted to mention, gently, that your dog has been barking at night, and it is waking me up. I know dogs cannot always be helped, so I would be grateful if we could find a solution together. Thank you for understanding.
Warm regards,
Gita
Please write a notice for choir tryouts for students of Classes 5 to 8 in the music room on Wednesday at 3:30 pm, about 50 words.

NOTICE
Choir Tryouts
Tryouts for the school choir will be held on Wednesday at 3:30 pm in the music room. All students of Classes 5 to 8 who enjoy singing are welcome to attend. Come with a happy voice and a smile. We look forward to hearing you.
Write a thank-you message, about 40 words, to my neighbour Mrs. Bhat for feeding my cat while I was away. I'm Varun.

Dear Mrs. Bhat,
Thank you so much for feeding my cat while I was away. It was a great relief to know she was in good hands. I really appreciate your kindness. I owe you a favour.
Varun
Invite my uncle to my piano recital on Sunday at 5 pm. Keep it warm and short, about 45 words. I'm Meghna.

Dear Uncle,
I am playing in my piano recital this Sunday at 5 pm, and I would love for you to be there. It would mean a lot to me to see you in the audience. I'm a little nervous, but excited too. Please do come!
With love,
Meghna
Write an invitation for my friends, about 50 words, to a kite-flying morning on our terrace for Makar Sankranti. I'm Bhavin, and the plan is to start at 8 am.

Hello friends,
It's Makar Sankranti, and what better way to celebrate than with kites? Come to our terrace at 8 am and let's fill the sky with colour. Bring your own kite if you have one, and your best flying spirit. Let me know if you can join us.
Bhavin
Write a polite request to the office cafeteria manager to add more vegetarian options to the lunch menu. About 70 words. I'm Rohini Das, from the third floor.

Dear Cafeteria Manager,
I am Rohini Das from the third floor. I enjoy the lunches at the cafeteria, but I would like to request that you add more vegetarian options to the menu. I believe it would give everyone a wider choice. Thank you for considering my request, and thank you for the good service you already provide.
Regards,
Rohini Das
Write a thank-you email, about 80 words, to Mr. Banerjee, who interviewed me on Tuesday for a content writer position. I'm Aarti Sen.

Subject: Thank You for the Interview

Dear Mr. Banerjee,
Thank you for taking the time to interview me on Tuesday for the content writer position. I enjoyed learning more about the role. The conversation made me even more interested in working with you. Please let me know if you need anything more from me. I hope to hear from you soon, and I thank you again for your time and kindness.
Sincerely,
Aarti Sen
My son Ayaan Sheikh studies in Class 6, section B. Write a short email, about 70 words, to the school office asking for a copy of his bonafide certificate. I'm his father, Imtiaz Sheikh.

Subject: Request for a Bonafide Certificate

Dear Sir or Madam,
My son, Ayaan Sheikh, studies in Class 6, section B. I would be grateful if you could issue a copy of his bonafide certificate at the earliest. Please let me know if any form or other document is needed from my side, and I will send it promptly. Thank you for your help.
Yours sincerely,
Imtiaz Sheikh
Please write a notice, about 50 words, announcing a book fair in the school hall from Wednesday to Friday. It is from the Library Committee.

NOTICE
Book Fair
The school is holding a book fair in the school hall from Wednesday to Friday. Students are welcome to visit and look at the books. Come, browse and discover your next favourite read. Let us celebrate the joy of reading together.
Library Committee
Describe my father's old bicycle in about 55 words.

My father's old bicycle leans against the wall of our veranda. Its black paint has faded, and the bell rings with a tired little clang. The seat is worn smooth from years of use. It creaks when it moves, but it still has plenty of roads left.
Describe a conductor collecting tickets on a crowded bus, in about 80 words.

The bus is full, but the conductor moves through it like a dancer. A leather bag hangs from his shoulder, and a bundle of tickets is tucked between his fingers. He calls out the stops in a loud, cheerful voice. When the bus lurches, he catches a pole and keeps going. He nods at a boy for a seat, counts coins quickly and tears off tickets with a snap. Then he whistles twice, and the bus rolls on.
Can you write a diary entry, about 65 words, for a boy who learned to swim today. Say he was scared at first but swam one full length by the end.

Dear Diary,
Today I learned to swim! At first I was scared and held the edge of the pool tightly. My coach said, "Just kick and breathe." I took a deep breath and let go. My arms were tired, but I kept going. By the end of the class, I swam one full length of the pool. I felt so proud!
Write a diary entry of about 65 words about an evening with a power cut when my family played cards by candlelight.

Dear Diary,
The lights went out this evening, and the whole house became dark. We lit two candles and sat around the table. Someone brought out the old pack of cards, and we played until we were laughing so loudly that the neighbours could hear. I almost forgot about the fan and the TV. It was one of the nicest evenings we have had in a long time.
Please write a story, about 100 words, about a farmer who plants a magic seed. End with a very big pumpkin growing from it.

A farmer named Ramu found a shiny seed on his path and planted it in a corner of his field. Each morning he watered it and spoke kindly to it. Within days, a green shoot appeared, and then a strong vine spread across the ground. The villagers laughed and said it was only a weed. Ramu kept caring for it anyway. Months later, the vine bore one round fruit that grew bigger and bigger. At last it became a very big pumpkin, as large as a bullock cart.
Can you write a story, about 85 words, about a girl whose paper plane has to cross a river. End with the plane landing on the far bank.

Diya folded a paper plane and ran to the river's edge. On the other bank, her friend Sameer was waiting with a notebook. The river was wide, and the wind was strong. Diya smoothed the wings and held her breath. Then she threw the plane high into the air. It wobbled, dipped and rose again over the shining water. Everyone on the bank watched in silence. Finally, the little plane glided down and landed softly on the far bank.
Please write a paragraph of about 70 words on what makes a good friend.

A good friend listens when you speak and tells you the truth kindly. She shares your happiness and stays beside you when you are sad. A good friend does not laugh at your mistakes but helps you fix them. She keeps your secrets safe and forgives small quarrels quickly. You can trust her, and she can trust you. Such a friend is a treasure, and we should try to be one.
Please write a paragraph of about 90 words on how a library helps a town.

A library is a gift to a town. It lets people of every age read books they could never buy for themselves. Children discover stories there, students find quiet places to study, and elders enjoy the newspapers. Many libraries also hold story hours and reading clubs, which bring neighbours together. A library teaches us that knowledge belongs to everyone. When a town cares for its library, it is really caring for the minds of all its people.
Write a paragraph, about 75 words, on the benefits of walking to school.

Walking to school is good for the body and the mind. It gives us fresh air and gentle exercise before the day begins. On the way, we notice trees, birds and shops that we would miss in a vehicle. It is also a good time to chat with friends. Walking saves fuel and keeps the roads less crowded. Children who walk often arrive at school feeling cheerful and awake.

Sailing so slowly, so soft and so high.
It watches the sleepers, it lights up the street,
It shines on the rooftops and fields of wheat.
When morning arrives and the stars slip away,
The moon says goodbye till the end of the day.

Describe my grandmother making halwa in the kitchen, in about 70 words.

My grandmother stands at the stove, stirring a heavy pan. The ghee melts, and the mixture turns slowly darker. The smell fills the whole house and reaches me in the next room. She adds sugar and hot water, and the mixture hisses and puffs. Her wrist moves in slow circles. When she is done, the halwa shines like a soft, warm treasure.
Describe a night sky during a power cut in about 70 words.

When the power goes out, the sky above the town comes alive. Without the street lights, hundreds of stars appear, small and sharp against the deep dark. The moon hangs low like a lantern. Everyone steps out of their houses and looks up in wonder. Children point at the brightest stars, and the elders speak in low voices. The whole neighbourhood becomes calm, and for a while, no one wishes the lights to return.
Write a description of a fishing harbour at low tide in about 60 words.

At low tide, the harbour is quiet and still. The water has drawn back, and the wooden boats lean sideways on the wet mud. Fishermen mend their nets on the quay, their fingers moving quickly. Gulls walk along the edge, searching for scraps. A thin smell of salt and fish hangs in the air. Everyone waits patiently for the sea to return and lift the boats again.
Describe the sound of a thunderstorm heard from inside a house, in about 60 words.

First comes a low rumble, far away, like a big drum rolling across the sky. Then the wind pushes against the windows, and the first drops begin to tap the glass. Suddenly, there is a sharp crack of thunder that shakes the room. Rain pours down loudly on the roof. Inside, everything feels snug, and the sound of the storm seems to wrap around the house.
Describe a cat sleeping on a window ledge, about 50 words.

The cat lies curled on the window ledge, a soft grey ball in a patch of sunshine. Her chest rises and falls slowly. Her tail wraps around her paws, and one ear twitches at a sound outside. She is warm and completely at peace. The whole afternoon seems to slow down just to let her sleep.
Draft a diary entry, about 70 words, about the day I cleaned my room and found an old letter from my best friend, who moved away.

Dear Diary,
Today I finally cleaned my room. Under a pile of old books, I found a letter from my best friend, who moved away. Her handwriting looked just the same as I remembered. I sat on the floor and read it three times. It brought back so many happy memories. I decided to write to her tonight. I hope she remembers me as well as I remember her.
Draft a diary entry, about 80 words, about a train journey to my grandparents' village. Mention the window, the snacks and my grandmother waiting on the platform.

Dear Diary,
Today I took the train to my grandparents' village. I got a window seat and watched the fields and trees rush past. I had packed some snacks, and I shared them with a boy sitting beside me. When the train stopped at our station, I saw my grandmother waiting on the platform, waving with a big smile. I ran to her and hugged her tight. I am so happy to be here.
Draft a diary entry, about 60 words, for a nine-year-old whose teacher praised his drawing in front of the whole class today.

Dear Diary,
Today was a wonderful day. Our teacher held up my drawing in front of the whole class and said it was beautiful. My cheeks felt hot, but I was smiling so much. My friends clapped for me. I want to draw even more tomorrow. I think this is the happiest day of my school life so far.
Compose a diary entry, about 75 words, about a quarrel with my best friend Anaya and how we made up the next day.

Dear Diary,
I had a big quarrel with Anaya yesterday. We both said unkind things, and I went home feeling terrible. All night I kept thinking about it. This morning, I went to her and said I was sorry. She smiled and said she was sorry too. We hugged, and the heavy feeling disappeared. I have learned that saying sorry quickly saves a lot of sadness.
Compose a diary entry, about 70 words, about the first time I cooked dinner for my family. I made khichdi. Mum said it was tasty but a little salty.

Dear Diary,
Today I cooked dinner for the whole family for the first time. I made khichdi. I was nervous when everyone sat down to eat. Mum tasted it and said it was tasty but a little salty. Everyone laughed, and I laughed too. Everyone had a second helping, which made me proud. Next time, I will add less salt.
Draft a story, about 80 words, about a hedgehog who loses her way home at night. End with fireflies lighting her path to her burrow.

Pinky the hedgehog went out to look for berries and wandered far from her burrow. When the sky turned dark, every bush looked the same, and she could not find the way home. She sat down and began to cry softly. Just then, tiny lights floated out of the grass. A group of fireflies glowed around her and slowly flew ahead. Pinky followed them, and soon the fireflies lit her path all the way to her burrow.
Tell me a story, about 75 words, about a small star who thinks she is too tiny to shine. End with her shining brightly.

Tara was a tiny star in a big night sky. All around her, large stars blazed, and she felt too small to matter. She hid behind a cloud and stopped trying to glow. One dark night, a lost traveller looked up, searching for a light to guide him home. Tara took a deep breath and shone with all her might. The traveller smiled and followed her light. Tara was shining brightly at last.
Write a story of about 90 words about an old lady who forgets her bag on a bus. The conductor runs after the bus to return it. End with her thanking him.

Mrs. Pillai stepped off the bus and walked towards the market, but she had left her bag on the seat. A moment later, the conductor saw it and shouted her name. The bus had already moved, so he jumped off at the next stop and ran back, holding the bag high. Out of breath, he found her by the vegetable stall. Mrs. Pillai gasped and took her bag. With a warm smile, she thanked him and blessed him.
Draft a story, about 90 words, about a boy who practises the tabla every day. End with him playing at the school function.

Nikhil loved the tabla, but he was not very good at it. Every day after school, he sat on the floor and practised the same beats. His fingers hurt, and sometimes his mistakes made his friends giggle. But he kept going, and little by little, the rhythm began to flow. When the school function came, the teacher asked him to play. Nikhil took a deep breath, and his hands moved confidently. He played the tabla at the school function while everyone clapped.
Draft a story, about 75 words, about a snowman who is built in summer. End with a flower growing where he melted.

Children built a snowman on the one cold morning of a long hot summer. By noon, the sun was strong, and the snowman began to shrink. He did not mind, because he had made everyone laugh. Slowly, his hat tilted and his carrot nose slid down. At last, only a small puddle was left on the grass. A few days later, a tiny flower grew exactly there.
Please write a paragraph, about 80 words, on why pets teach children to care for others.

Pets teach children to care for others because they depend on us. A dog needs food and walks, and a cat needs water and affection. Children learn to be responsible when they feed a pet on time. They also learn to be gentle, as animals can feel pain and fear. When a pet is happy, the child feels proud. In this way, children grow into kind and caring people.
Write a short paragraph, about 60 words, on honesty.

Honesty means telling the truth, even when it is difficult. An honest person does not cheat, hide mistakes or pretend to be what he is not. People trust honest friends because they know their words are true. Telling lies may seem easy for a moment, but it creates problems later. When we speak the truth, we feel light and free.
Draft a paragraph of about 60 words on why sharing is better than keeping things for ourselves.

Sharing makes both people happier. When we give a friend half of our lunch or lend a toy, we feel warm inside, and the friend feels cared for. Things that are kept alone often lose their joy, but things that are shared grow sweeter. Sharing also teaches us to think of others. A child who shares will always have friends.
Please write a paragraph, about 70 words, on why patience is a good habit.

Patience is the ability to wait calmly without getting angry or upset. It is a good habit because many good things take time. A seed needs days to sprout, and a student needs months to learn. When we are patient, we think clearly and make fewer mistakes. We also get along better with others, since we listen and do not rush them. Patience helps us grow.
Write about 75 words on the joy of cooking with family.

Cooking with family is a joy that goes beyond food. When everyone gathers in the kitchen, the work becomes a game. Someone chops the vegetables, someone stirs the pot, and someone tastes it far too often. We talk, laugh and tell old stories while the food cooks. The meal that we make together tastes better than any other, because it carries our love in every bite. These moments become memories that stay with us for life.
Write a funny rhyme, about 60 words, about a sleepy elephant.

He was far too sleepy to move his big feet.
He snored in the morning, he snored in the noon,
And the crows made a nest on his trunk by the moon.
The whole town went quiet to let him sleep,
For his snores made the ground go beep, beep, beep!

Green light, green light, off we go,

I hope you are doing well. I was thinking about our school days the other day, and an idea came to me. Why don't we organise a reunion for our class this winter? It would be wonderful to see everyone again. Could you help me contact a few of our old friends? Let me know what you think.
Warm regards,
Nitin

Annual Day Rehearsal
All students of Class 5 are informed that the annual day rehearsal will be held on Monday at 2 pm in the hall. Please be on time and bring your costumes if you have them. Everyone must attend.
Class Teacher
Describe a mountain village in mist in about 80 words.

The village sits on the hillside, wrapped in a thick white mist. Houses with slanting roofs appear and vanish like shadows. A narrow path winds between stone walls, wet and slippery. Somewhere, a bell tinkles on a cow's neck, though no cow can be seen. Smoke from kitchen fires rises slowly and mixes with the fog. The air is cold and smells of pine and wet earth. It feels as if the whole village is asleep inside a cloud.
Describe the first rain falling on dry earth, in about 65 words.

After months of dry heat, the first drops fall on the earth. They make small dark spots on the dusty ground. Then the rain comes faster, and a sweet, fresh smell rises from the soil. The trees shake their leaves and look greener. Children run out with open arms. Birds sing loudly from the branches. The whole land seems to take a long, deep breath and smile.
Describe a quiet library reading room in about 60 words.

The reading room is calm and cool. Tall windows let in soft light that falls on long wooden tables. A few people sit with open books, turning pages slowly. The only sounds are the hum of a ceiling fan and the soft squeak of a chair. The shelves rise along the walls, full of old and new covers. Time moves gently here.
Describe the empty school hall after the annual day in about 70 words.

An hour ago, the school hall was full of music and clapping. Now it is quiet. Rows of chairs stand crooked, and paper streamers lie on the floor. A single shoe sits under a bench, and a half-drunk glass of water rests on the stage. The curtains hang still, and the lights are dim. A watchman walks slowly down the aisle, picking up programmes. The hall seems to remember the evening.
Describe a pani puri stall in the evening, in about 65 words.

As the sun sets, the pani puri stall comes alive. The vendor stands behind a glass counter with a pile of crisp little puris. People gather around, holding small leaf bowls. He taps each puri, fills it with potato and spicy water, and hands it over quickly. Customers pop it in their mouths, and their eyes water and smile at the same time. The stall stays busy until dark.
Compose a diary entry, about 65 words, about a day when I missed the school bus, walked home in the rain, got very wet but laughed about it. I'm a girl in Class 7.

Dear Diary,
Today I missed the school bus, and then it began to rain. I had no umbrella, so I walked home. By the time I reached our gate, I was soaked from head to toe. Mummy shook her head when she saw me, but I could not stop laughing. It was a silly day, but a fun one.
I'd like you to write a diary entry, about 70 words, for a boy whose team lost the final football match today, but who still felt proud of how they played.

Dear Diary,
Our football team lost the final today. The score was close, and my heart sank when the whistle blew. I felt like crying. But then I looked at my friends. We had played with all our strength and never given up. Our coach said he was proud of us. I am proud of us too. We will try again next year.
I'd like you to write a diary entry, about 60 words, about the night before a big exam. I was nervous, and my mother brought me a glass of warm milk.

Dear Diary,
Tomorrow is my big exam, and I am very nervous. I kept going through my notes again and again. Then Mummy came in with a glass of warm milk and sat beside me for a while. She said I had worked hard and should sleep well. I felt much calmer. I will do my best.
I'd like you to write a diary entry, about 70 words, about watching the first monsoon rain from the veranda with my grandfather.

Dear Diary,
This evening, dark clouds gathered, and then the first monsoon rain came down. My grandfather and I sat on the veranda with hot tea and watched it. The air smelled of wet earth. He told me how, when he was a boy, they used to run out and dance in the first rain. We sat quietly for a long time. It was a lovely, peaceful evening.
Prepare a diary entry, about 65 words, about the last day of the school year. I hugged my friends and promised to meet them in the vacations.

Dear Diary,
Today was the last day of the school year. We cleaned our desks and said goodbye to our teachers. My friends and I hugged each other for a long time. We promised to meet in the vacations and not to forget one another. I walked out of the gate with a smile, but my eyes were a little wet. I will miss them.
A lost kitten finds a home. Write a story, about 70 words, with the ending that the kitten purrs.

A small grey kitten wandered through the cold, wet street. She was hungry and tired, and every door was closed to her. At last, she crept under the gate of a little house and curled up on the doorstep. A girl named Mina opened the door and saw her. She picked up the kitten, wrapped her in a towel and gave her warm milk. The kitten closed her eyes and began to purr.
Compose a story, about 90 words, about a robot who has never laughed. End with the robot laughing at a joke.

Robo lived in a workshop and did every task perfectly, but he had never laughed. A boy named Aman visited each day and told jokes, but Robo only blinked. One day, Aman said, "Why did the clock go to school? To learn how to tell the time!" Robo's lights flickered, and his head tilted. There was a strange sound inside him, a beep, then a buzz, and then a happy, wobbly noise. Robo was laughing at last.
Compose a story, about 80 words, about two brothers who fight over the last mango and then decide to share it.

Two brothers, Raju and Sonu, saw one last mango on the plate. Both wanted it and began to argue. Raju pulled it one way, and Sonu pulled it the other. Their mother watched quietly and said, "If you keep pulling, nobody will eat it." The brothers stopped and looked at each other. Then Raju took a knife and cut the mango in half. Each brother got his share, and both of them ate happily.
Compose a story, about 65 words, about a girl whose balloon flies away. End with her waving goodbye to it.

Pia held a bright red balloon at the fair. A sudden gust of wind pulled the string from her fingers, and the balloon floated up. She cried out and jumped, but it was too high. Her father hugged her and pointed upwards. The balloon was rising higher and higher into the blue sky. Pia wiped her tears and smiled. She waved goodbye until it was a tiny red dot.
Prepare a story, about 80 words, about a village that has no clock. A boy makes a sundial, and the story ends with everyone meeting at the same time.

In a small village, nobody owned a clock. People met whenever they pleased, and meetings were always late. One day, a boy named Gopal noticed that the shadow of a tall pole moved slowly across the ground. He pushed a stick into the ground and marked the line where the shadow fell at noon. Soon, he added more marks. He had made a sundial. The villagers were amazed. Next morning, everyone gathered by the sundial together at the same time.
Draft a paragraph of about 80 words about a machine I would invent to help my grandmother in the kitchen.

If I could invent a machine for my grandmother, it would be a helpful kitchen robot. It would peel vegetables, grind spices and carry heavy pots, so her hands would never get tired. It would also remind her to switch off the gas. But I would make sure it never cooks, because nobody can make dal like my grandmother. The machine would only help, and she would remain the real chef.
Draft a paragraph of about 70 words on spending a day without screens at home.

A day without screens can be surprisingly pleasant. Without phones and television, we notice things we usually miss. We talk more at the table and play board games together. Children draw or read, and grown-ups cook or walk in the garden. The hours feel longer and calmer. At night, we sleep better, since our eyes and minds are rested. I think everyone should try it at least once a month.
Write about 75 words on how festivals bring people together.

Festivals bring people together like nothing else. At Diwali, Eid and Christmas, families gather in one home, and neighbours exchange sweets and greetings. People forget their quarrels and share food and laughter. Children enjoy the lights, the music and the new clothes. Even those who live far away try to return home. Festivals remind us that happiness grows when it is shared. Whatever our religion, a festival teaches us to open our doors and our hearts.
Compose a paragraph of about 60 words on why we should respect elders.

Elders have lived long and learned many things. They have faced hard times and know what works and what does not. When we respect them, we listen to their advice and treat them politely. This does not mean we must agree with every word, but we should hear them with patience. Respect for elders makes our families and our communities warm and strong.
Compose a paragraph of about 75 words on the joy of receiving a letter in the post.

Getting a letter in the post is a small joy in a busy world. The postman hands over an envelope, and your name is written on it by a real hand. You can see the writer's style in every loop and line. Opening it is like opening a little door to someone's heart. Unlike a quick message, a letter can be read again and kept in a drawer for years. It feels special.
Write an eight-line poem about a sleepy village in the afternoon, about 65 words.

The village naps in the afternoon sun,
The lanes are empty, the work is done.
The dog lies down in the shade of the wall,
And the hens are silent, one and all.
A bullock cart creaks, then stops by a tree,
The farmer is dreaming of sweet cold tea.
The breeze goes by with a whispering sound,
And peace lies soft on the sleepy ground.
Write a counting rhyme for small children about five cows, going from one to five. About 50 words.

One cow in the meadow, eating green grass,
Two cows in the meadow, watching us pass.
Three cows in the meadow, mooing so loud,
Four cows in the meadow, under a cloud.
Five cows in the meadow, home in a line,
Say goodnight to the cows, the sun will soon shine.
Write a short poem on friendship, four lines, about 30 words.

A friend will laugh when you are glad,
And hold your hand when you are sad.
With her, you walk through every storm,
And every day feels bright and warm.
Please write a four-line rhyme for a toddler about putting on shoes, about 30 words.

One shoe, two shoe, on we go,
Left foot, right foot, in a row.
Pull the strap and tie it tight,
Now we are ready, shoes are right!
Please write a six-line rhyme about a monkey who steals a banana, about 40 words.

A monkey swung from tree to tree,
He saw a banana by the sea.
He tiptoed down without a sound,
And grabbed it from the sandy ground.
He climbed back up with a happy grin,
And ate it all, even the skin!
Write a note to my sister saying I have taken her blue notebook and will return it tonight. About 30 words. I'm Kiran.

Dear Sister,
I have taken your blue notebook from your desk. I needed it for my homework. I promise to put it back tonight. Sorry for not asking first!
Kiran

Hi Meena,
Thank you so much for covering my shift yesterday. It really helped me, and I am truly grateful. Please tell me when you need a favour, and I will gladly return it.
Rohan

Could you write an email, about 60 words, to my teacher Mrs. Kulkarni asking for a two-day extension on my science project because I was unwell. I'm Sahil of Class 10.

Subject: Request for Extension on Science Project

Dear Mrs. Kulkarni,
I am Sahil of Class 10. I was unwell for a few days and could not finish my science project on time. May I please have a two-day extension to complete it? I will submit it as soon as I can. Thank you for your understanding.
Yours sincerely,
Sahil
Could you write an email, about 60 words, to my cousin Rahul asking for travel tips for visiting Jaipur next month. I'm Alisha.

Subject: Travel Tips for Jaipur

Dear Rahul,
I hope you are well. I'm planning to visit Jaipur next month, and I remember that you have been there. Could you please tell me which places are worth visiting and what I should keep in mind? Any tips would be a big help. Write back when you can.
Love,
Alisha
Power cuts have been happening every evening in our lane for a week. Write an email, about 80 words, to the electricity department asking them to look into it. I'm Mr. Dutta.

Subject: Daily Evening Power Cuts in Our Lane

Dear Sir or Madam,
For the past week, there has been a power cut in our lane every evening. This is causing a lot of trouble for all the families here, especially the children who need to study. I request you to please look into the cause of these cuts and fix the problem as soon as possible. Kindly let us know when we can expect a solution. Thank you.
Yours faithfully,
Mr. Dutta
Draft an email, about 65 words, to my sports teacher offering to help organise the relay race on Sports Day. I'm Chandan of Class 11.

Subject: Offer to Help with the Relay Race

Dear Sir,
I am Chandan of Class 11. I would like to offer my help in organising the relay race on Sports Day. I can help with the lines, the batons or whatever else you need. Please let me know how I can be useful. Thank you.
Yours sincerely,
Chandan
Draft an email, about 55 words, to a conference organiser confirming that I will attend on 5 March and asking if vegetarian food will be available. I'm Dr. Anand Rao.

Subject: Confirmation of Attendance on 5 March

Dear Sir or Madam,
I would like to confirm that I will attend the conference on 5 March. I would also like to ask whether vegetarian food will be available during the event. Thank you for organising this, and I look forward to attending.
Best regards,
Dr. Anand Rao

A water bottle with a dragon sticker has been found in Room 12. The owner may collect it from the staff room. Please remember to check your belongings before leaving the classroom. Thank you for your cooperation.

NOTICE
Extra Lab Practice
The science lab will be open for extra practice from 3 pm to 4 pm on Tuesday and Thursday. This is for Class 10 students. Please come prepared and bring your lab records. Make good use of this chance.
Science Department
