NOTICE
Garden Closed
The society garden will be closed on Saturday and Sunday for grass cutting. Residents are requested not to enter during these two days. It will reopen once the work is complete. Thank you for your understanding.
Garden Committee
Kindly write a notice, about 40 words: the last date for submitting school photograph order forms is Friday. From the Office.

NOTICE
Photograph Order Forms
Students are reminded that the last date for submitting school photograph order forms is Friday. Forms received after that day cannot be accepted. Kindly give your form to your class teacher in time.
School Office
Describe a street at five in the morning before anyone has woken up, in about 60 words.

The street is silent at five in the morning. The shops are shuttered, and the lamp posts glow dimly. A dog sleeps on the pavement, curled in a ball. In the distance, a milk van hums. The sky above the buildings turns slowly from black to blue. A cool breeze carries the faint smell of wet earth. The city is still, waiting for its day to begin.
Describe the face of a very old man who tells the best stories in about 60 words.

His face is a map of many years. Deep lines run across his forehead and around his eyes, which twinkle when he begins a story. His white eyebrows rise and fall as he speaks. His smile shows a few missing teeth but warms the whole room. Children sit near him, wide-eyed, while he waves his hands. Every wrinkle seems to hold a tale.
Describe a classroom on the last day before the holidays in about 70 words.

The classroom feels different on the last day before the holidays. The desks are bare, and the board is clean, with a big "Happy Holidays" written across it. Students chat loudly, and their bags are packed and ready by the door. The teacher smiles and hands out report cards. A few children look sad, but most are bursting with plans. When the bell rings, the room empties in a flash.
Describe a kitchen at midnight when everyone in the house is asleep, in about 55 words.

At midnight, the kitchen is dark and quiet. The fridge hums softly, and a tap drips slowly into the sink. A little moonlight falls across the steel plates on the rack. The air still smells faintly of dinner. Everything is in its place, resting. Only the clock on the wall ticks, counting the minutes of the sleeping house.
Describe a cricket match in a narrow lane in about 75 words.

In the narrow lane, the match is in full swing. A brick marks the wicket, and a tennis ball flies between two parked scooters. The batsman swings hard, and the ball bounces off a wall. Fielders squeeze against the gates. Someone's mother shouts from a balcony, but nobody listens. A fierce argument starts about whether the batsman is out. Soon everyone is laughing again, and the game goes on.
Prepare a diary entry, about 65 words, about a visit to the zoo where I saw an elephant and a giraffe. I'm a ten-year-old boy.

Dear Diary,
Today we went to the zoo. I saw an elephant, and it sprayed water over its back with its trunk. Then I saw a giraffe munching leaves from a very tall tree. Its neck is so long! I took many photographs. I was tired by the evening, but I wanted to stay longer. It was a wonderful day.
Prepare a diary entry, about 60 words, about baking my first cake. It sank in the middle but tasted good.

Dear Diary,
Today I baked my first cake. I followed every step carefully, but when I took it out of the oven, it had sunk in the middle! I felt disappointed at first. Then my family tasted it, and everyone said it was delicious. We ate it all by the evening. Next time, I will try to make it rise properly.
Kindly write a diary entry, about 75 words, about my grandfather telling me a story about his village school.

Dear Diary,
This evening, my grandfather told me about his village school. He said it had only one room and one teacher, and the children sat on the floor. They walked a long way every day, without shoes in the summer. I could not imagine it! He laughed as he remembered his friends and the games they played. I felt lucky to listen. I hope he tells me more stories soon.
Kindly write a diary entry, about 65 words, for a woman who has just received her first job offer letter and feels happy and a little scared.

Dear Diary,
Today I got my first job offer letter! I read it three times to be sure it was real. I'm so happy that I want to dance. But when I think about starting, my stomach feels funny. New people, new work, new place. Still, I know I can do it. I will start with a smile and learn every day.
Kindly write a diary entry, about 50 words, for a girl who finally learned to ride a bicycle without training wheels.

Dear Diary,
I did it! Today I rode my bicycle without training wheels. Papa held the seat at first and then let go without telling me. I wobbled and then went straight. I rode all the way to the end of the lane. I was so proud that I rang my bell the entire way back.
Prepare a story, about 90 words, about a fisherman who catches a golden fish. End with him setting it free.

Old Kesu had been fishing since dawn but had caught nothing. Just as he was about to leave, his net felt heavy. He pulled it in, and a golden fish flapped inside. Kesu thought of the money it could bring. But the fish looked at him with its small, bright eyes, and he felt it wanted to live. He slowly lifted it and laid it back in the river. With a flick of its tail, the fish swam away and disappeared.
Prepare a story, about 100 words, about two tea-sellers who are rivals on the same street. End with them sharing one stall during a heavy rain.

Two tea-sellers, Hari and Gopal, had stalls on opposite sides of the same street. They never spoke and often shouted that their tea was better. One afternoon, a thunderstorm hit the street. Rain poured down, and Hari's stall began to leak. Gopal's stall had a strong roof. He looked across the road and waved. Hari hesitated, then carried his kettle over. Soon both men stood under one roof, pouring tea for customers who had run in from the rain. They shared the stall and even chuckled together.
Kindly write a story, about 80 words, about a boy who is learning to ride a bicycle. End with him riding alone.

Sameer's new bicycle stood in the corner of the yard. Every evening, his father held the back of the seat while Sameer pedalled. Each time he fell, he got up and tried again. His knees were scraped, and his hands were sore. One day, he asked his father to let go. Papa smiled and loosened his grip. Sameer pedalled steadily down the lane and did not look back. At last, he was riding alone.
Kindly write a story, about 70 words, about the mystery of the missing socks. End with the socks being found under the sofa.

Every morning, Dia could find only one of her socks. She searched the cupboard, the laundry basket and the balcony. She asked her brother, who swore he had not touched them. Finally, one afternoon, she lay on the floor and looked under the sofa. There, in the dusty shadows, sat all her missing socks in a messy heap. Her puppy had been hiding them. The mystery was solved.
Kindly write a story, about 60 words, about a shy parrot who learns to say good morning. End with him saying it to the grandmother.

Mitthu was a shy parrot who never spoke. Every morning, the children said "Good morning" to him, but he only blinked. Slowly, he began to copy the sounds in his head. One day, Grandmother came into the garden with her tea. Mitthu puffed his chest and said, "Good morning!" Grandmother laughed with delight. Mitthu had said it to her.
Compose a paragraph of about 80 words on why I want to become a pilot when I grow up.

I want to become a pilot because I love the sky. When I see a plane glide over our house, I feel that I too want to fly. A pilot sees clouds from above and travels to faraway places. It is also a job of great responsibility, because many people trust the pilot with their lives. I know I must study hard and stay calm. Someday, I hope to sit in that seat.
How would you describe a good neighbour? Give me a paragraph of about 70 words.

A good neighbour is kind and helpful. She says hello with a smile and offers help in times of need. She keeps her music low at night and does not leave rubbish near other people's doors. When someone is ill, she brings a warm meal. A good neighbour respects privacy but is always ready to listen. Such neighbours turn a street into a friendly community.
Prepare a paragraph of about 85 words on why we should walk or cycle for short trips instead of using vehicles.

For short trips, walking or cycling is better than using a vehicle. It saves fuel and money and keeps the air clean. Fewer vehicles mean less noise and less traffic on the roads. Walking and cycling also give us exercise and fresh air. We can enjoy the view and say hello to people we meet. A short ride to the corner shop does not need a car. Small choices like this make our streets safer and our towns more pleasant.
Give me a paragraph, around 70 words, about learning from our mistakes.

Everyone makes mistakes, and that is not a bad thing. A mistake shows us what does not work, so that we can try something better. A child who falls while learning to walk gets up and tries again. If we hide our mistakes, we will repeat them. If we accept them and learn, we grow wiser. So let us not fear mistakes, but learn from them.
Prepare a paragraph of about 75 words on the value of keeping a diary.

Keeping a diary is a wonderful habit. Writing down our thoughts at the end of the day helps us understand our feelings. When we feel angry or sad, putting it into words calms us. A diary also keeps our memories safe, and years later, we can read about days we have forgotten. It teaches us to write clearly and honestly. Best of all, a diary is a private friend who always listens.
Make up a short rhyme for little ones about a bicycle bell. Four lines, about 25 words.

Ting-a-ling goes my bicycle bell,
It rings out loud and rings out well.
Here I come, so clear the way,
I'm riding to school this sunny day!
Please write a four-line poem about stars in the night sky, about 30 words.

Little stars in the midnight sky,
Shine so bright and sit so high.
They watch us sleep and guard our dreams,
Till the sun comes up with golden beams.
Write a six-line poem for a Class 1 child about the first day of school, about 45 words.

My bag is new, my shoes are bright,
I'm going to school, what a sight!
I wave goodbye to Mum at the gate,
I hope my new friends will not be late.
I hold my pencil, I find my seat,
School is going to be so sweet!
Write a six-line poem, about 45 words, thanking a teacher at the end of the year.

Dear Teacher, thank you for all you do,
For every lesson, old and new.
You helped me read, you helped me write,
You made my school days warm and bright.
I will remember all you said,
The kind words that stay in my head.
Write a funny four-line rhyme about a hen who wanted to learn to swim, about 35 words.

A hen once dreamed of learning to swim,
So she waddled to the pond on a whim.
She flapped and she splashed, and she sank to her chin,
Then she hopped back out with a soggy grin.
Leave a note for my flatmate Dev: the milk is finished and I will buy more on my way back. Roughly 35 words, from Ishaan.

Dev,
The milk is finished, so please don't wait for it with your cereal. I will buy a fresh packet on my way back this evening and put it in the fridge.
Ishaan
My friend Lucy is nervous before her first dance show tonight. I want a cheerful good-luck text for her, 30 words. I'm Omar.

Hi Lucy,
You have practised so hard, and tonight everyone will see it. Breathe, smile and enjoy every step. I'll be cheering for you. Good luck, you will shine!
Omar
Text to my mother, please: the bus is late and I will reach home after seven. Keep it near 30 words. Tanvi here.

Hello! My bus is running late today, so I will reach home a little after seven. See you soon.
Tanvi
Quick message to my teammate Hugo, asking him to share the meeting notes by evening. About 30 words, from Priya.

Hi Hugo,
Could you please share the notes from today's meeting by this evening? I would like to read them before tomorrow. Thank you for your help.
Priya
Slip-under-the-door note needed: my neighbour keeps receiving my parcels by mistake and I'd like them back. 40 words, kindly worded. Adaeze, flat 4.

Dear neighbour,
A few parcels meant for me have been delivered to your door by mistake. If you have any, could you please leave them outside my door, or ring my bell? Thank you for your kindness.
Adaeze, Flat 4
My grandmother turns seventy-five on Sunday. Put together an invitation to our relatives for tea at four, about 40 words. Signed Rekha.

You are warmly invited to tea at our house this Sunday at 4 pm. We are celebrating my grandmother's seventy-fifth birthday, and she would love to see you all. Please come and share the happy day with us.
Rekha
We just moved into a new flat. Draft a friendly housewarming invitation for our friends, dinner on Saturday at 7 pm, 50 words. We are Sam and Leila.

Hello friends,
We have moved into our new flat, and we would love you to see it! Please join us for dinner on Saturday evening at 7 pm. The rooms are still half empty, but the food will be full. Do come and bring your smiles.
Sam and Leila
I'd like a short invitation for a kite-flying morning in the park on Sunday at 8 am. Cheerful, for neighbourhood kids and parents, around 45 words. Arjun.

Come fly a kite with us! We are meeting in the park this Sunday at 8 am for a morning of colourful kites and open sky. Kids and parents are all welcome. Bring your kite and your good cheer. It will be a windy, happy morning.
Arjun
Our family is hosting a Diwali dinner for the cousins on the evening of the festival. Make an invitation for the family group, dinner at 8 pm, 45 words, from Neha.

Dear cousins,
This Diwali, please come to our house for dinner. We will light the lamps together, and dinner will be served at 8 pm. Wear your best clothes and come hungry! It will not feel like a festival without all of you.
Neha
As secretary of the Green Group, Mr Fernandes needs a formal invitation to all residents for a tree-planting day on the first Sunday of the month at 7 am. Write it in 35 words.

Dear residents,
The Green Group invites you to a tree-planting day in our colony on the first Sunday of the month at 7 am. Please wear comfortable clothes. Families are most welcome.
Mr Fernandes
Secretary, Green Group
The shirt that was delivered to me is a size too small. Write a polite complaint asking for an exchange, around 30 words. I'm Kavya.

Dear Sir or Madam,
The shirt delivered to me is a size too small. Could you please exchange it for the right size? I would be grateful for your help. Thank you.
Kavya
Our tap in the kitchen has been dripping for a week. Please write to the landlord, politely asking him to repair it, 40 words. Marcus.

Dear Landlord,
The kitchen tap in my flat has been leaking for a week, and it wastes a lot of water. Could you please send a plumber to repair it this week? Thank you for your help.
Marcus
Help me ask my class teacher, respectfully, whether I can hand in my science project on Monday instead of Friday because I was away. About 40 words. I'm Imran.

Dear Teacher,
I was away from school and could not finish my science project. May I please hand it in on Monday instead of Friday? I will work hard to complete it well. Thank you for understanding.
Imran
The music upstairs plays loudly after ten at night. A kind but firm request to the neighbours to lower it, 40 words. Written by Farah.

Dear neighbours,
We enjoy a good song too, but the music late at night comes through our walls and keeps us awake. Could you please keep the volume low after ten o'clock? Thank you for being considerate.
Farah
We waited a long time at a cafe and the tea arrived cold. Compose a calm complaint to the manager, under 50 words, from Jonas.

Dear Manager,
I visited your cafe recently. We waited a long time for our order, and the tea was cold when it arrived. I hope you can look into this. I would happily visit again if service improves.
Jonas
An email to my tailor, Mr Gupta, asking whether my kurta will be ready by Friday, and thanking him in advance. 40 words. Ananya.

Dear Mr Gupta,
I hope you are well. I wanted to ask if my kurta will be ready by Friday, as I need it soon. Please let me know if there is any delay. Thank you very much for your help.
Ananya
Email my uncle Raj and ask him to suggest two good adventure books for a long train trip. I'd like it in about 45 words, from Nikhil.

Dear Uncle Raj,
I hope you are well. I have a long train trip coming up and want something exciting to read. Could you suggest two good adventure books? I know you read a lot, so I trust your choice. Thank you!
With love,
Nikhil
Write an email to the swimming coach asking whether there is space in the beginners' class on Saturdays. 35 words, signed Mei.

Dear Coach,
I would like to learn swimming and wonder if there is a place in your beginners' class on Saturdays. Could you tell me the timings and the fee? Thank you for your time.
Mei
I've got a new pen friend in Kenya. Write my first email to him introducing myself, about 40 words. My name is Sanjay and I love cricket and chess.

Dear friend,
My name is Sanjay, and I am happy to be your pen friend. I love playing cricket and chess. Please tell me about your town and what you enjoy. I look forward to your reply.
Sanjay
Hostel permission email: I want to go home for the harvest festival from Thursday to Sunday. Write it to the warden in 35 words. Lakshmi.

Dear Warden,
I would like to request permission to go home from Thursday to Sunday for the harvest festival. I will return to the hostel on Sunday. Thank you for considering my request.
Lakshmi
Notice from the colony secretary: the library room is closed on Saturday for repainting. Write it up, under 40 words.

NOTICE
The reading room of our colony library will remain closed this Saturday for repainting. It will reopen once the work is finished. We thank you for your patience.
Secretary
Lost-and-found notice for the park gate: a green umbrella has been found near the swings. 30 words please.

FOUND
A green umbrella has been found near the swings in the park. If it belongs to you, please ask at the park gate and describe it to collect it.
Our cricket practice shifts from Wednesday to Thursday evening at 5 because the ground is booked. Put that on a notice board, 30 words.

NOTICE: Cricket Practice
This week, cricket practice will be on Thursday at 5 pm instead of Wednesday. The ground has been booked for another event on Wednesday. Please arrive on time.
The overhead tank gets scrubbed Tuesday, 10 am to 2 pm, and taps will run dry meanwhile. Prepare a short residents' notice, under 50 words.

NOTICE
The overhead water tank will be cleaned this Tuesday. There will be no water supply from 10 am to 2 pm. Please store enough water in advance. We are sorry for the trouble and thank you for your support.
Create a notice announcing a book fair in the community hall next Saturday and Sunday from 10 to 6, free entry. 45 words.

BOOK FAIR
Come to the community hall next Saturday and Sunday for a book fair! Books for all ages will be on sale. The fair is open from 10 am to 6 pm, and entry is free. Bring your family and find a new favourite book.
Describe a rainy market street in about 50 words, as if for a travel magazine.

The rain came suddenly, and the market turned into a river of colour. Umbrellas of red and blue bobbed above the crowd. Vendors pulled plastic sheets over mounds of oranges and spices. The smell of hot tea and wet earth floated through the lane, while puddles shook with every passing cart.
Tell me, in about 50 words, what my grandmother's kitchen is like: small, warm, brass pots, the smell of ginger.

My grandmother's kitchen is small, but it feels like the warmest room in the house. Brass pots shine on the shelf, and a pot of tea always simmers on the stove. The air smells of ginger and fresh bread. Every corner holds a memory of her hands at work.
Paint a picture in 50 words of a railway platform at dawn.

The platform is quiet and grey in the early light. A tea seller pours steaming cups into small glasses. Pigeons walk along the tracks, waiting for crumbs. A few sleepy passengers sit on their bags and watch the far signal. Then a distant whistle hums, and the whole platform slowly wakes.
One mango tree stands at the end of our lane. Give me a vivid description of it in 50 words.

The mango tree at the end of our lane is old and wide. Its thick branches shade the whole corner, and crows argue among its leaves. In summer, golden fruit hangs low, and the sweet smell reaches every house. Children wait below with sticks and eager eyes, hoping for one to fall.
Describe a crowded bus stop at five in the evening. Show the noise and the hurry. About 55 words.

At five o'clock, the bus stop is full of noise and hurry. Office workers check their watches and students squeeze closer to the edge of the road. Horns blare, and conductors shout the names of far-off places. When a bus finally comes, everyone pushes forward at once, and the crowd moves like a single wave.
Diary entry for the day I finally learned to ride a bicycle, around 50 words. I'm writing as Rafi.

Dear Diary,
Today I rode a bicycle without help! At first someone held the seat, and then I realised nobody was holding it any more. I wobbled and nearly fell, but I kept pedalling. When I looked back, the road was far behind me. I have never felt so proud and so free.
Rafi
Write a diary page about my first day at a new job, in 55 words. I felt nervous but met kind people. I'm Sofia.

Dear Diary,
Today was my first day at the new office. My hands shook when I walked in, but my team welcomed me with warm smiles. Someone showed me my desk and shared a cup of tea. I still have a lot to learn, but I think I will like it here.
Sofia
Diary, please: a power cut one evening, we all sat on the terrace and talked and ate mangoes. About 55 words. Writer: Chitra.

Dear Diary,
The lights went out this evening, and at first everyone grumbled. Then we carried mats to the terrace. We ate mangoes under the stars and talked more than we had in weeks. We told old stories and laughed until the lights returned. I almost wished they would stay off.
Chitra
I saw the sea for the first time today. Write that as a diary entry, around 55 words. I'm Dmitri.

Dear Diary,
Today I saw the sea for the first time. It was much bigger than I had imagined. The water kept rolling in and rolling out as if it were breathing. I took off my shoes and let the cold foam touch my feet. I laughed out loud, and I did not want to leave.
Dmitri
Zara here. After a kabaddi defeat I felt sad yet strangely proud of everyone; turn that into my diary page, about 50 words.

Dear Diary,
We lost the kabaddi match today. I was sad at first, but then I remembered how hard we fought. Everyone ran, tackled and cheered for each other until the end. Next time we will practise more. Losing hurt, but I am proud of my team.
Zara
Tiny story, about 65 words, about a lantern that was afraid of the dark.

A lantern hung on a porch and trembled each evening when the sun went down. He was afraid of the dark. One night, a lost child came walking down the lane, crying. The lantern glowed as brightly as he could. The child saw the light and ran home. After that night, the lantern was never afraid again, for he knew the dark needed him.
A story, short and sweet, of a girl named Noor who finds a stray kitten on a rainy day. 50 words.

On a rainy afternoon, Noor heard a tiny cry near the gate. A wet kitten sat shivering under a bench. She wrapped it in her scarf and carried it inside. Then she warmed some milk for it. By evening, the kitten was purring on Noor's lap, and the house had a new member.
Write a tiny story, about 60 words, about a boy who sold balloons and gave away his last one.

Every evening, a boy sold balloons near the temple steps. One day, only a single red balloon was left. A small girl stood nearby, looking at it with big eyes, but her mother had no money. The boy smiled and handed her the balloon. She laughed, and he walked home with an empty hand and a full heart.
Compose a short story for children, 60 words, of a tortoise who is not afraid of a big rainstorm.

Everyone in the forest ran for shelter when the storm clouds rolled in. Only the old tortoise stayed calm. She pulled in her head and legs and sat inside her shell. The wind howled and the rain thundered, but she stayed dry and warm. When the sky cleared, the animals came out and thanked her for the lesson.
I want a funny and gentle story of about 55 words about a bakery clock that ran backward.

The clock in the corner bakery ran backward. At noon it said eleven, and at closing time it said afternoon. The baker kept laughing and serving customers anyway. One morning, the clock said it was yesterday, and the baker baked yesterday's bread again. The customers loved it, and the clock kept its place on the wall.
Explain in about 55 words, as one paragraph, how a kind person next door improves daily life.

A good neighbour makes a home feel safe. When we need a spoon of sugar or help with a heavy bag, they are the nearest hand. They notice when something is wrong and offer a kind word. Even a simple smile each morning builds trust, and trust turns a row of houses into a real community.
In a short paragraph of 50 words, say what makes a festival special for a family.

A festival is special because it brings the family together. We cook old recipes, wear new clothes and decorate the house. Relatives who live far away return home, and grandparents tell stories from their childhood. The food is delicious, but the real joy is being together, laughing and remembering.
A paragraph for my school magazine on why I love the monsoon, about 55 words. I'm writing as Ritu.

The monsoon is my favourite season. After many hot days, the first rain brings a lovely smell of wet earth. The streets shine, the trees look greener, and the whole city seems to take a deep breath. I love sitting by the window with a cup of tea, watching the rain make small rivers on the road.
Paragraph on saving water at home, simple words, 55 words.

We can save a lot of water at home with small habits. Turn off the tap while brushing your teeth. Use a bucket instead of a running hose for washing the floor. Fix leaking taps quickly. Water the plants with the water left after washing vegetables. If everyone helps, our family will use less and waste nothing.
Tell readers in a paragraph of about 60 words why I enjoy painting. I'm Oliver and I paint landscapes on weekends.

I enjoy painting because it slows me down. On weekends, I take my brushes outside and paint landscapes of hills, rivers and fields. Mixing colours feels like a small adventure, and I forget my worries while I work. When a painting is finished, I feel calm and happy, as if I have shared a quiet moment with nature.
A four-line rhyme about a lazy cat who sleeps in the sun. Keep it around 30 words.

A lazy cat lay in the sun,
Her day of work was never begun.
She yawned and stretched, then closed her eyes,
And dreamed of fish and cloudy skies.
Please give me a four-line poem about the first rain of the monsoon, about 25 words.

The first drops fall on dusty ground,
And all the earth smells fresh and sweet.
The children dance and jump around
With bare and happy dripping feet.
Rhyme for toddlers, four short lines, counting stars. About 30 words.

One little star in the sky so high,
Two little stars wink and blink goodbye.
Three little stars twinkle all night through,
Four little stars say, 'Sleep well, you.'
I need a short poem of six lines, rhyming in pairs, about a train that goes through the hills. About 40 words.

The little train climbs up the hill,
Through mist so soft and air so still.
It winds past pines and waterfalls,
Past tiny huts with painted walls.
The whistle sings a happy tune,
And we will reach the town by noon.
Verse about a friendly bus driver who waves at everyone, four lines, light and cheerful.

Our bus driver waves with a smile every day,
To the baker, the child and the man on his way.
He honks a small hello as he rolls through the town,
And the grumpiest faces forget how to frown.
Cheer up my friend Arun, who failed his driving test today, with a warm message of around 40 words. I'm Beth.

Hi Arun,
I heard about the test, and I'm sorry. It is a bad feeling, but it is only one try. Lots of people pass on their second go, and you will too. Call me whenever you want to talk.
Beth
Message for the office group: I am leaving early on Friday for a family event and will finish my tasks by Thursday. About 40 words, from Vikram.

Hello team,
I will be leaving early this Friday for a family event. I plan to finish all my tasks by Thursday evening, so nothing will be left pending. Please call me if anything urgent comes up before then.
Vikram
Text my brother that dinner is in the fridge and he only needs to heat it. 30 words. Sent by Chiara.

Hi, dinner is in the fridge. You only need to heat it before you eat. Enjoy your meal, and don't leave it too late!
Chiara
Roommate note: I'm away this weekend, so could they water the balcony plants on Saturday? Warm tone, 35 words. From Yuki to Pooja.

Dear Pooja,
I will be away this weekend. Could you please water the balcony plants on Saturday? They only need a little water each. Thank you so much, I really appreciate your help.
Yuki
Birthday wishes for a friend named Selvi, who loves books and music, in about 40 words. I am Dev.

Happy birthday, Selvi!
May your year be full of good books and better songs. You are a friend who makes every room happier, and I'm lucky to know you. I hope today brings you laughter, cake and lots of love.
Dev
Our group is planning a picnic by the lake next Sunday at nine. Whip up a fun invitation, 55 words, signed Tara.

Pack your hats and your appetite! We are going on a picnic by the lake next Sunday at 9 am. Bring a snack to share and a mat to sit on. We will play games, sing songs and splash our feet in the water. Say yes soon so we can plan the food.
Tara
An invitation to parents for our Class 5 art show on Friday at 3 pm in the school hall. Formal, around 40 words. From Mrs Pillai.

Dear parents,
You are cordially invited to the Class 5 art show on Friday at 3 pm in the school hall. Our children have worked hard, and they will be proud to show their art to you.
Mrs Pillai
Need a short invitation to my parents' wedding anniversary dinner on Sunday at 8 in the evening. It's a surprise, so mention that. Roughly 35 words, from Anjali.

Please join us this Sunday at 8 pm for a dinner to celebrate my parents' wedding anniversary. It is a surprise, so please do not mention it to them! I can't wait to see their faces.
Anjali
Residents' meeting invitation: Saturday 6 pm in the garden, topic is cleaning the lane. 40 words, signed Ravi.

Dear residents,
You are invited to a meeting this Saturday at 6 pm in the garden. We will talk about how to keep our lane clean and share the work fairly. Every voice matters, so please come and bring your ideas.
Ravi
I'm organising a small singing evening at home on Friday. Write the invite, 40 words, in a relaxed tone. Name: Mira.

Come sing with us on Friday evening at my house! There is no stage and no judge, only good company and good songs. Bring a favourite tune, or just come to listen. Everyone is welcome.
Mira
Could you help me politely ask my school principal for permission to hold a bake sale for charity on Friday at lunch break in the courtyard? About 50 words, from Hana of Class 9.

Dear Principal,
I would like to request permission to hold a bake sale in the courtyard on Friday during lunch break. All the money will go to a local charity for children. My classmates and I will handle everything and clean up afterwards. Thank you for considering this.
Hana
Class 9
Complaint to the railway office: my train was two hours late and no announcement was made. Keep it courteous, under 55 words. Signed Mr Bose.

Dear Station Master,
My train arrived two hours late, and no announcement was made at the platform. Many passengers waited without any information. I request that announcements be made in the future. Thank you for your attention.
Mr Bose
Ask the building watchman, politely, to lock the main gate at ten every night. 35 words, from Mrs D'Souza.

Dear Watchman,
Could you please lock the main gate every night at ten o'clock? We worry about our safety when the gate is left open. Thank you for your good work and your help.
Mrs D'Souza
My neighbour's dog barks every morning at six. Write a friendly note asking whether anything can be done. 45 words. I'm Tomas.

Dear neighbour,
I love dogs, and yours is lovely. But the barking at six in the morning is waking my family. Could we think of a way to help him stay quiet? I'm happy to talk whenever suits you. Thank you for understanding.
Tomas
Write a message to a bookshop asking if they can order a cookbook called Simple Suppers for me and call me when it arrives. Around 45 words. Signed Alice Menon.

Dear Bookshop,
I am looking for a cookbook called Simple Suppers, which I could not find on your shelves. Could you please order a copy for me? Kindly call me when it arrives, and I will come to collect it. Thank you.
Alice Menon
A note to my manager, Ms Rao, asking for a day off next Monday to attend my cousin's wedding. 40 words. From Imran.

Dear Ms Rao,
I would like to request a day of leave next Monday to attend my cousin's wedding. I will complete my pending tasks before I go. Thank you for considering my request.
Imran
Our trip needs a room: send a small hill guesthouse an email asking if a double room is free for the last weekend of the month and what the rate is. 45 words, signed Rohini.

Dear Sir or Madam,
I would like to know if a double room is available at your guesthouse for the last weekend of this month. Could you please tell me the rate per night and what meals are included? I look forward to your reply.
Rohini
Write an email thanking my old teacher, Mr Kapoor, for helping me get through college. 45 words, from Sarah.

Dear Mr Kapoor,
I hope you are well. I have finished college, and I wanted to thank you. Your patience and kind advice made a real difference in those years. I still remember your lessons and often think of them. Thank you for believing in me.
Sarah
Email to the team: our Thursday meeting moves to Friday at 11 am, same room. Make it clear and short, 35 words. Sent by Deepa.

Subject: Meeting moved to Friday
Hello all,
Our Thursday meeting has been moved to Friday at 11 am. The room is the same. Please update your calendars, and let me know if you cannot attend.
Thanks,
Deepa
Email to the neighbourhood group asking who can lend a ladder for the weekend, and promise to return it clean. 35 words. Hiro.

Hello neighbours,
Does anyone have a ladder I could borrow this weekend? I will take good care of it and return it clean. Thank you very much!
Hiro
Compose a notice for the school notice board announcing that Class 8 will go on a museum trip on the twelfth, with permission slips due Monday. About 25 words.

NOTICE
Class 8 will go on a trip to the museum on the 12th. Students must bring a signed permission slip by Monday.
Notice: the community garden needs volunteers to weed the beds on Sunday morning at 8. Cheerful tone, under 45 words.

VOLUNTEERS WANTED
Our community garden is waiting for helping hands! Come and weed the flower beds this Sunday morning from 8 am. Bring a friend, enjoy the sunshine, and help our little garden bloom.
Put up a notice for the lift: it will be out of service on Wednesday for repairs. Keep it polite and short, under 40 words.

NOTICE
The lift will be out of service on Wednesday for repairs. Please use the stairs on that day. We are sorry for the inconvenience, and we thank you for your patience.
A notice asking residents not to park in front of the gate so ambulances and delivery vans can pass. 40 words.

NOTICE
Please do not park your vehicles in front of the main gate. The space must stay clear so that ambulances and delivery vans can pass. Park in the marked area instead. Thank you for your cooperation.
The annual fair runs from Friday to Sunday near the river ground. Write a poster-style notice with rides, food and music. 25 words.

ANNUAL FAIR
Friday to Sunday, near the river ground. Come for rides, tasty food and live music! Bring your friends and enjoy three days of fun.
Create a vivid word-picture of a quiet lake at sunrise, about 55 words.

The lake lies still in the early light. A thin mist floats above the water, and the sky turns pink and gold. A lone bird skims the surface, leaving small rings that spread and fade. Across the shore, the hills rise soft and blue. Everything is quiet, as if the whole world were holding its breath.
Write a description of a street-side stall frying fresh snacks, using smells and sounds. Around 55 words.

The stall sits at the corner, and you smell it long before you see it. Oil crackles in a wide pan, and golden snacks bob up to the top. The vendor shouts for customers and flips each piece with a quick hand. The smell of spice and onion drifts down the road and pulls everyone closer.
How would you describe a bedroom after a long day of rain, with clothes drying on a line and a window fogged? Give me 55 words.

The bedroom feels heavy with rain. Clothes hang from a line across the room, dripping slowly onto a towel. The window is fogged, and the outside world has turned into a grey blur. A lamp glows softly, and the quilt on the bed looks inviting. Everything smells of damp cotton and warm tea.
In 55 words, describe an elephant bathing in a river, as seen by a child on the bank.

The elephant walked into the river like a king. It sucked up water with its trunk and sprayed it over its back. Its skin shone dark and wet in the sun. A little calf splashed beside it, kicking up waves. I sat on the bank and laughed, hoping the water would reach me.
Sketch with words the lights of a city at night, seen from a rooftop. 50 words.

From the rooftop, the city glows like a field of tiny stars. Windows shine yellow, and car lights crawl along the streets in red and white lines. The sound of horns rises and fades, soft as a hum. A cool breeze brushes my face, and for a moment everything below feels calm.
Diary page about the last day of exams, 50 words, in the voice of a student named Asha, relieved but a little sad.

Dear Diary,
The last exam is finally over! I walked out of the hall feeling as light as a feather. We hugged and laughed, and everyone talked about holidays. Then I realised that we won't meet in these classrooms as often. I am relieved, but a little sad too.
Asha
Write a diary entry for the night of a festival of lights, in about 55 words. I'm Mohan, ten years old.

Dear Diary,
Tonight we lit lamps all around the house. We drew a rangoli at the door, and I helped with the colours. Then we burst a few sparklers in the yard. The sky glowed with far-off fireworks, and the whole street smelled of sweets. It was the best night of the year.
Mohan
I'd like a diary entry, around 55 words, about the day I found a bird's nest in our garden. I'm Lena.

Dear Diary,
Today I found a tiny nest in our guava tree. Three small blue eggs lay inside, soft against the twigs. I did not touch them, but I watched from far away. The mother bird returned and sat on the eggs. I will check every day, but only from a distance.
Lena
Write as Kofi: a diary page about my first long bus journey alone, 55 words, nervous at the start and happy at the end.

Dear Diary,
Today I took a long bus journey alone for the first time. I was nervous when the bus pulled away, and I held my bag tight. Then I watched green fields roll past and chatted with a kind old man next to me. By the time I arrived, I felt brave and happy.
Kofi
My first attempt at baking bread went wrong, but we ate it anyway. A diary entry about this, 50 words. Writer: Fatima.

Dear Diary,
Today I baked bread for the first time. It came out of the oven as flat and hard as a stone. My family tried a slice anyway, and we all laughed so much that we cried. Next week, I will try again with more yeast and less worry.
Fatima
Tiny tale, 55 words, about a little fox who learns to share her berries.

A little fox found a bush full of red berries. She ate and ate, then hid the rest in a hole. Winter came, and a hungry rabbit knocked on her door. At first she wanted to say no. Then she remembered how cold the snow was, and shared her berries. They ate together and kept warm.
Tell a short story, about 55 words, of an old man who plants a tree every birthday.

Every birthday, an old man planted one tree on the hill behind his house. People laughed at first and said he would never see them grow tall. Years passed, and the hill turned green. Birds came, and shade followed. On his last birthday, children sat under the oldest tree and sang for him.
I want a tiny story where a boy forgets his homework but learns an honest lesson. 60 words.

A boy forgot his homework at home. He wanted to say the dog ate it, but he knew that was not true. He stood up and told the teacher the truth. She was not angry. She asked him to bring it the next day, and he did. The boy felt lighter, because honesty is easier to carry than a lie.
A short story in 55 words about two cloud friends who disagree about the colour of the sky.

Two clouds floated side by side. The first one said, "The sky is blue." The second said, "No, it is orange!" They argued all afternoon. Then the sun began to set, and the sky slowly turned from blue to orange. They looked at each other and laughed. They were both right, only at different times.
A little story of 55 words in which two friends find a lost kite and decide to return it.

Two friends found a red kite caught in a tree. They climbed up carefully and pulled it down. It had a name written in small letters on the tail. They walked from house to house until they found a girl crying on her doorstep. She smiled when she saw her kite. They flew it together.
Write a paragraph of 55 words about why spending time in a park makes people feel cheerful.

A park is a gentle place. Green trees and open space give our eyes a rest from walls and screens. People walk, laugh and play together, and the fresh air feels light. Children run, and old friends sit on benches and chat. Spending time in a park reminds us that simple things can make us happy.
Describe in one paragraph, about 55 words, what a library feels like to someone who loves reading.

For someone who loves reading, a library feels like a calm treasure house. Shelves stand in tall rows, and each spine holds a different world. The air is quiet, and pages rustle softly. You can pick up any book and travel anywhere without leaving your chair. It feels like a place where time slows down.
Paragraph for a school newsletter: why learning an instrument teaches patience, around 55 words.

Learning an instrument teaches patience. At first, the notes sound rough and every finger feels clumsy. But with daily practice, the music slowly becomes smoother. Students learn that progress comes in small steps. They also learn to listen carefully and to accept mistakes. In time, the patience they build helps in other parts of life too.
Persuade readers in a paragraph of 55 words to take the train instead of a car for a short journey.

For a short journey, the train is often a better choice. It lets you relax, look out of the window and read a book instead of watching the road. It also uses less fuel for each passenger and avoids traffic jams. You arrive calm, and the world around you stays a little cleaner.
As a short paragraph of about 55 words, explain what a good morning routine means to me. I'm Gita and I like tea, a short walk and quiet.

For me, a good morning is calm and simple. I wake up early and make a cup of tea. Then I take a short walk around the block while the streets are still quiet. This small routine gives me peace and energy for the whole day. When I skip it, my mind feels hurried and heavy.
Write a four-line rhyme about a puppy that chases his own tail, bouncy and fun.

A puppy spun round in a circle so tight,
He chased his own tail with all of his might.
He tumbled and rolled on the grass in a heap,
Then yawned and curled up in a happy sleep.
Poem: four lines, rhyming, about the moon following a traveller home. Around 30 words.

The moon came out to walk with me,
A silver lamp above the tree.
It followed me down every lane
And waited as I reached my door again.
Rhyme about a kitchen full of sleeping spices, four lines, gentle and funny.

The cumin dreams in a quiet jar,
The pepper naps on a shelf afar.
But when the pan begins to sing,
They wake up fast and join the fling.
Can I have a short rhyme of eight lines, in pairs, about a clock that is always late? About 65 words.

The clock on the wall is always late,
It ticks along at a sleepy rate.
When morning comes it is still in bed,
While the sun climbs up above its head.
We laugh and tell it to hurry up,
It answers with a yawn and a hiccup.
But who can blame it? It works all day,
And it deserves a break, I would say.
Write a short rhyming poem, four lines, about the quiet feeling of waiting for a friend who is coming from far away.

I watch the road and count the hours,
I set the table, tidy flowers.
The sky grows soft, the lamps shine bright,
My friend will come before the night.
Tell my friend Pablo I am sorry I missed his birthday party and ask to make it up over lunch. A heartfelt text, about 40 words, from Ines.

Hi Pablo,
I am so sorry I missed your birthday party. I feel bad about it, and I wish I had been there. Let me make it up to you over lunch. You choose the place. Happy belated birthday!
Ines
Text for my aunt: thank her for the lovely sweater she knitted me. Keep it warm and about 45 words. Signed Kunal.

Dear Aunt,
Thank you so much for the lovely sweater. It fits perfectly, and the colour is my favourite. I can feel all the love you put into every stitch. I wore it as soon as I could. You are very kind.
Kunal

Dear friend,

Notice for students: the science lab is out of bounds this week without a teacher. Firm but friendly, around 40 words.

NOTICE

NOTICE

A notice about a bus route change from tomorrow: the number 14 will stop near the temple instead of the market. Short, 25 words.

NOTICE

Put out a call on the club board for new members to join the evening badminton group. Friendly, 40 words.

JOIN US!
Our evening badminton group is looking for new members. Whether you are a beginner or a seasoned player, you are welcome. Come, play, make friends and enjoy the game. Please speak to any member for details.
Describe a forest path after a night of rain, in about 50 words. Make us smell the leaves.

The forest path was soft and dark after the rain. Every leaf dripped with silver drops, and the air smelled of wet earth and green leaves. Mushrooms peeked out from under the roots. A thin mist floated between the trunks, and somewhere above, a bird shook the water from its wings.
Tell me what a hot bowl of soup tastes like on a cold evening, in 45 words, as a short description.

The soup is thick and golden, and the steam warms my face before I take a sip. It tastes of garlic and gentle pepper, and each spoonful slides down like a small hug. My fingers curl around the warm bowl. The cold evening outside feels far away.
Sketch a stallholder who sells vegetables in the early bazaar, 50 words, with a warm eye for his hands.

The vegetable seller arranges tomatoes in a neat red pyramid. His hands are quick, and his voice rings out over the noise. He weighs each bag with a smile and adds one extra chilli for luck. The morning sun lights up his baskets, and the whole stall looks like a painting.
A lonely cottage up on a hillside, viewed from the valley as evening falls: describe it in around 55 words.

Far away, a small house sits on top of the hill. At dusk, its windows glow like tiny gold coins against the darkening sky. A thin line of smoke rises from the chimney. The hill is quiet, and the first stars appear above the roof, as if the house were wearing a crown.
How does a hot summer afternoon feel in a village? Describe it in 50 words.

A hot summer afternoon in a village is very still. The sun beats down on the dusty path, and even the dogs lie quiet in the shade. Leaves hang without a flutter. Far away, a cart creaks slowly, and the air shimmers above the fields like a thin curtain of glass.
My diary for the evening before my final maths exam, nervous and a bit hopeful. Around 45 words. Written as Devika.

Dear Diary,
Tomorrow is my final maths exam. My heart is racing, and I keep opening my notebook again and again. I have studied well, and I know I can do it. I will go to bed early and trust myself. Wish me luck!
Devika
Write the diary page where I describe planting my first vegetable seeds on the balcony. 50 words. I'm Ayesha.

Dear Diary,
Today I planted my first vegetable seeds in small pots on the balcony. I pressed them into the soil and watered them gently. Now I must wait and be patient. I hope tiny green shoots will appear soon. I already feel like a proud gardener.
Ayesha
A diary page, 45 words, about making up with a friend after an argument. I'm Luca.

Dear Diary,
Today I made up with my best friend. We had not spoken for days, and it felt terrible. I walked up to him and said sorry first. He smiled and said he was sorry too. We laughed, and the heavy feeling disappeared.
Luca
Please write a diary entry about getting lost in a new city and finding help from a kind stranger. 50 words. Written by Rania.

Dear Diary,
Today I got lost in the new city. All the streets looked the same, and my phone had no signal. I was scared until a kind stranger noticed my face and showed me the way. I thanked her warmly. Kindness can turn a stranger into a friend.
Rania
Diary entry: the first day of winter, with fog on the road and a warm cup of tea. About 50 words. I'm Harsh.

Dear Diary,
Winter came today. The road was covered in thick fog, and the streetlights glowed like small moons. I wore my woollen cap and carried a warm cup of tea to the balcony. The cold nipped my nose, but the tea felt wonderful. I love this season.
Harsh
Here's the idea for a tiny story in 50 words: an ant carries a leaf ten times her size across a stream.

An ant found a leaf ten times bigger than herself. She lifted it and marched towards the stream. The water was wide, and the other ants watched. She laid the leaf on the water, climbed onto it and floated across. On the far bank, she cheered, and the colony cheered with her.
A tiny story of about 50 words about a girl who is afraid to speak in class and finds her voice.

A girl sat at the back and never spoke in class. Her heart pounded whenever the teacher looked at her. One day, the teacher asked a question that she knew well. Slowly, she raised her hand and answered. Her voice shook, but it came out clear. The class clapped, and she smiled.
Write a tiny story, about 50 words, about a fisherman who returns a very small fish to the sea.

At dawn, a fisherman pulled up his net and found one very tiny fish inside. It looked up at him with round eyes. He smiled, lifted it gently and returned it to the sea. The little fish flashed away. That evening, he went home with a light basket and a lighter heart.
Spin a gentle tale, about 55 words, about a river that wanted to see the sea.

A little river began on a hill and wondered where it would end. It ran past rocks and fields and villages, asking every stone about the sea. Nobody knew. Then one day, the land opened wide, and the river saw something huge and blue. It rushed forward, and the sea welcomed it home.
A short tale in 55 words about a student who finds a lost pencil box and returns it to the owner.

At the end of the day, a student found a pencil box under a bench. Inside were bright pens and a small eraser shaped like a fish. She thought about keeping it, but then she saw a name on the lid. Next morning, she handed it to its owner, who smiled and said thank you.
In about 50 words, as a paragraph, tell what makes a rainy Sunday perfect.

A rainy Sunday is perfect when there is nowhere to go. The sound of rain on the roof makes the house feel cosy. You can read a book, sip hot tea and listen to old songs. Nobody hurries, and time moves slowly. By evening, the whole day feels like a gentle pause.
Tell children, in a paragraph of 55 words, why saving a little coin each week teaches a good habit.

Saving a little each week teaches us patience. When you put a coin in a jar, you wait for it to grow into something bigger. You learn that small amounts add up, and that you can plan for a future wish. It also helps you think before you spend. A small habit can become a strong one.
A paragraph of about 55 words on why we should look up from our screens to talk to the people around us.

Screens are useful, but people matter more. When we look up from our devices, we see the faces around us. A smile, a joke or a quiet talk can make someone's day brighter. Real conversations help us understand each other and build strong bonds. So now and then, put the screen down and say hello.
Short paragraph, 55 words: what I like best about walking in my city early in the morning. Written by Arman.

My favourite time to walk in the city is early morning. The streets are quiet, and the air is fresher than at any other hour. Shopkeepers lift their shutters, and the first tea of the day steams on the corner. I love feeling that the city belongs to me before it wakes up.
In 50 words, a paragraph on how reading a little every day improves the mind. Use simple words.

Reading a little every day helps the mind grow. You learn new words and find new ideas. Stories help you imagine different lives, and facts help you understand the world. Even ten minutes a day makes a difference. Over time, reading becomes a friend that makes you wiser and calmer.
Write a rhyme of four lines about a sleepy owl who stays up too late.

A sleepy owl sat in a tree,
And stayed up late till half past three.
At dawn he yawned, "I need a rest!"
And went to bed in his cosy nest.
Please compose a short poem, about 40 words, about a river that never stops singing.

The river sings from hill to plain,
A song of stones and summer rain.
It never pauses, never sleeps,
And all along the shore it keeps
A silver rhythm, soft and low,
As through the valley it will flow.
Something light: a four-line rhyme about a plate of hot jalebi disappearing in a minute.

A plate of jalebi, golden and sweet,
Arrived on the table as a treat.
We looked away for a second or two,
And the plate was bare. We had no clue.
Four-line poem needed: lamps lighting up the street during a festival night. Gentle and joyful.

Little lamps along the street,
Glow like stars beneath our feet.
Every doorway shines with light,
And joy begins to fill the night.
Write a short rhyming verse, around 45 words, about being brave on the first day at a new place.

My heart goes thump, my steps are slow,
I do not know the way to go.
But I will smile and take a chance,
And soon my fear will learn to dance.
A friendly face will say hello,
And then I'll feel the courage grow.
A funny five-line limerick about an umbrella that hates the rain.

An umbrella who hated the rain
Said, "Every drop gives me a pain!"
He grumbled all day,
Then hid far away,
And wished for the sun on the plain.
Pin a reminder on the fridge for my brother Sahil: take out the rubbish before he leaves and lock the door. About 30 words, from Maya.

Sahil,
Please take out the rubbish before you leave today. Don't forget to lock the door behind you. Thank you for remembering.

Our evening walking club meets at the gate at 6 pm. Come and walk with us, share a chat and enjoy the evening air.
Write a notice that a stray puppy has been fed and sheltered in the parking area and neighbours should be gentle. 30 words.

NOTICE
A stray puppy is being fed and sheltered in the parking area. Please be gentle with the little one and do not scare it. Thank you for your kindness.
Notice: a bhajan evening on Thursday in the temple courtyard. Short and welcoming, 25 words.

BHAJAN EVENING
A bhajan evening will be held on Thursday in the temple courtyard. Come and sing, or simply listen in peace. Everyone is welcome.
Describe an old wooden door with peeling blue paint, in 55 words, as if it had stories to tell.

The old wooden door stands at the end of the lane, its blue paint peeling like dry leaves. Its handle is worn smooth by countless hands. It creaks a long, slow hello whenever it opens. If it could speak, it would tell of children running in, travellers leaving and festivals coming and going.
Describe a field of sunflowers on a bright day, in 50 words. Make it feel cheerful.

A field of sunflowers stretches to the horizon, every flower turned to the sun. Their golden faces seem to smile at the sky. Bees hum from bloom to bloom, and a light breeze sets the whole field swaying like a happy crowd. Standing among them, you feel small and warm.
Write what a small railway station in the hills looks like in the afternoon, about 50 words.

The little station sits quietly among the hills. A single bench faces the empty tracks, and a stray dog naps in the sun. Pine trees whisper behind the red roof. Now and then, the stationmaster steps out and looks down the line. Time feels slow here, and nobody minds.
Give a lively description of a flower market at five in the morning, 50 words.

Before sunrise, the flower market is already busy. Mountains of marigolds glow orange under bright lights. Sellers shout prices, and buyers bargain with sleepy smiles. Roses, jasmine and tuberose fill the air with scent. Garlands are strung at lightning speed, and every pair of hands is wet with morning dew.
What does a cricket ground feel like just before the match begins? Describe it in 50 words.

The ground is hushed before the first ball. The grass is freshly cut and shining, and the white lines are sharp. Players stretch and chat quietly while the umpires check the stumps. In the stands, the crowd waits with a deep, happy buzz. Everyone knows that the game is about to begin.
Diary of a school day when it rained so hard that classes ended early. I'm writing as Pranav, about 45 words.

Dear Diary,
It rained so hard today that the school sent us home early. Water filled the playground like a pond, and we jumped in the puddles on the way out. My shoes were soaked, but I didn't mind. It felt like a surprise holiday.
Pranav
Diary: the first time I cooked dinner for my family on my own. Around 45 words. I am Jyoti.

Dear Diary,
Today I cooked dinner for my family all by myself. I was nervous, and I burned the first roti. But the dal turned out well, and everyone had a second helping. They smiled and said they were proud. I felt very grown-up tonight.
Jyoti
A diary page from a camping trip under the stars, around 45 words. Written by Pedro.

Dear Diary,
We camped in the hills tonight. After dinner, we lay on our backs and watched the sky. There were so many stars that I couldn't count them. A cool breeze blew, and the campfire crackled softly. I want to remember this night forever.
Pedro
Write a diary entry, 45 words, about missing my best friend who moved to another town. I'm Nisha.

Dear Diary,
I miss my best friend so much. Today I passed the bench where we used to sit and share snacks. It felt empty without her. I wrote her a long letter and put it in the post box. I hope she writes back soon.
Nisha
My grandfather told our whole street about a good deed done by a stranger. Write a diary page about that evening in about 45 words. I'm Amit.

Dear Diary,
This evening, my grandfather gathered the whole street and told us about a stranger who returned his lost wallet. He said that kindness still lives in the world. Everyone listened quietly. Afterwards, we all felt a little warmer and a little better.
Amit
A crow and a snail are the heroes of a tiny story. Write it in about 55 words, with a gentle ending.

A crow saw a snail crawling slowly across the road. "You are too slow," said the crow. The snail replied, "Yes, but I will get there." The crow laughed and flew off. By evening, the crow was tired and hungry, while the snail reached the garden fence and found a fresh green leaf.
Tell a story of 50 words about a grandmother's old sewing box that holds a surprise.

A girl found her grandmother's old sewing box in the attic. Inside were colourful threads, a silver thimble and a folded note. The note said, "Make something with love, and it will never wear out." The girl smiled, took out a needle and began to sew her first little pillow.
Tiny story for a bedtime, about 50 words, about a firefly who wanted to light up the whole forest.

A little firefly wished to light up the whole forest. She flew high and glowed with all her might, but the forest stayed dark. She felt small and sad. Then other fireflies joined her, one by one. Together, they filled the trees with soft golden light, and she smiled.
I'm after a short tale, around 55 words, about a bus conductor who helps a lost child find home.

A bus conductor noticed a small child sitting alone, holding a toy. The boy was crying. The conductor knelt, spoke gently and asked where he lived. The child remembered the name of a market. At the next stop, the conductor walked him to the market, where his mother ran forward and held him tight.
Share a very short story in 50 words about a class pet hamster that goes missing and is found.

One morning, the class hamster was missing from its cage. Everyone searched under desks and behind shelves. Finally, a student heard a tiny squeak inside a bag. The hamster had curled up in a woollen cap. The children laughed and promised to close the cage door every day.
Write one paragraph, 55 words, about why trees are like quiet friends.

Trees are like quiet friends. They give us shade when the sun is harsh and fruit when we are hungry. They hold the soil in place and give homes to birds. They never ask for anything, and they stand with us year after year. All we have to do is look after them in return.
Explain in one paragraph of around 55 words why playing a team game teaches us to share.

Playing a team game teaches us to share. A player who keeps the ball alone rarely wins, so we learn to pass it to someone better placed. We cheer for our teammates, and we accept that everyone has a turn. The joy of a shared goal is greater than the joy of a single player.
Tell me, in 50 words, why a family dinner together is worth protecting.

A family dinner is worth protecting because it is a moment when everyone slows down. We share food and talk about our day. Even a simple meal feels special when we eat together. Children learn from the conversation, and adults learn from the children. These small evenings become our warmest memories.
Why does gardening make people patient and calm? Answer in a 50-word paragraph.

Gardening teaches patience. A seed does not grow in a day, so a gardener learns to wait. Watering, weeding and watching become a quiet routine. The work is gentle, and the mind slows down among the green leaves. When the first flower opens, all the waiting feels worth it.
I'd like a paragraph of 55 words about what happens in a town when the power goes out and everyone steps outside.

When the power goes out in a small town, people step outside to see what is happening. Neighbours who rarely meet stand together under the stars. Someone lights a candle, and someone else shares a joke. The dark makes everyone friendly. When the lights return, people go back in, but the warmth lingers.
A rhyme of eight lines on a little fish who is learning to read, funny and bright.

A little fish who wished to read
Swam off to find the books he'd need.
He tried a shell, he tried a stone,
But none would let him read alone.
At last he found a bubble clear,
With words that floated far and near.
He read each one and learned it well,
And now he has a tale to tell.
A bedtime verse, four lines, with the moon saying goodnight to the sleepy town.

The moon looks down on the sleepy town,
And gently turns the lamplight down.
Goodnight, goodnight, the windows say,
And dream till the dawn of a new day.
A short poem in four lines about a street musician whose song makes people stop and smile.

A street musician sang one day,
And busy people slowed their way.
They paused and listened, then they smiled,
As if the music were a child.
A friendship rhyme in six lines, around 40 words, about two friends who share an umbrella.

Two friends walked home in the pouring rain,
With one umbrella to share.
They giggled and splashed all down the lane,
Half-wet, but they did not care.
A friend is a shelter in any weather,
And two wet friends are better together.
A playful four-line poem about the wind making the kites dance.

The wind came out to play today,
And made the kites all dance and sway.
It tickled trees and teased a hat,
Then spun around and ran off, just like that.

Leave a note on the kitchen table for my flatmate Tara. Facts: the milk is finished, I am going to the shop at the corner to buy more and will be back in ten minutes, and her parcel is waiting on the shelf in the hall. Signed Nikhil. Roughly 45 words.

Tara,
The milk is finished, so I am going to the shop at the corner to buy more. I will be back in ten minutes. Your parcel is waiting for you on the shelf in the hall, so please take it when you pass.
Nikhil
Text for my friend Lucia, about 40 words: her book is back in my bag, I finished it last night, I loved the ending, and I can hand it over when we meet at college on Monday. Sender is Param.

Hi Lucia,
I finished your book last night, and I loved the ending. It is back in my bag now, safe and clean. I can hand it over when we meet at college on Monday. Thank you for lending it to me.
Param

Short message from Hamza to his team: the printer on the second floor is broken, the technician has been called and will come this afternoon, and everyone should email files to Ms Rao instead for printing. 40 words.

Hi team,
The printer on the second floor is broken. The technician has been called and will come this afternoon. Until it is repaired, please email your files to Ms Rao instead, and she will print them for you.
Hamza

Write a sticky note from Grandma Rosa to her grandson Eli before school: his lunch is in the blue box on the counter, his jacket is on the chair, and the umbrella beside it should go with him because it may rain. About 45 words.

Eli,
Your lunch is in the blue box on the counter. Your jacket is on the chair, and the umbrella beside it should go with you, because it may rain. Please do not forget any of them. Have a good day at school.
Grandma Rosa

Note for the neighbour Mr Dutta from Shalini, around 40 words: his newspaper landed at our door by mistake this morning, I have placed it on his doormat, and I hope he does not mind the trouble. Also say I wish him a good day.

Dear Mr Dutta,
Your newspaper landed at our door by mistake this morning. I have placed it on your doormat, so please pick it up when you can. I hope you do not mind the trouble. I wish you a good day.
Shalini

Invite the whole class to a quiz night in the school hall at 6 pm on Friday. Snacks are free, teams have four players, and everyone should come with a team of friends. It comes from the Quiz Club. About 45 words.

You are invited to a quiz night in the school hall! It starts at 6 pm on Friday. Teams have four players, so please come with a team of friends. Snacks are free for everyone. We hope to see the whole class there.
The Quiz Club
Please write a housewarming invitation to friends from Joseph and Anita: new flat, Sunday at 4 pm, tea and samosas, no gifts. Around 35 words.

Dear friends,
We have moved into our new flat, and we would love to have you over. Please join us on Sunday at 4 pm for tea and samosas. Please do not bring gifts.
Joseph and Anita
A farewell tea for Mr Ghosh, who retires after thirty years at the library. Draft the invitation, 35 words. The place is the library garden, the time is 3 pm, and it comes from the staff.

Mr Ghosh is retiring after thirty years at the library, and we would like you to join us for a farewell tea. It will be held in the library garden at 3 pm.
The Staff
Write a short invitation to my daughter's naming ceremony for our relatives. It is at our house at 11 am, lunch will follow, and the baby is called Aarna. Signed Reema and Dev. 35 words.

Dear relatives,
We are happy to invite you to the naming ceremony of our daughter, Aarna. It will be held at our house at 11 am, and lunch will follow.
Reema and Dev
Neighbours are invited to a cleanliness drive in the lane at 7 am; gloves and bags will be provided; bring a broom if you have one. Please word it in about 35 words, from the Lane Committee.

Dear neighbours,
The Lane Committee invites you to a cleanliness drive in our lane at 7 am. Gloves and bags will be provided. If you have a broom, please bring it.
The Lane Committee
Politely ask the bus conductor to stop at the temple gate, because my grandmother is with me and cannot walk far, and say thank you at the end and wish him a good day. About 40 words.

Excuse me, could you please stop the bus at the temple gate? My grandmother is travelling with me, and she cannot walk far. It would be a great help to us. Thank you very much, and I wish you a good day.
Complain to the shop owner: the shoes I bought have a torn sole after one use, and I want a replacement. Polite but firm, 40 words. From Imran.

Dear Shop Owner,
The shoes I bought from your shop have a torn sole after only one use. I want a replacement. This is not what I expected from a new pair, and I ask you to treat it seriously.
Imran

My upstairs neighbour plays drums in the afternoon while my baby naps. Compose a kind request to keep the noise low during the nap, mention that the baby sleeps after lunch, and thank them. 45 words, from Mei.

Dear neighbour,
I can hear your drums in the afternoon while my baby naps. My baby sleeps after lunch, and the noise wakes her. Could you please keep the noise low during the nap? I would be very grateful for your kindness. Thank you for understanding.
Mei
Ask the librarian for a quiet corner table for me and two classmates to revise for our exam, and say we will leave it tidy and speak softly. Polite, around 40 words. I'm Zainab.

Dear Librarian,
My two classmates and I would like to revise for our exam. May we please use a quiet corner table? We will speak softly and leave the table tidy when we go. Thank you very much for your help.
Zainab
Write to the cafe manager: the bill charged us for two coffees but we ordered one coffee and one tea at lunch. Ask for a corrected bill, politely, and thank him. 40 words. Sender: Gaurav.

Dear Manager,
We had lunch at your cafe today. The bill charged us for two coffees, but we ordered one coffee and one tea. Could you please give us a corrected bill? Thank you for looking into this, and for your kind service.
Gaurav
Email to my landlord: the tap in the bathroom drips all day and night, the sound keeps me awake, and I want it fixed this week. Add a subject line, about 40 words. From Priyanka Nair.

Subject: Dripping bathroom tap

Dear Landlord,
The tap in my bathroom drips all day and night, and the sound keeps me awake. I would like it to be fixed this week. Please let me know when someone can come. Thank you for your attention.
Priyanka Nair
Email my teacher Mr Lobo to say I will miss the maths test on Monday because of a family wedding in another city, apologise, and ask for another date. Subject line too, 40 words, from Aditi.

Subject: Missing the maths test

Dear Mr Lobo,
I will miss the maths test on Monday because of a family wedding in another city. I am sorry for the trouble. Could I please take the test on another date? Thank you for your understanding.
Aditi

Compose an email to a hotel that confirms my booking for two guests is under the name Bianchi, and asks whether breakfast is included and what time it is served. Subject line please, about 45 words. Sign off with Thank you.

Subject: Booking for two guests

Dear Hotel Team,
I would like to confirm that my booking for two guests is under the name Bianchi. Could you also tell me whether breakfast is included, and what time it is served? I look forward to your reply.
Thank you.
Email for my colleague Farida: the budget sheet is attached, she should check the totals before the meeting, and she should tell me if anything looks wrong. From Sam, 35 words, with a subject line.

Subject: Budget sheet

Hi Farida,
I have attached the budget sheet. Please check the totals before the meeting. If anything looks wrong, please tell me, and I will correct it. Thank you for your help with this.
Sam

I need an email to the gym to pause my membership for a while because my knee is injured, and to ask what steps I must take and whether there is a form. Subject line, around 45 words, from Rajesh Menon.

Subject: Pausing my membership

Dear Gym Team,
I would like to pause my membership for a while because my knee is injured. Could you please tell me what steps I must take, and whether there is a form to fill in? Thank you for your help.
Rajesh Menon
Notice for the society board: the water tank will be cleaned on the 12th, supply stops from 10 am to 2 pm, and residents should store water in advance and use it carefully. 40 words.

NOTICE
The water tank will be cleaned on the 12th. The water supply will stop from 10 am to 2 pm. Residents are requested to store water in advance and to use it carefully. Thank you for your cooperation.
Put up a notice that the school canteen will be closed on Thursday for repairs, students should bring their own tiffin that day, and the canteen will open again on Friday. About 35 words.

NOTICE
The school canteen will be closed on Thursday for repairs. Students are asked to bring their own tiffin that day. The canteen will open again on Friday. We thank everyone for their patience and cooperation.
Park notice, short and firm, 45 words: dogs must be on a leash, owners must clean up after them, the gate closes at 8 pm, and people who break the rules will be asked to leave.

NOTICE
Dogs must be kept on a leash in this park. Owners must clean up after their dogs. The park gate closes at 8 pm. Anyone who breaks these rules will be asked to leave. Please help us keep the park clean and safe.
Lost-and-found notice in 35 words: a red umbrella was found near the bus stop on Tuesday, and the owner may collect it from the tea stall by describing it. Ask people to share the notice.

FOUND
A red umbrella was found near the bus stop on Tuesday. The owner may collect it from the tea stall by describing it. If you know whose umbrella it is, please share this notice with them.
Library notice, around 40 words: books must come back before the shelves are counted, late books cost five rupees per day, and the reading room must stay silent. Thank readers at the end.

NOTICE
All books must be returned before the shelves are counted. Late books will cost five rupees per day. Please keep silence in the reading room so that everyone can read in peace. Thank you for your cooperation.
Describe my grandfather's armchair in 40 words: brown leather, cracked on the arms, smells of old books, squeaks when you sit, and it stands by the window.

My grandfather's armchair stands by the window. It is made of brown leather, and the arms are cracked. The chair smells of old books. When you sit down in it, it gives a loud squeak, as if it were greeting you.
Short description of a rainy bus stop, about 40 words: puddles on the road, steam from a tea stall, people holding umbrellas, and a bus coming slowly through the rain.

At the rainy bus stop, puddles cover the road. Steam rises from the tea stall, and people stand close together holding umbrellas. A bus comes slowly through the rain, and everyone looks up to see whether it is theirs.
Four sentences describing a mango, about 40 words: golden skin, sweet smell, soft and juicy inside, and a big seed in the middle. Make it sound like summer.
The mango has golden skin that glows like the summer sun. Its sweet smell fills the whole room. Inside, it is soft and juicy, and every bite tastes of summer. In the middle, there is one big seed.
How would you describe the reading corner of our community library in 40 words? It has thirty chairs, a green rug, a window facing the garden and a plant on the front desk. Make it feel calm.
The reading corner is a calm place. It has thirty chairs and a green rug. A window faces the garden, so soft light falls on the books. There is a plant on the front desk, and the room is quiet.
Write a short description of a lighthouse, 40 words: white tower, red top, waves hitting the rocks, a light that turns at dusk, and a lonely spot on a cliff, and ships that are guided home by it.
The lighthouse stands alone on a cliff. It is a white tower with a red top. Waves hit the rocks below it. At dusk, its light begins to turn, and it guides the ships safely home across the dark water.

Diary entry for today about my first time at the swimming pool, around 35 words: I was scared of the deep water, the coach held my hands, I floated for a few seconds, and I felt proud. Write as Kavya.

Dear Diary,
Today I went to the swimming pool for the first time. I was scared of the deep water. The coach held my hands, and I floated for a few seconds. I felt proud.
Kavya
Neel wants a diary page about the power cut this evening: we lit candles, the family played cards, dinner was by candlelight, and it felt cosy. Keep it to about 35 words.

Dear Diary,
There was a power cut this evening. We lit candles, and the family played cards. We even ate dinner by candlelight, and it felt cosy. I wish every evening could be like this.
Neel
Write today's diary lines from Tomas, about 35 words: he planted tomato seeds in a pot, watered them, put the pot on the balcony where the sun comes in, and is excited to see them grow.

Dear Diary,
Today I planted tomato seeds in a pot. I watered them and put the pot on the balcony, where the sun comes in. Now I must wait, and I am excited to see them grow.
Tomas
Anjali's diary for today, 35 words: she found a kitten crying under a car near her house, gave it milk, carried it home in her scarf, and her heart felt warm.

Dear Diary,
Today I found a kitten crying under a car near my house. I gave it some milk and carried it home in my scarf. It stopped crying and fell asleep, and my heart felt warm.
Anjali
Chen's diary page for today, 35 words: I lost the school chess final, shook hands with the winner, still feel sad, and want to practise more every evening.

Dear Diary,
Today I lost the school chess final. I shook hands with the winner, but I still feel sad. I want to practise more every evening, so that I can play better next time.
Chen
Tiny story, about 35 words: a thirsty crow finds a jug with a little water, cannot reach it, drops pebbles in one by one, and drinks.
A thirsty crow found a jug with a little water in it. He could not reach the water. So he dropped pebbles into the jug, one by one. The water rose, and the crow drank.
Tiny story for a child, 35 words: a little snail wants to see the sea, travels slowly past the garden gate, rests under a leaf at noon, and finally reaches the sand.
