A little snail wanted to see the sea. She travelled slowly past the garden gate. At noon, she rested under a leaf. Then she went on again. Finally, she reached the sand and saw the sea.
Short story in about 35 words about a girl named Pia who finds a key in her coat pocket, tries it on the old trunk in the attic, and finds a photograph inside.
Pia put her hand in her coat pocket and found a key. She carried it up to the attic and tried it on the old trunk. The lock opened with a click. Inside, she found a photograph.
A tiny story in 35 words: two friends, Bao and Jaya, argue about whose kite flies higher, then their strings tangle, and they sort them out together and fly both kites again.
Bao and Jaya argued about whose kite flew higher. Then the wind blew, and their strings tangled. Neither of them could fly a kite now. So they sorted out the knots together and flew both kites again.
Tiny story, around 35 words, about a lonely lamp post that glows on a foggy street at night and guides a lost dog home.
A lonely lamp post stood on a foggy street at night. A lost dog wandered by, shivering and unsure of the way. The lamp post glowed softly, and the dog followed its light all the way home.
Give me a paragraph of 45 words on why walking is a good habit: it is free, it clears the head, and you notice your neighbourhood.

Walking is a good habit for several reasons. It is free, so anyone can do it at any time. It also clears the head after a busy day. When you walk, you notice your neighbourhood in a way you never do from a vehicle.
A paragraph of about 45 words on why a good umbrella matters: it keeps you dry, it keeps your bag dry, and it works in sun as well as rain.
A good umbrella matters because it keeps you dry when the rain comes down. It also keeps your bag dry, so your books stay safe. It works in the sun as well as in the rain, so you can use it all year.
Short paragraph on the joy of cooking for friends, 40 words: chopping together, the smell of spices, laughing at the table.

Cooking for friends is a joy. First, you chop the vegetables together and talk as you work. Then the smell of spices fills the kitchen. At last, you all sit down at the table and laugh over the meal you made.
Paragraph, 40 words, explaining why we should switch off lights when leaving a room: it saves electricity, lowers the bill, and helps the planet.

We should switch off the lights when we leave a room. It saves electricity, because the bulb is not using power for nothing. It lowers the bill that a family pays each month. It also helps the planet.
Compose a paragraph about the sound of rain on a tin roof, 40 words: steady drumming, a cosy feeling, makes you want to sleep.
The rain makes a steady drumming sound on a tin roof. Inside, the sound gives a cosy feeling, as if the whole house were wrapped in a blanket. It slowly makes you want to close your eyes and sleep.
Six rhyming lines, please, about a sleepy cat that loves the sun on the windowsill; about 45 words.

A sleepy cat lay in the sun so bright,
She purred and blinked in golden light.
Her fur was warm, her whiskers still,
She stayed all day upon her sunny sill.
The sun moved slowly across the sky,
And she slept on while the hours went by.
Three rhyming couplets for a children's toothbrush song, about 40 words; mention the front and the back, and sugar bugs.

Brush your teeth, up and down,
Chase the sugar bugs from town.
Brush the front and brush the back,
Keep your smile upon the track.
Brush each morning, brush at night,
Make your teeth all clean and bright.
I'd like a six-line rhyme about the moon following a train, 45 words.

The moon kept pace beside the train,
It glided over field and lane.
It followed on from town to town,
And never once did it slow down.
The train rolled on into the night,
And the moon went with it, round and bright.
Six rhyming lines about children jumping in monsoon puddles, around 35 words.

Splish, splash, the rain came down,
Puddles gathered all through town.
Jump with a hop and a happy shout,
Watch the water splash about.
Boots are wet and socks are too,
Monsoon fun for me and you.
A rhyme about a tea kettle that bubbles and whistles, six lines, 40 words.

The kettle bubbles, hot and loud,
It whistles like a happy crowd.
The steam goes up, the water's done,
Now tea is ready, everyone.
Pour it out and share the cheer,
A cup of tea brings friends right here.

Draft a quick text to my cousin Leela: I'm stuck in traffic on the way to the cinema, I will be ten minutes late, I have the tickets with me, and she should start the film without me. From Arun. About 45 words.

Hi Leela,
I am stuck in traffic on the way to the cinema, so I will be ten minutes late. I have the tickets with me. Please go in and start the film without me, and I will join you as soon as I can.
Arun
Fridge note from Dev for his roommates Hari and Sam, about 35 words: the leftover pasta is for lunch tomorrow, and the cake must not be eaten because it is for a birthday party on Saturday.

Hari and Sam,
The leftover pasta is for lunch tomorrow, so please help yourselves. Please do not eat the cake, because it is for a birthday party on Saturday. Thank you both for leaving it alone.
Dev
Thank-you note to the postman Mr Gill, who brings parcels to our door on the third floor even when the lift is broken. Around 30 words, from the Sharma family.

Dear Mr Gill,
Thank you for bringing our parcels to our door on the third floor, even when the lift is broken. We really appreciate your effort.
The Sharma family
A get-well message for my teammate Colin, who hurt his ankle in football. Warm and brief, 30 words. It is from the whole team.

Dear Colin,
We were sorry to hear that you hurt your ankle in football. We are thinking of you and wish you a quick recovery. Rest well.
The whole team
Apology message for forgetting Naina's birthday: I was careless, I feel bad, and I want to make it up to her with dinner. About 30 words. I'm Vikram.

Dear Naina,
I am sorry that I forgot your birthday. I was careless, and I feel bad about it. I would like to make it up to you with dinner.
Vikram
Write a note inviting my teacher Ms Pereira to our class farewell party in the auditorium at 2 pm. It comes from the students of class 10.

Dear Ms Pereira,
The students of class 10 invite you to our farewell party in the auditorium at 2 pm. We would be honoured by your presence.
The students of class 10
A kite-flying invitation for the street's children and parents: bring your own kite, flat ground near the river, 4 pm on Sunday, snacks for everyone, from Uncle Raju. About 40 words.

Dear children and parents,
Please join us for kite flying on the flat ground near the river at 4 pm on Sunday. Bring your own kite. There will be snacks for everyone. Come and enjoy a happy evening with us.
Uncle Raju

Wedding anniversary dinner invitation, 40 words: twenty-five years together, dinner at the Lotus Hall at 7:30 pm on Saturday, hosts Mala and Suresh, traditional dress, and ask friends to come and share the joy.

Mala and Suresh are celebrating twenty-five years together, and they would love you to come and share the joy. Please join them for dinner at the Lotus Hall at 7:30 pm on Saturday. The dress code is traditional.
My book club meets at my flat to discuss a mystery novel on Friday evening at 7. Invite the members, tell them tea is provided and to bring their copy, about 40 words, from Hira.

Dear members,
Our book club will meet at my flat on Friday at 7 in the evening to discuss our mystery novel. Tea will be provided. Please bring your own copy of the book, and come ready to share your guesses.
Hira
An invitation to a rooftop stargazing evening for neighbours at 8 pm on Saturday, binoculars welcome, hot cocoa on offer, from Mr Bose. 40 words.

Dear neighbours,
Please join me on the rooftop for a stargazing evening at 8 pm on Saturday. Binoculars are welcome if you have them. I will offer hot cocoa to everyone. I hope to see you all under the stars.
Mr Bose
I need to politely ask my manager Ms Fernandes for half a day off to attend my sister's graduation. Email format with a subject line, 30 words, from Tarun.

Subject: Request for half a day off

Dear Ms Fernandes,
I would like to request half a day off to attend my sister's graduation. Thank you for considering my request.
Tarun
Our building lift is stuck again. Write a complaint to the secretary asking for a repair this week and mentioning that elderly residents struggle on the stairs. About 40 words, from Flat 4B.

Dear Secretary,
The lift in our building is stuck again. Elderly residents struggle on the stairs, and they find it very hard to go up and down. I request you to have the lift repaired this week. Thank you for your help.
Flat 4B
The food delivery arrived cold and the dessert was missing. Write a calm complaint to the restaurant asking for a refund of the dessert only, and thank them for reading. 40 words. Sender is Lakshmi.

Dear Restaurant Team,
My food delivery arrived cold today, and the dessert was missing from the bag. I would like a refund for the dessert only. I am writing calmly, and I hope you will look into this. Thank you for reading.
Lakshmi
Politely ask a classmate named Pooja to lend me her science notes for a day because I missed the lesson on Tuesday, and say I will return them tomorrow. I'm Ali. 40 words.

Hi Pooja,
Could you please lend me your science notes for a day? I missed the lesson on Tuesday, and I would like to catch up. I will return them tomorrow. Thank you so much for helping me.
Ali

Write a firm but polite request to the landlord not to enter the flat without informing me first, because it is a matter of privacy, and ask him to call or message before he comes. Around 40 words. From Ms Das.

Dear Landlord,
I request you not to enter my flat without informing me first. This is a matter of privacy. Please call or message me before you come, and I will be glad to arrange a time. I would appreciate your understanding.
Ms Das
Draft an email to the bank branch manager asking for a new passbook because mine is full, and ask what to do next. Subject line, 35 words, from Meenakshi Rao.

Subject: Request for a new passbook

Dear Branch Manager,
My passbook is full, so I would like to request a new one. Could you please tell me what to do next?
Meenakshi Rao
Please email the course organiser: I would like to join the pottery class, I have never tried pottery, and I need to know the fee. Subject included, about 30 words. From Gina.

Subject: Joining the pottery class

Dear Course Organiser,
I would like to join the pottery class. I have never tried pottery before. Could you please tell me the fee?
Gina

Write an email to our supplier saying the last delivery had five broken plates and asking for replacements this week. and say we will keep the broken ones for you to see. Subject, 40 words. Signed Omar.

Subject: Broken plates in the last delivery

Dear Supplier,
We checked the last delivery, and it had five broken plates. Could you please send five replacements this week? We will keep the broken ones for you to see. Thank you for your help.
Omar
Email to a friend overseas, about 35 words: my new job is going well, I miss our long chats, and I would like to video-call soon, maybe next weekend. I am Elena and he is Marcus.

Subject: Hello from me

Dear Marcus,
I hope you are well. My new job is going well, and I am enjoying it. I miss our long chats very much. Would you like to video-call soon, maybe next weekend?
Elena

A cover email for a job application as a junior designer, addressed to the Hiring Manager: my CV and portfolio are attached and I am available for an interview. Subject line, 30 words, from Ritu Bansal.

Subject: Application for junior designer

Dear Hiring Manager,
I am applying for the post of junior designer. My CV and portfolio are attached, and I am available for an interview.
Ritu Bansal
For the temple committee, a notice that the evening aarti is moved to 6:30 pm from now on, devotees should note the new time, and the morning aarti stays the same. 35 words.

NOTICE
The evening aarti is moved to 6:30 pm from now on. Devotees are requested to note the new time and to arrive a little early. The morning aarti stays the same.
The Temple Committee
Cinema club notice, about 35 words: a film show in the hall on Saturday at 5 pm, entry free, bring your own cushion, and everyone is welcome.

NOTICE
The cinema club will hold a film show in the hall on Saturday at 5 pm. Entry is free, and everyone is welcome. Please bring your own cushion. We hope to see many of you there.
A school notice, 40 words: students must wear the white uniform on Monday because of a photo session, and they should come in time for it, with their uniforms clean and neat.

NOTICE
All students must wear the white uniform on Monday because of a photo session. Please come to school in time for it, and keep your uniform clean and neat. Please follow this instruction without fail, and thank you for your cooperation.
Put a notice on the lift door in 35 words: close the door fully after use, and do not load more than six people. Also say the lift is for residents only, and thank everyone.

NOTICE
Please close the lift door fully after use. Do not load more than six people at a time. The lift is for residents only. Thank you for using the lift with care and for your cooperation.
Notice for visitors of the hospital garden, about 40 words: visiting hours end at 7 pm, keep silence, do not pluck flowers, and keep the paths clear. Add a line of thanks.

NOTICE
Visiting hours in the hospital garden end at 7 pm. Please keep silence, so that patients can rest. Do not pluck the flowers. Please keep the paths clear for everyone who walks here. Thank you for your cooperation.
Describe a busy railway platform in about 35 words: whistles, tea sellers calling, bags piled up, a train arriving, and people hurrying to the door with their bags.

The railway platform is busy. Whistles blow, and tea sellers call out to the crowd. Bags are piled up everywhere. A train is arriving, and people hurry towards the door with their bags in their hands.
How about a short portrait of an old teacher in 40 words: silver hair, round glasses, a soft voice, chalk on his sleeves, a kind smile, and a gentle way of walking.
The old teacher has silver hair and round glasses. His voice is soft, and there is chalk on his sleeves. He walks gently between the desks, and when he looks at his students, he has a kind smile.
Describe the smell of a bakery in the morning in 35 words: warm bread, butter, sugar, a little cinnamon, and it makes people hungry.

In the morning, the bakery smells of warm bread and butter. There is the sweetness of sugar and a little cinnamon in the air. The smell drifts into the street and makes everyone who passes feel hungry.
Please describe a river at sunset, about 35 words: orange water, a boat drifting, birds flying home, and a cool breeze.
At sunset, the river turns orange. A boat drifts slowly across the water. Birds fly home above it, and a cool breeze blows over the bank. The whole river looks calm, and the day seems to rest.
Describe my little sister's room, 40 words: pink curtains, a shelf of dolls, stars on the ceiling, a small desk, and it is always tidy.
My little sister's room has pink curtains and a shelf of dolls. There are stars on the ceiling and a small desk by the wall. The room is always tidy, and it feels like her own little world.
Diary entry from Keisha about today's school sports day, around 40 words: I ran the relay, we came second, I was tired but happy, and my friends cheered for us.

Dear Diary,
Today was our school sports day. I ran the relay, and we came second. My friends cheered for us from the side of the track. I was tired after the race, but I was very happy.
Keisha
Jot a diary entry for Faisal about today's long train journey: he watched fields go by, shared biscuits with a stranger, and fell asleep near the window as the evening came. 35 words.

Dear Diary,
Today I took a long train journey. I watched the fields go by and shared biscuits with a stranger. As the evening came, I fell asleep near the window, and the train carried me along.
Faisal
Write Mira's diary entry for today, 40 words: she baked her first cake in the afternoon, it sank in the middle, and she laughed and ate it anyway with her mother.

Dear Diary,
This afternoon I baked my first cake. It sank in the middle, but I laughed and ate it anyway with my mother. It was not perfect, but I enjoyed every bite, and I want to bake again.
Mira
My diary today, written as Arjun, 35 words: I fixed my bicycle chain myself, my hands got oily, I wiped them on a rag, and I felt capable, so I want to learn more repairs.

Dear Diary,
Today I fixed my bicycle chain myself. My hands got oily, so I wiped them on a rag. When the chain finally moved again, I felt capable. I want to learn more repairs.
Arjun
Diary page, 40 words, for today: I walked by the lake with Grandpa Lal, he told me an old story, and I want to remember it. Writer: Nisha.

Dear Diary,
Today I walked by the lake with Grandpa Lal. He told me an old story as we walked. I want to remember it, so I am writing about it here, and I will read it again some day.
Nisha
A tiny story with a moral, 35 words: a lion spares a mouse, later the mouse chews through a net and frees the lion.
A lion caught a mouse and let it go. Later, the lion was trapped in a net. The mouse chewed through the net and freed him. Even a small friend can help a big one.
Write a very short story in 35 words about a boy called Karan who is afraid of the dark, gets a small torch from his father, and walks to the kitchen alone at night.
Karan was afraid of the dark. One night, his father gave him a small torch. Karan switched it on and walked to the kitchen alone. The dark did not frighten him any more, and he smiled.
Tiny bedtime story, about 35 words: a firefly named Glim cannot light up, tries again, and finally shines for the sleepy forest, where the owls and the rabbits watch.
Glim the firefly could not light up. She tried again, and then once more. Finally, she shone for the sleepy forest, and it glowed in the dark. The owls and the rabbits watched her happily.
Short story in 35 words: a baker named Ines gives her last loaf to a hungry stranger and then finds a coin in the bread box.
Ines the baker had one loaf left at the end of the day. A hungry stranger came to her door, and she gave him the loaf. Then she looked in the bread box and found a coin.
Tiny story, 35 words: an old clock stops, a boy opens it, finds a tiny leaf inside, and the clock starts ticking again once he takes the leaf out.
The old clock stopped one morning. A boy opened it and looked inside. He found a tiny leaf stuck in the gears. When he took the leaf out, the clock started ticking again, and the boy smiled.
Write a paragraph of about 35 words on the value of saving paper: trees are cut for it, it can be used on both sides, and recycling helps.
Saving paper is important because trees are cut to make it. We can use both sides of a sheet before we throw it away. Recycling helps too, because old paper can be made into new paper.
Paragraph on why friends matter, 35 words: they listen, they share laughs, they help in trouble, and they make us feel we belong.
Friends matter because they listen to us when we talk. They share laughs with us and make ordinary days happy. They also help us when we are in trouble. With friends, we feel that we belong.
Paragraph for a school magazine, 40 words, about the library: quiet, many books, long tables, and a place to dream, where every student feels calm.
The school library is a quiet place with many books on its shelves. It has long tables where students sit and read. For many of us, it is also a place to dream, and everyone feels calm there.
A paragraph, about 35 words, about the festival of lamps: rows of diyas, sweets shared, rangoli at the door.

During the festival of lamps, rows of diyas light up the homes and the streets. Sweets are shared with family and neighbours. A rangoli decorates the door, and the whole house looks bright and welcoming.
Write 40 words on why a window seat on a train is special: moving scenery, fresh air, time to think.
A window seat on a train is special. You see the scenery move past you, and the fresh air touches your face. The wheels keep a steady rhythm, and it gives you time to sit quietly and think.
Write a four-line rhyming riddle about a spoon without using the word spoon, 30 words; it stirs tea and lifts rice and soup.

I dive in soup and stir the tea,
I have a bowl, though not a knee.
I lift your rice up to your face,
And then I wait back in my place.
Six lines for toddlers about a sleepy owl, about 40 words, with real rhymes.

The owl is sleepy, soft and round,
She makes no hoot and makes no sound.
She tucks her head and shuts her eyes,
And dreams beneath the starry skies.
The moon is up, the night is deep,
Little owl is fast asleep.
Cheerful four-line verse: a ringing cycle bell, spinning wheels, a bird, the sky. Keep the rhymes real, roughly 30 words.

My bicycle bell goes ring, ring, ring,
I pedal fast like a bird on wing.
The wheels go round, the road goes by,
And I feel as if I could fly.
Could you rhyme four lines about a snowman with a scarf and a hat who melts in the sun? 30 words.

The snowman wore a scarf and hat,
And stood so proudly, just like that.
The sun came out and he grew small,
Till he was not a snowman at all.
Rhyme four lines long to say goodnight to a child named Ravi, with stars and the night in it, and ending with morning, 40 words.

Goodnight, Ravi, the stars are bright,
They twinkle softly all through the night.
Close your eyes and dream away,
Till the stars give way to day.
Sleep tight, little Ravi, sleep tight,
The stars will keep you safe all night.
A short message to the plumber: please come to the second-floor bathroom, the pipe under the sink leaks, and the door is open for him in the morning. From Mrs Joshi. Around 40 words.

Dear Plumber,
Please come to the second-floor bathroom as early as you can. The pipe under the sink leaks, and the water is spreading. The door is open for you in the morning, so please go straight in. Thank you.
Mrs Joshi
Pass a note to my deskmate Rhea in class: I will share my eraser, she can borrow my ruler, and we should meet at the gate after the bell to walk home together. 35 words. Signed Sana.

Rhea,
I will share my eraser with you, and you can borrow my ruler for the test. Let's meet at the gate after the bell, and then we can walk home together. Don't forget!
Sana
Message for the dog-walker Mr Fonseca, 40 words: Bruno has eaten his breakfast, the leash hangs by the door, and the keys are under the mat. Ask him to lock up after the walk. From Lena.

Dear Mr Fonseca,
Bruno has eaten his breakfast, so he is ready for his walk. His leash is hanging by the door, and the keys are under the mat. Please lock up after the walk. Thank you very much.
Lena
A note of encouragement for my brother Kiran before his driving test: stay calm, check the mirrors, I believe in him, and I am proud of how he practised. About 40 words, from Asha.

Dear Kiran,
Good luck with your driving test! Stay calm, and remember to check your mirrors. I believe in you, and I am proud of how you practised for this. You will do well, and I will be thinking of you.
Asha

Write a voice-message script for Shreya telling her friend Teresa that the concert tickets are sold out but she found two seats at the lake festival instead, and ask whether Teresa wants them. 40 words.
Hi Teresa, it's Shreya. I have some news. The concert tickets are sold out, I am sorry to say. But I found two seats at the lake festival instead. Do you want them? Please call me back and tell me.
Write a harvest-festival invitation for farmers' families at the village school ground, with folk songs and a shared meal, on Sunday at noon, from the Panchayat. 35 words.

Dear farmers' families,
You are invited to the harvest festival at the village school ground on Sunday at noon. There will be folk songs, and we will share a meal together. Please come with your whole family.
The Panchayat
Compose a boat-ride picnic invitation to my colleagues: gather at the jetty at 9 am on Saturday, bring a packed lunch, life jackets provided. From Neha. Around 40 words.

Dear colleagues,
You are invited to a boat-ride picnic on Saturday. Please gather at the jetty at 9 am, and bring a packed lunch with you. Life jackets will be provided for everyone. I hope you can all come.
Neha
A baby shower invitation from the office team for Priya: cake, games, small gifts welcome, in the meeting room at 1 pm. 35 words.
The office team invites you to a baby shower for Priya! It will be held in the meeting room at 1 pm. There will be cake and games, and small gifts are welcome.
Invitation to a poetry open mic for the neighbourhood: each person gets three minutes, tea at the end, at Anand's cafe, 6 pm on Friday. About 40 words, from Anand.

Dear neighbours,
Come to a poetry open mic at my cafe at 6 pm on Friday. Each person gets three minutes to read a poem. There will be tea for everyone at the end. I look forward to hearing you all.
Anand
I'd like an invitation to my grandmother's eightieth birthday lunch: relatives only, vegetarian menu, a small garden near our house, 12:30 pm. 35 words. Signed the Nair family.

Dear relatives,
We invite you to my grandmother's eightieth birthday lunch. It will be held in a small garden near our house at 12:30 pm. The menu will be vegetarian.
The Nair family
A polite message asking the tailor to shorten my trousers by two inches and have them ready before the wedding next Saturday. 40 words, from Jatin.

Dear Tailor,
Could you please shorten my trousers by two inches? I need them ready before the wedding next Saturday. Please let me know when I can come to collect them. Thank you very much for your help.
Jatin
Draft a complaint to the airline about a damaged suitcase wheel on my flight yesterday, asking for a repair or compensation, 40 words, passenger name Rosa Martins.

Dear Airline Team,
I travelled on your flight yesterday, and the wheel of my suitcase was damaged during the journey. I request a repair or compensation. Please let me know how to go about it. Thank you for looking into this.
Rosa Martins
Request to the colony watchman to keep the gate light on at night because the lane is dark and children come home late from tuition. Around 40 words, from the residents of lane 3.

Dear Watchman,
The lane is very dark at night, and the children come home late from tuition. We request you to keep the gate light on every night. It will help everyone get home safely. Thank you for your help.
The residents of lane 3
Ask the principal for permission to start a reading club in the free period, with a teacher as guide. 30 words. From Fatima of class 8.

Dear Principal,
I would like to request permission to start a reading club in the free period. A teacher would guide us. Thank you for your time.
Fatima, class 8
Polite complaint to a courier company: my parcel arrived two weeks late and the box was dented, and I want an explanation and an apology. 40 words, signed Lars.

Dear Courier Company,
My parcel arrived two weeks late, and the box was dented. I would like an explanation, and I would also like an apology for the delay and the damage. Please reply to me soon. Thank you.
Lars
Email to my team announcing that the Friday meeting is shifted to 3 pm in room B and agenda points are due by Thursday. Subject line, about 40 words. From Kavita.

Subject: Meeting shifted to 3 pm

Hi team,
Please note that the Friday meeting is shifted to 3 pm in room B. Please send your agenda points by Thursday, so that I can put them all together before we meet. Thank you for your cooperation.
Kavita
Write an email to a customer, Mr Alvarez, saying his order has shipped and the tracking number is attached, and thanking him for shopping with us. Subject, 40 words, from the Support Desk.

Subject: Your order has shipped

Dear Mr Alvarez,
Good news. Your order has shipped, and it is now on its way to you. The tracking number is attached to this email, so you can follow your parcel. Thank you for shopping with us.
The Support Desk

I want to email my professor Dr Menon to thank her for writing my recommendation letter and to say I will tell her the result. say her advice helped me, and add a subject line. Subject line please, 40 words. From Yash.

Subject: Thank you for the recommendation letter

Dear Dr Menon,
Thank you for writing my recommendation letter. Your advice helped me a great deal, and I am very grateful for your support. I will tell you the result as soon as I hear it.
Yash
Group email about a lost brown wallet near the park on Sunday morning, asking anyone who finds it to contact Dhruv. Subject, around 40 words, signed Dhruv.

Subject: Lost brown wallet near the park

Dear all,
I lost a brown wallet near the park on Sunday morning. If anyone finds it, please contact me. I would be very grateful for any help, and thank you for looking out for it.
Dhruv
Email from Sofia to her landlord: the rent will be paid by bank transfer on the first of the month, and she asks for a receipt. 35 words with a subject.

Subject: Rent payment

Dear Landlord,
I will pay the rent by bank transfer on the first of the month. Could you please give me a receipt once you have received it? Thank you for your help.
Sofia
Compose a notice for the colony: the street lights will be repaired by the municipal team on Wednesday, and residents should not park near the poles. 35 words.

NOTICE
The municipal team will repair the street lights in our colony on Wednesday. Residents are requested not to park near the poles, so that the team can work safely. Thank you for your cooperation.
Notice about a blood donation camp at the community hall, 9 am to 1 pm on Sunday, organised by the youth club, everyone welcome. 40 words.

NOTICE
The youth club is organising a blood donation camp at the community hall on Sunday from 9 am to 1 pm. Everyone is welcome to come. We request you to join us and to tell your friends and family.
A notice for a yoga class in the park, about 40 words: new batch, beginners welcome, bring a mat, first session free, early morning.

NOTICE
A new yoga batch is starting in the park in the early morning. Beginners are welcome. Please bring a mat. The first session is free, so come and try it with us. We look forward to meeting you.
School notice: sports day rehearsals are moved to the ground, students should wear sports shoes, parents need not attend, and the rehearsal ends at noon. 35 words.

NOTICE
Sports day rehearsals are moved to the ground. All students should wear sports shoes. Parents need not attend. The rehearsal will end at noon. Please make sure that students come on time and follow the instructions.

A shop notice: closed for stocktaking on the 20th, will reopen on the 21st, sorry for the inconvenience, and thank customers for their understanding. Ask them to plan their visits around it. Around 40 words.

NOTICE
This shop will be closed on the 20th for stocktaking. It will reopen on the 21st. We are sorry for the inconvenience, and we thank all our customers for their kind understanding. Please plan your visits accordingly.
Describe a village well at noon in 35 words: stone rim, a rope and bucket, women filling pots, the cool shade of a banyan tree.
At noon, the village well has a stone rim, and a rope and bucket hang over it. Women come to fill their pots. Nearby, the banyan tree gives cool shade from the heat. The place is quiet.
The first snowfall in a mountain town, described in about 35 words: soft flakes, quiet streets, children with open mouths trying to catch snow, and smoke rising from the chimneys

The first snow falls on the mountain town in soft flakes. The streets are quiet, and the whole town seems to listen. Smoke rises from the chimneys. Children stand with open mouths, trying to catch the snow.
Describe my mother's kitchen, 35 words: steel containers, a pressure cooker singing, the smell of cumin, a calendar on the wall.
My mother's kitchen has rows of steel containers on the shelf. The pressure cooker sings, and the smell of cumin fills the room. A calendar hangs on the wall. It is a warm and busy place.
What does a train compartment at night look like? Describe it in 35 words: dim lights, snoring passengers, the rhythm of wheels, and a chai seller's call.
At night, the train compartment is lit by dim lights. Passengers are snoring on their berths, and the wheels keep a steady rhythm. Now and then, a chai seller calls out as the train rolls on.
Describe a school playground during the break, 35 words: swings creaking, children running, a teacher's whistle, a vendor selling ice candy.

The playground is busy during the break. The swings creak, and children run in every direction. A teacher blows a whistle, and a vendor at the gate sells ice candy to the children, who gather around him.
Write a diary entry for today for Sunita, 40 words: the first day of her new job, she was nervous, her colleague Meera showed her the pantry, and she felt welcomed.

Dear Diary,
Today was my first day at my new job. I was nervous in the morning. My colleague Meera showed me the pantry and was very kind, and by the end of the day I felt welcomed.
Sunita
Bilal's diary for today, around 35 words: it poured heavily, he stayed home, read a comic, listened to the rain on the window, and drank hot tea.

Dear Diary,
Today it poured heavily, so I stayed home. I read a comic and listened to the rain on the window. I also drank hot tea. It was a quiet and happy day.
Bilal
Diary note for today by Hana, about 40 words: she visited the zoo with her class, the elephants were her favourite, and she bought a toy giraffe at the gift shop.

Dear Diary,
Today I visited the zoo with my class. The elephants were my favourite animals, and I watched them for a long time. At the gift shop, I bought a toy giraffe. I had a lovely day.
Hana
Write today's diary note for Ethan: he got a haircut he did not like, his sister laughed, and then he laughed too, so the haircut did not matter. 40 words.

Dear Diary,
Today I got a haircut that I did not like at all. My sister laughed at me, and then I laughed too. After that, the haircut did not matter any more, and I felt much better.
Ethan
A diary page for today by Pallavi, 35 words: she sang in front of an audience for the first time, her voice shook, everyone clapped, and she wants to sing again.

Dear Diary,
Today I sang in front of an audience for the first time. My voice shook at the start, but everyone clapped when I finished. I was so happy, and I want to sing again.
Pallavi
Tiny story about a tortoise and a hare racing, in 40 words, where the hare naps and the tortoise wins.
A hare and a tortoise had a race. The hare ran far ahead and thought he had plenty of time, so he took a nap. The tortoise kept walking slowly and passed him. In the end, the tortoise won the race.
Story in 40 words: a girl named Sia sells lemonade on a hot street on a sunny afternoon, a thirsty boy drinks a glass, a boy pays with a button, and she keeps the button in her pocket.
On a sunny afternoon, Sia sold lemonade on a hot street. A thirsty boy came by and drank a glass. He paid her with a button. Sia smiled at him and kept the button safe in her pocket.
A very short spooky tale in 35 words: an old house creaks at night, a boy hears tapping, he sits up and looks, and it is only a branch at the window.
The old house creaked at night. A boy heard a tapping sound and sat up in bed. His heart beat fast. He looked at the window, and it was only a branch tapping on the glass.
A tiny tale about two umbrellas, one red and one yellow, who argue over who keeps people drier, until the rain stops and both are folded. 35 words.

A red umbrella and a yellow umbrella argued about who kept people drier. They went on arguing as the rain fell. Then the rain stopped, and both umbrellas were folded and put away together, side by side.
A tiny story: Rina finds a paper boat on the pond, sends it back with a note saying hello, and a different boat returns. 35 words.
Rina found a paper boat on the pond. She wrote the word hello on a small note and sent the boat back across the water. After a while, a different boat returned to her, and she smiled.
A paragraph, 40 words, on why reading before sleep is relaxing: a quiet mind, soft light, a story to dream about. Say I read a few pages every night.

Reading before sleep is relaxing. It gives you a quiet mind, because you stop thinking about the day. With soft light and a story to dream about, sleep comes easily. That is why I read a few pages every night.
Write a paragraph on the importance of teamwork, 35 words: tasks get done faster, ideas are shared, people support one another, and the work feels lighter. Say the team feels strong.

Teamwork is important because tasks get done faster when many people help. Ideas are shared, and people support one another. When we work together as a team, the work feels lighter, and the team feels strong.
Paragraph about the monsoon in my city, about 35 words: cool air, green trees, muddy roads, and hot pakoras.
The monsoon brings cool air to my city after the summer heat. The trees turn green, but the roads become muddy. Still, it is a good time to sit at home and eat hot pakoras.
Write a paragraph about the bicycle as a way to travel, 35 words: it is cheap, uses no fuel, gives good exercise, and is easy to park.
The bicycle is a good way to travel. It is cheap, and it uses no fuel. Riding it gives good exercise. It is also easy to park, so you can stop almost anywhere you like.
A paragraph, 35 words, on why we should help a neighbour: it builds trust, makes the street friendly, and one day you may need help yourself.

We should help a neighbour because it builds trust between people. It makes the street friendly, and everyone feels safe. One day, you may need help yourself, and your neighbour will be ready to help you.
A four-line rhyme about a postman on a bicycle delivering letters, about 45 words.

The postman rides his bicycle through the town each day,
With a bag of letters on his back, he whistles on his way.
He rings his bell at every door, and waits a little while,
Then hands the letters over with a warm and cheerful smile.
Limerick, five lines, with a real rhyme scheme, about a clumsy cook who trips and spills a pot of soup, about 35 words.

A clumsy cook carried a big pot
Of soup that was bubbling and piping hot.
She tripped on the lace of her shoe,
And the soup, in a stew,
Went flying all over the whole lot.
A seven-line rhyme about two friends sharing one mango, about 45 words.

Two friends had a mango to share,
They sliced it with patience and care.
One half for you,
One half for me too,
And sweet juice ran down everywhere.
They smiled and they laughed and they ate,
Then said that the mango was great.
Four lines of rhyme: a little boat rocking on a stormy sea through the night, 30 words.

The little boat rocked on the sea,
As waves came rolling wild and free.
It bobbed and tilted, held on tight,
And sailed on bravely through the night.
Welcome verse of six lines for baby Zoya, with real rhymes, 35 words.

Welcome, Zoya, little one,
Your life has only just begun.
Our hearts are full, our smiles are wide,
We welcome you with joy and pride.
Sleep sweetly now, our little star,
We love you just the way you are.
Quick text for my roommate Dan: I am at the laundry, the washing will take an hour, and he can have my share of dinner if he is hungry. Also say I will be back by eight. About 40 words.

Hi Dan,
I am at the laundry, and the washing will take an hour. I will be back by eight. If you are hungry before then, you can have my share of dinner. Please do not wait for me.
A bookmark note from Grandpa to Maya, about 35 words: the story inside is his favourite, he read it many times as a boy, she should read it slowly, and he hopes she likes it. Sign it Grandpa.

Dear Maya,
This story is my favourite. I read it many times when I was a boy. Please read it slowly, and enjoy every page. I hope you like it as much as I do.
Grandpa
Write a sorry note to my classmate Imran: I borrowed his pen and lost it, I feel bad about it, and I will buy him a new one on Monday. 40 words. From Jaya.

Dear Imran,
I am sorry. I borrowed your pen and lost it, and I feel bad about it. I will buy you a new one on Monday. Please forgive me for the trouble, and thank you for being so kind.
Jaya

Reminder note for myself on the door, 35 words: take the keys, the wallet, and the library book, and switch off the fan. Also: lock the door, and do not forget to say bye to Mum and to turn off the light. Also take the umbrella.
Before you go, remember to take your keys, your wallet, the library book and the umbrella. Switch off the fan and turn off the light. Lock the door. Do not forget to say bye to Mum.
A kind note for a teammate who made a mistake in the report: it happens, the fix is easy, and we will check it together after lunch. From Omar, 35 words.

Hi,
Please don't worry about the mistake in the report. It happens to everyone, and the fix is easy. We will check it together after lunch. Thank you for all your hard work on it.
Omar
Invite parents to the annual art exhibition in the school corridor: paintings by children of class 4, tea and biscuits, 10 am. It is from the art teacher. 35 words.

Dear parents,
You are invited to the annual art exhibition in the school corridor at 10 am. You will see paintings by the children of class 4. Tea and biscuits will be served.
The art teacher
A tea-party invitation for my sister's friends, in the garden gazebo at 4 pm on Sunday, with sandwiches and lemon tea, from Rekha. About 40 words.

Dear friends,
You are invited to a tea party in the garden gazebo at 4 pm on Sunday. There will be sandwiches and lemon tea for everyone. We hope you can come and spend a happy afternoon with us.
Rekha
Invite the cricket team to a post-match dinner at Lala's dhaba on Saturday where everyone pays for themselves, from captain Zubin. 35 words. Also say we will meet at 8 pm.

Dear team,
Well played, everyone! Let's have a post-match dinner at Lala's dhaba on Saturday. Everyone will pay for themselves. We will meet at 8 pm. Please come and enjoy the evening together.
Zubin, captain
Invitation to a cooking demonstration of idlis at the community kitchen, 11 am on Sunday, please bring an apron, from Chef Mohan. About 35 words.

You are invited to a cooking demonstration of idlis at the community kitchen at 11 am on Sunday. Please bring an apron, so that you can cook along with us. We hope to see you there.
Chef Mohan
Short wedding invitation for relatives: Sunil and Rani are getting married at the lakeside hall on Sunday, the ceremony is at 10 am, and lunch follows. 35 words.

Dear relatives,
Sunil and Rani are getting married at the lakeside hall on Sunday. The ceremony will begin at 10 am, and lunch will follow. We would be very happy if you could attend and bless them.
Politely request the neighbour to move their bike that blocks our gate, and mention that we need to take the car out this evening. Compose it in 35 words, signed Hema.

Dear neighbour,
Your bike is blocking our gate. We need to take the car out this evening. Could you please move it as soon as you can? Thank you very much for your help and understanding.
Hema
Complain to the municipal office that garbage has not been collected from our street for a week, and ask for a cleaning and a regular pickup. 40 words. Signed Residents of Park Lane.

Dear Municipal Office,
Garbage has not been collected from our street for a week. We request you to arrange a cleaning as soon as possible, and to see that it is picked up regularly in future. Thank you for your help.
Residents of Park Lane
Ask the receptionist at the clinic to move my appointment to a later time today because I am delayed in traffic. Polite, 40 words, patient Rohit Sen.

Dear Receptionist,
I am delayed in traffic, so I cannot reach the clinic at my appointment time. Could you please move my appointment to a later time today? I am sorry for the trouble. Thank you for your understanding.
Rohit Sen
A student asks the class teacher Mrs Iyer for an extra copy of the worksheet because the first one got wet in the rain. 35 words. From Danish. Say I will keep the new copy dry.

Dear Mrs Iyer,
My worksheet got wet in the rain. Could I please have an extra copy? I will keep the new copy dry and bring it back on time. Thank you for your kindness.
Danish
Complaint to a restaurant about a hair in the soup, calm tone, asking for a fresh bowl and saying that I would like to finish my meal. About 35 words, from Mr Pillai.

Dear Restaurant Team,
I found a hair in my soup. I am writing calmly, but I would like a fresh bowl, please. I would like to finish my meal here. Thank you for your attention.
Mr Pillai
Write an email inviting colleagues to a farewell lunch for Mr Rao on his last working day in the cafeteria at 1 pm. Subject, 35 words, from the HR team.

Subject: Farewell lunch for Mr Rao

Dear colleagues,
Please join us for a farewell lunch for Mr Rao on his last working day. It will be held in the cafeteria at 1 pm.
The HR team
Email to the vendor asking for a quotation for 50 chairs and 10 tables, with delivery to our office, and ask for a reply by Friday. Subject line, around 35 words. From Anita George.

Subject: Quotation for chairs and tables

Dear Vendor,
Please send us a quotation for 50 chairs and 10 tables, with delivery to our office. We would be grateful for your reply by Friday. Thank you for your help.
Anita George
An email to my cousin Jasmine congratulating her on her new baby and wishing the family joy, and saying I want to visit soon. Subject line, 40 words. From Vivek.

Subject: Congratulations on your new baby

Dear Jasmine,
Congratulations on your new baby! I am so happy for you and for the whole family. I wish you all lots of joy and many happy days. I would love to visit you soon.
Vivek

Write a polite email declining an invitation to a conference because of a clash with another work trip, and thank them for inviting me. Subject, 30 words, from Dr Nanda. Address it to the conference organisers.

Subject: Regarding your invitation

Dear Organisers,
Thank you for inviting me to the conference. I am sorry that I must decline, because it clashes with another work trip.
Dr Nanda

Email to a tutor saying my son is in class 9 and asking whether she can teach him algebra on weekends, what her fee is, and which weekend day suits her. Say thank you. Subject line, 50 words, from Mr Khan.

Subject: Algebra lessons for my son

Dear Tutor,
My son is in class 9, and I would like him to learn algebra. Could you teach him on weekends? Please also tell me what your fee is, and which weekend day suits you. I look forward to your reply. Thank you for your time.
Mr Khan
A notice about a book fair: in the school hall for three days, discounts on all titles, and students may bring friends. 35 words. Add that everyone is welcome.

NOTICE
A book fair will be held in the school hall for three days. All titles will have discounts. Students may bring their friends, and everyone is welcome. Come and find a book you will love.
A notice about cycle parking, 35 words: bikes must be parked in the shed, not in the corridor, they must be locked, and the gate must not be blocked.

NOTICE
All bikes must be parked in the shed, not in the corridor. They must also be locked. Please do not block the gate. Thank you for following these rules and keeping the way clear for everyone.
A notice for a garden club meeting: the first meeting, bring seeds to swap, in the community garden at 5 pm on Saturday. About 35 words.

NOTICE
The garden club will hold its first meeting in the community garden at 5 pm on Saturday. Please bring seeds to swap with other members. Everyone who loves plants is welcome to join us.
A water-saving notice for the hostel, 40 words: close taps tightly, report leaks to the warden, turn off the tap while brushing teeth, and take short showers. Thank the students at the end.

NOTICE
Please save water in the hostel. Close the taps tightly after use, turn off the tap while brushing your teeth, and take short showers. Report any leaks to the warden at once. Thank you, students, for helping us.
Notice for the temple fair, 35 words: stalls open from 4 pm, no plastic bags, free drinking water at the entrance, and everyone is welcome.

NOTICE
The stalls at the temple fair will open from 4 pm. Plastic bags are not allowed. Free drinking water is available at the entrance. Everyone is welcome, so please come and enjoy the fair.
Describe a busy market in 30 words: piles of vegetables, calling sellers, the smell of fresh coriander, bargaining voices.
The market is busy. There are piles of vegetables, and sellers call out to the crowd. The smell of fresh coriander is in the air, and voices bargain on every side.
Describe a grandmother's hands in 35 words: wrinkled, warm, smelling of coconut oil, quick at stitching. Also gentle when patting a head.
A grandmother's hands are wrinkled and warm. They smell of coconut oil. They are quick at stitching, and the needle moves faster than your eyes can follow. They are gentle when patting a head, too.
Describe a rainy window in 35 words: drops sliding down, fogged glass, blurred lights outside. Also a cup of tea on the sill.
On the rainy window, drops slide slowly down the glass. The glass is fogged, and the lights outside look blurred. A cup of tea sits on the sill, and its steam rises beside the window.
Describe a campfire at the beach in 40 words: crackling wood, sparks rising, faces glowing, waves in the dark.
At the beach, the campfire burns with crackling wood. Sparks rise high into the night air, and the faces around it glow in the light. Beyond the fire, the waves move in the dark, and we hear them.
Describe a sleepy village road, 35 words: dust, a cow resting, an old bicycle leaning on a wall.
The village road is sleepy and still. There is soft dust on the ground, and a cow is resting in the middle of it. An old bicycle leans on a wall, and nobody is in a hurry.
Rohini's diary for today, about 35 words: she planted a mango sapling with her father, dug the hole herself, and promised to water it every day, and hopes it will give mangoes one day.

Dear Diary,
Today I planted a mango sapling with my father. I dug the hole myself. I promised to water the sapling every day. I want to see it grow tall and give us mangoes one day.
Rohini
Write Yusuf's diary for today: he cooked egg curry alone, it was too salty, his family still ate it, and he learned to taste before adding salt. 40 words.

Dear Diary,
Today I cooked egg curry alone for the first time. It was too salty, but my family still ate it. Now I have learned that I must taste before adding salt, and I will remember it.
Yusuf
Diary entry, 40 words, for today by Greta: she met a stray puppy, named it Biscuit, and fed it half her sandwich. She felt happy.

Dear Diary,
Today I met a stray puppy on my way home. I named it Biscuit and fed it half my sandwich. It wagged its tail, and I felt very happy. I hope I will see it again.
Greta
A diary entry for today by Manoj, 35 words: he missed the bus, walked to the station, caught the next one, and was proud that he kept calm.

Dear Diary,
Today I missed the bus. I did not panic, but walked to the station and caught the next one. I was proud that I kept calm when things went wrong, and I reached on time.
Manoj
Diary note for today from Alma: she finished a thousand-piece puzzle with her brother, and the last piece was under the sofa. 35 words. She cheered because she was so happy.

Dear Diary,
Today my brother and I finished a thousand-piece puzzle together. The last piece was under the sofa, and we found it at last. I cheered because I was so happy, and so did he.
Alma
Tiny story, about 35 words: a girl named Tia plants a seed, waits and waits, and a small green shoot comes out. She smiles at it.
Tia planted a seed in the soil. She waited and waited. Each day she looked at the soil, but nothing happened. At last, a small green shoot came out. Tia smiled at it, and she felt proud.
A small tale in 35 words about a shy robot named Bolt who wants to join a dance and finally taps his foot. The other robots cheer.
Bolt the robot was shy. He wanted to join the dance, but he stood by the wall and watched. Finally, he tapped his foot. The other robots saw it and cheered, and Bolt felt happy.
A tiny story about a boy named Leo who loses a blue balloon, watches it rise into the clouds, and waves goodbye as it grows smaller until it is a dot. 35 words.
Leo lost his blue balloon. He watched it rise into the clouds. Then he waved goodbye to it. The balloon grew smaller and smaller until it was only a tiny dot in the sky above him.
A moral story in 35 words: two goats meet on a narrow bridge, neither will move, then one lies down and the other steps over. End with the lesson.

Two goats met on a narrow bridge. Neither would move. Then one goat lay down, and the other stepped over him. Both reached the other side safely. Kindness solved the problem, and they went their ways.
Tiny story: a fisherman named Ravi catches a golden fish, the fish asks to be set free, and he lets it go. 35 words. The fish swims away happily, and he goes home.
Ravi the fisherman caught a golden fish in his net. The fish asked him to set it free. Ravi felt kind, and he let it go. The fish swam away happily, and Ravi went home.
Compose a paragraph of 40 words on why we should keep our surroundings clean: it prevents bad smells, makes places nice to see, and shows respect to others.
We should keep our surroundings clean. A clean place has no bad smells, and it is nice to see. It also shows respect to other people who use the same place, so we should all do our part.
A paragraph for a school essay, 35 words, on the benefits of sports: teamwork, fitness, and joy. Say it is for children, and add friendship, discipline and keeping active.

Sports have many benefits for children. They teach teamwork, discipline and friendship, and they help children build fitness and stay active. Above all, sports bring joy, and playing together with friends is fun for everyone.
Paragraph about a favourite street food, 35 words: crisp pani puri, tangy water, shared with friends on the roadside.
Pani puri is my favourite street food. The puris are crisp, and the water is tangy. It tastes best when it is shared with friends on the roadside, where everyone laughs together over a plate.
A paragraph, about 35 words, on kindness: small acts like a smile or holding a door can brighten someone's day.
Kindness does not need to be big. Small acts, like a smile or holding a door, can brighten someone's day. A little kindness costs nothing, yet it can stay with a person for a long time.
Write a paragraph about stars in the sky, 35 words: they are far-away suns, they twinkle, and sailors used them to find their way. Say they are easy to see on clear nights.
Stars are far-away suns. They twinkle in the sky at night. Long ago, sailors used them to find their way across the sea. Stars are easy to see on clear nights, so look up and enjoy them.
A rhyme about a frog and the rain, six lines, about 50 words.

The frog sat still while the rain came down,
He croaked a happy song for all the town.
He hopped and splashed from pond to log,
A cheerful, soggy, singing frog.
The rain stopped soon, the sun came through,
And the frog sang on, as frogs will do.
Four-line rhyme about a bus rolling through town, up a hill and back down, with wheels going round, 30 words.

The bus rolls on through the busy town,
It climbs the hill and rolls back down.
Its wheels go round and round all day,
And carry us along the way.
Short rhyme for kids about washing hands with soap, rubbing between the fingers, rinsing and drying, six lines, 40 words.

Wash your hands with soap so clean,
Rub them front and in between.
Rinse them well and shake them dry,
Clean hands wave a friendly hi.
Wash them well before you eat,
Then you're ready for a treat.
A rhyme, six lines, about a red balloon slipping from a hand and floating away, 45 words.

The balloon slipped out of my hand,
And floated high above the land.
It rose up, red against the sky,
And waved to me as it went by.
It grew so small I could not see,
And that was how it said goodbye to me.
A rhyme about sunrise over a village, six lines: roosters crow, doors swing open, 45 words.

The sun peeks over the hill so high,
And paints with gold the village sky.
The roosters crow, the doors swing wide,
And all the village steps outside.
A new day starts, so bright and new,
With so much work and play to do.
